name: Abiding Hex
stats: Supported Skills consume a Power Charge on use
Supported Skills have 80% more duration when consuming a Power Charge
description: Supports Curse Skills you cast yourself. Supported Skills will consume Power Charges on use, gaining significant Curse duration if they do.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for curses you cast yourself. The curse eats one of your power charges when you cast it, and in exchange it lasts far longer.
beginner.whyItMatters: Recasting a curse in the middle of a fight costs you the time you should be spending on damage, so a curse that stays on the target changes how a whole fight feels.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Attach it once you have a reliable way to build power charges. Without charges to spend it gives you nothing, so it is a mid-build support rather than an early one.

name: Accelerated Growth I
stats: Triggers Accelerated Growth on Overgrowing Plants created by Supported Skills
description: Supports Plant Skills, causing them to Trigger an explosion after they have been Overgrown.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for plant skills. Once a plant the skill made has finished overgrowing, it detonates instead of just sitting there.
beginner.whyItMatters: Plants that only grow are a slow setup with no payoff attached; adding the detonation turns that waiting period into a second wave of damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it as soon as a plant skill becomes your main way of clearing packs, because the explosion is what makes the setup time worth paying.

name: Accelerated Growth II
stats: Triggers Accelerated Growth on Overgrowing Plants created by Supported Skills
description: Supports Plant Skills, causing them to Trigger an explosion after they have been Overgrown, Blinding enemies Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version of the plant detonation support: the explosion also blinds every enemy it hits.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blinded enemies miss you far more often, so the same explosion now does defensive work as well as damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap up to this one once you have the gem tier for it and you are taking hits from the packs your plants are meant to be killing.

name: Acrimony
stats: Enemies affected by non-Ailment Damage over time from Supported Skills have 50% reduced Life regeneration rate
description: Supports Skills which can Damage Enemies. Enemies affected by Damage over time from Supported Skills which was not caused by a Damaging Ailment have reduced Life regeneration rate. Only the strongest instance of this Debuff will apply. Does not Support Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that cuts the life regeneration of anything suffering damage over time from the supported skill, as long as that damage is not from an ailment like ignite or poison.
beginner.whyItMatters: Tough enemies heal through slow damage; halving that healing is what stops a long fight from becoming an unwinnable stalemate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on a skill whose damage is a lingering effect rather than a burst, and mainly against bosses and rare monsters that regenerate.

name: Adhesive Grenades I
stats: Supported Grenade Skills stop where they initially land
Supported Grenade Skills deal 10% less Damage
description: Supports Grenade Skills. Grenades from Supported Skills do not bounce, instead halting movement where they intially land, but doing lower damage when they detonate.

beginner.whatItIs: A grenade support that stops your grenades from bouncing. They stick where they land, but hit for a little less.
beginner.whyItMatters: A bouncing grenade lands somewhere you did not choose, so trading a slice of damage for knowing exactly where the blast happens is usually the better deal.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Attach it the first time a grenade rolls past a pack and explodes on empty ground. Skip it if you are throwing into a corridor where bounces already land well.

name: Adhesive Grenades II
stats: Supported Grenade Skills stop where they initially land
description: Supports Grenade Skills. Grenades from Supported Skills do not bounce, instead halting movement where they intially land.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded sticky-grenade support. Grenades still stop where they land, but you no longer pay any damage for it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the one reason to think twice about the earlier version, so grenade placement becomes reliable for free.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the first version with this one the moment you can, and keep it in every grenade setup after that.

name: Admixture
stats: 20% more Magnitude of Bleeding inflicted by Supported Skills against Poisoned Enemies
20% more Magnitude of Poison inflicted by Supported Skills against Bleeding Enemies
description: Supports Skills which can cause Damaging Hits. Bleeding inflicted by those Hits is more effective against Poisoned Enemies, and Poison inflicted by Supported Skills is more effective against Bleeding Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes bleeding land harder on poisoned targets and poison land harder on bleeding targets.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two damage-over-time effects that normally just stack side by side start feeding each other, so a build that applies both gets more out of each.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only worth a slot when your character genuinely applies both bleed and poison. On a build that only does one, it does nothing at all.

name: Advancing Storm
stats: Supported Skills originate from the player and move towards the target location
description: Supports Storm skills, causing them to appear at the user's location and move towards the target location.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for storm skills that changes where they begin. Instead of appearing on your target, the storm starts on you and travels outward toward where you aimed.
beginner.whyItMatters: A storm that walks across the ground sweeps everything between you and your target instead of only hitting the spot you clicked.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good when enemies come at you in a line or a corridor. Poor when you want damage on one distant target and nothing in between.

name: Aftershock I
stats: Supported skills have 25% chance to cause an additional Aftershock
description: Supports Slams you use yourself, giving them a chance to create an Aftershock.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for slams you use yourself, giving each slam a one-in-four chance to strike a second time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slams are slow and committed, so any chance of a free repeat is a large share of the damage you get out of that commitment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Put it on your main slam early. It costs the slam nothing, so there is no downside to carrying it while you level.

name: Aftershock II
stats: Supported skills have 35% chance to cause an additional Aftershock
description: Supports Slams you use yourself, giving them a chance to create an Aftershock.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved slam repeat support, raising the chance of an extra aftershock to just over one slam in three.
beginner.whyItMatters: The higher chance means the repeat shows up often enough to plan around rather than being a pleasant surprise.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it over the earlier version as soon as your gem tier allows, on any build where a slam is the attack you actually spend your time using.

name: Ahn's Citadel
stats: Walls from Supported Skills are created along a Fissure instead
description: Supports skills that create walls in a line, causing them to instead be created along a fissure.
flavourText:
As possessed golems ravaged the land, Aul - crowned Ahn
by blood and tyranny - began the last ritual, causing azurite
crystals to rupture and grow throughout his doomed citadel.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for skills that create a wall. The wall stops being a straight line and instead forms along a fissure cracked into the ground.
beginner.whyItMatters: It changes the shape of your wall entirely, which matters for builds that care about where a wall sits rather than that one exists.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Reach for it when your wall skill is meant to work with fissure effects, not when you simply want something to block a doorway.

name: Ailith's Chimes
stats: 25% Surpassing chance to gain a Power Charge when expending Combo with Supported Skills per Combo expended
description: Supports Skills which can expend Combo. On expending Combo with Supported Skills, you have a chance to gain Power Charges based on the amount of Combo expended.
flavourText:
Ailith awoke to find her fire iridescent, and her mind alive
with visions. By morning, she began teaching what she'd
seen... thus was born the Keepers of the Pale Vision.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for skills that spend combo. Each point of combo you spend gives a separate chance to gain a power charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: Power charges are one of the steadier ways to raise critical hit chance, and this turns an attack rhythm you already have into a way of generating them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For builds that build and spend combo constantly and want charges without dedicating another skill to making them.

name: Alignment I
stats: Supported Skills indicate one of four directions
Indicated direction changes when an Attack with Supported Skill matches indicated direction
Supported Skills deal 30% more Projectile Damage when Attacking in indicated direction
description: Supports Bow Attacks. Supported Skills indicate one of four directions, changing indicated direction when an Attack with Supported Skill matches that direction. Attacks from Supported Skills which match the indicated direction deal much more Damage. Cannot Support Channelled Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A bow support that shows one of four directions. Attack in that direction and the shot deals 30% more projectile damage, then the indicated direction changes.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards moving around a fight and firing from the right side rather than standing still, which is how bow characters stay alive anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when you are comfortable repositioning mid-fight. If you tend to plant your feet, most of the bonus goes unclaimed.

name: Alignment II
stats: Supported Skills indicate one of four directions
Indicated direction changes when an Attack with Supported Skill matches indicated direction
Supported Skills deal 40% more Projectile Damage when Attacking in indicated direction
description: Supports Bow Attacks. Supported Skills indicate one of four directions, changing indicated direction when an Attack with Supported Skill matches that direction. Attacks from Supported Skills which match the indicated direction deal much more Damage. Cannot Support Channelled Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: The middle version of the directional bow support, raising the reward for a matching shot to 40% more projectile damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The bigger number changes it from a small nudge into a real reason to move to the indicated side before you fire.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in over the first version once available, particularly on single-target fights where you have room to circle a boss.

name: Alignment III
stats: Supported Skills indicate one of four directions
Indicated direction changes when an Attack with Supported Skill matches indicated direction
Supported Skills fire 4 additional Projectiles when Attacking in indicated direction
description: Supports Bow Attacks. Supported Skills indicate one of four directions, changing indicated direction when an Attack with Supported Skill matches that direction. Attacks from Supported Skills which match the indicated direction fire additional Projectiles. Cannot Support Channelled Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: The final directional bow support. Instead of extra damage, a shot fired in the indicated direction fires four additional arrows.
beginner.whyItMatters: Extra arrows spread damage across a whole pack rather than concentrating it, so this version is about clearing rather than killing one target.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick this over the damage versions when your bow skill is your pack-clearing tool. Keep an earlier version for boss fights.

name: Amanamu's Tithe
stats: 50% chance to gain an Abyssal Monster Modifier for 20 seconds when a Minion from Supported Skills dies
Maximum 3 Abyssal Monster Modifiers gained this way
description: Supports Persistent Minion Skills, granting a chance when Supported Minions die for you to gain an Abyssal Monster Modifier.
flavourText:
Those that serve the Liege of the Lightless are his, utterly.
Blood, flesh, and soul are fodder to bend to his will.
Under a Lich Lord, not even death is an escape.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for persistent minion skills. When one of the supported minions dies, you have an even chance of gaining an abyssal monster modifier for twenty seconds, up to three at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: It flips a dead minion from a pure loss into a temporary buff on you, which changes how you feel about sending them into danger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For minion builds whose minions are expendable and quickly replaced, not for ones built around keeping a few strong companions alive.

name: Ambrosia I
stats: Supported Skills consume 14% of your maximum Mana Flask charges on use
Supported Skills Gain 2% of Damage as extra Lightning Damage per Mana Flask charge consumed
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which damage enemies with Hits. Supported Skills consume a percentage of your maximum Mana Flask charges, Gaining a percentage of damage as extra Lightning damage per Mana Flask charge consumed.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that spends a chunk of your mana flask charges every time you use the skill, and adds lightning damage on top of the hit for each charge spent.
beginner.whyItMatters: Flask charges are usually a resource you sit on until you need mana; this turns the surplus into damage you were not otherwise getting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Works when you kill things fast enough to keep flask charges refilling. On a slow build you will run the flask dry and get nothing.

name: Ambrosia II
stats: Supported Skills consume 35% of your maximum Mana Flask charges on use
Supported Skills Gain 1% of Damage as extra Lightning Damage per Mana Flask charge consumed
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which damage enemies with Hits. Supported Skills consume a percentage of your maximum Mana Flask charges, Gaining a percentage of damage as extra Lightning damage per Mana Flask charge consumed.

beginner.whatItIs: The heavier version of the mana-flask trade. It eats far more of your flask charges per use, in exchange for a smaller added-lightning bonus per charge spent.
beginner.whyItMatters: Because it burns charges much faster, it turns your flask into an outright damage resource rather than a small top-up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on slower, harder-hitting skills used a few times per fight, and on builds that refill flask charges quickly.

name: Ambush
stats: Supported Skill has 100% more Critical Hit Chance against Enemies that are on Full Life
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making it more likely to Critically Hit enemies on full life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that doubles your critical hit chance against any enemy still on full life.
beginner.whyItMatters: The first hit of a fight is where a big critical is worth the most, because it can take a dangerous monster out before it ever acts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Ideal on an opening skill or on a build that kills packs in one hit each. It gives nothing once a fight is already underway.

name: Ammo Conservation I
stats: Bolts fired by Supported Crossbow Attacks have 20% chance to not expend Ammunition
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, granting a chance to not consume a Bolt when firing.

beginner.whatItIs: A crossbow support giving each bolt a one-in-five chance of not being spent when you fire it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reloading is the pause where a crossbow character is defenceless, so firing more shots per magazine directly means less time standing still.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it into any crossbow skill you fire continuously. It matters more the longer a fight lasts.

name: Ammo Conservation II
stats: Bolts fired by Supported Crossbow Attacks have 25% chance to not expend Ammunition
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, granting a chance to not consume a Bolt when firing.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger ammunition-saving support, raising the chance to keep a bolt to one in four.
beginner.whyItMatters: The higher chance stretches a magazine noticeably further, so the reload interruption comes around less often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A straight upgrade over the first version. Take it as soon as your gem tier allows.

name: Ammo Conservation III
stats: Bolts fired by Supported Crossbow Attacks have 30% chance to not expend Ammunition
Supported Skills have 20% less Reload speed
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, granting a chance to not consume a Bolt when firing, at the cost of Reload speed.

beginner.whatItIs: The top ammunition-saving support: bolts have a 30% chance to be kept, but the skill reloads 20% more slowly.
beginner.whyItMatters: You fire more shots between reloads and each reload takes longer, so it only wins if you actually get value out of the longer magazine.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good on a build that already reloads quickly through other means. Avoid it if your reload is slow, since the drawback compounds.

name: Ancestral Call I
stats: Supported Skills are Ancestrally Boosted once every 5 seconds
description: Supports Strikes you use yourself, providing a powerful Ancestral Boost every few seconds. Cannot Support Channelled Skills and does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for strike skills you use yourself. Every five seconds the next strike is ancestrally boosted.
beginner.whyItMatters: It bakes a periodic power spike into an attack you were already making, with no cost or condition to manage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Suits a single-target strike build. Its worth drops if you switch between many attacks and rarely have the boosted one ready.

name: Ancestral Call II
stats: Supported Skills are Ancestrally Boosted once every 3 seconds
description: Supports Strikes you use yourself, providing a powerful Ancestral Boost every few seconds. Cannot Support Channelled Skills and does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded version of the strike boost, cutting the wait between boosted strikes from five seconds to three.
beginner.whyItMatters: At three seconds the boost arrives inside every meaningful exchange rather than only in long fights.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier version once available, especially on bosses where the fight is long enough to collect many boosts.

name: Arakaali's Lust
stats: Supported Skills deal 8% more Damage with Hits for each Poison on the Enemy, up to 40%
description: Supports any Skill that Hits Enemies, causing it to deal increasingly higher damage the more Poisons are on the target.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that makes the skill hit harder for every stack of poison already on the target, up to 40% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links a slow poison build to a burst finisher, so the poison you stack up is not only damage but also a growing multiplier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Put it on the skill you use to finish targets, on a build whose other skill stacks poison quickly.

name: Arbiter's Ignition
stats: Gain Elemental Archon when you Ignite an Enemy
description: Supports Fire Spell Skills causing you to gain Elemental Archon when Igniting with them.
flavourText:
"This carving seems to depict curled bodies floating in vats...
the next shows all but one of them dying. What were they
trying to do? It seems they kept trying... kept experimenting..."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for fire spells. Igniting an enemy with the supported spell grants you Elemental Archon.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts ignites, which you were applying anyway, into a buff on yourself rather than leaving them as pure damage over time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a fire caster who ignites reliably. On a spell that rarely ignites, the buff will not be up when you need it.

name: Arbiter's Reach
stats: Allies in your Presence gain Guard equal to 10% of your maximum Life for 4 seconds, every 6 seconds while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you periodically grant Guard to allies in your Presence while the Skill is active.
flavourText:
"They designed our salvation. No longer shall
our people's grief be in vain. From their hands,
perfection is wrought. Within His reach, we are safe."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for persistent buff skills. Every six seconds, allies near you gain guard worth a tenth of your maximum life for four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a buff you keep running anyway into a repeating shield for your whole party, without any button to press.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best in a group or on a minion build with allies standing near you. Solo with no companions, most of the value is unused.

name: Arcane Surge
stats: Gain Arcane Surge for 10 seconds after Spending a total of 100% of your Maximum Mana on Supported Skills
description: Supports Spells you cast yourself, tracking the mana you spend to cast them. Spending enough mana grants a burst of Mana Regeneration and Cast Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that counts the mana you spend casting the supported spell. Spend your full mana pool's worth and you gain Arcane Surge for ten seconds, giving mana regeneration and cast speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a free power spike attached to casting, and the mana regeneration partly pays for the casting that triggered it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pair it with a cheap spell you cast constantly so the buff comes up often. On an expensive spell it triggers too rarely to rely on.

name: Arjun's Medal
stats: 25% chance to load a bolt into all Crossbow skills on dealing a Killing Blow with Supported Skill
description: Supports Crossbow Skills, causing them to load a bolt into all Crossbow Ammunition on kill.
flavourText:
Confident their enemy was defenseless, the Keitans brazenly
charged the walls - but Arjun's ammunition supply reports
had been... 'inaccurate'... just like everything else Bardiyan.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage crossbow support. Killing something with the supported skill has a one-in-four chance to load a bolt into every one of your crossbow skills.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the reload pause from packs entirely, because each kill can refill everything at once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For crossbow builds that swap between several ammunition skills and want them all loaded when a pack dies.

name: Armour Break I
stats: Break Armour equal to 15% of Physical Damage dealt by Supported Skill
description: Supports Skills that Hit Enemies, causing those Hits to Break Armour based on a portion of Physical Damage dealt.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes hits break armour equal to 15% of the physical damage they dealt.
beginner.whyItMatters: Broken armour means everything you and your allies do afterwards lands harder, so it multiplies the rest of your damage rather than adding a little of its own.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Attach it to a physical skill you use to open on tough enemies. It does nothing against targets with no armour.

name: Armour Break II
stats: Break Armour equal to 15% of Physical Damage dealt by Supported Skill
15% chance to gain an Endurance Charge when Supported Skills Fully Break Armour
description: Supports Skills that Hit Enemies, causing those Hits to Break Armour based on a portion of Physical Damage dealt. On Fully Breaking Armour with Supported Skills, you have a chance to gain an Endurance Charge.

beginner.whatItIs: The middle armour-breaking support. It breaks the same 15% of physical damage as armour, and adds a 15% chance to grant you an endurance charge when armour is fully broken.
beginner.whyItMatters: The endurance charge means the same action that softens the enemy also hardens you, which is rare on a single support.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it over the plain version on a build that wants endurance charges but has no dedicated way to generate them.

name: Armour Break III
stats: Break Armour equal to 20% of Physical Damage dealt by Supported Skill
20% chance to gain an Endurance Charge when Supported Skills Fully Break Armour
description: Supports Skills that Hit Enemies, causing those Hits to Break Armour based on a portion of Physical Damage dealt. On Fully Breaking Armour with Supported Skills, you have a chance to gain an Endurance Charge.

beginner.whatItIs: The top armour-breaking support, raising both numbers to 20%: more armour broken per hit, and a better chance at an endurance charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: At this level the armour comes off fast enough that a single opening sequence sets up the rest of the fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to settle on once your gem tier allows it, on any physical build that fights armoured rares and bosses.

name: Armour Demolisher I
stats: Supported Skills Break 50% more Armour
description: Supports any skill, causing Armour Break it inflicts to be stronger.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that increases how much armour the skill strips, by half again as much as it normally would.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stacks on top of whatever is already causing the armour break, so it makes an existing armour-stripping plan finish sooner.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only useful if the skill already breaks armour somehow. On its own it creates no armour break at all.

name: Armour Demolisher II
stats: Supported Skills Break 70% more Armour
description: Supports any skill, causing Armour Break it inflicts to be stronger.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger armour-stripping multiplier, raising armour broken by 70% instead of 50%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Getting a boss's armour fully broken a few hits earlier is the difference between a burst window landing and being wasted.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap up from the first version whenever your gem tier permits, keeping it alongside a skill that actually breaks armour.

name: Armour Explosion
stats: Supported Skills trigger an Explosion when they Fully Break an enemy's Armour
description: Supports Attacks and Warcries, causing them to trigger a Fiery explosion when they Fully Break an enemy's Armour.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for attacks and warcries. When one of them fully breaks an enemy's armour, a fiery explosion goes off.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives armour breaking a visible payoff instead of leaving it as a setup step you never see the result of.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good on a physical melee build that is already stripping armour off packs. Poor if you rarely finish an armour break.

name: Astral Projection
stats: Supported Skills Cast at the targeted location instead of around you
Supported Skills have 25% less Area of Effect
description: Supports Nova Skills, causing those Skills to take place at the targeted location when used instead of around you.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for nova skills. The nova goes off where you aimed rather than centred on you, but covers 25% less area.
beginner.whyItMatters: Novas normally force you into the middle of a pack; casting one at range keeps you out of it entirely.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For fragile casters who want nova damage without standing in melee. Skip it if you have the defences to stand in the pack, since the area loss is real.

name: Atalui's Bloodletting
stats: Supported Skills have Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs
Supported Skills Gain 2% of Damage as extra Physical Damage per 20 Life cost, up to 40%
description: Supports any Skill, turning a portion of its Mana cost into a Life cost. Does not support Skills which reserve Spirit. Supported Skills Gain a portion of their Life cost as extra Physical Damage.
flavourText:
Atazek and Atalui rose, battered and dark, bleeding from a hundred
different wounds. She gave her brother a sinister grin. "Shall we
show them what happens to those who challenge the Vaal?"

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that turns the skill's mana cost into a life cost, then adds physical damage on top of the hit for every twenty life it costs, up to forty percent added.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes your life pool a second mana pool, which is powerful if you can heal fast and dangerous if you cannot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a build with strong life recovery. Without it, a hard fight becomes a race between your damage and your own costs.

name: Atziri's Allure
stats: Curses inflicted by Supported Skills ignore Curse limit
Curses inflicted by Supported Skills are reflected back to you
Supported Skills have 20% less Curse Effect
description: Supports Curse Spells you cast yourself, causing those Curses to ignore the usual Curse Limit, but be reflected back to you when inflicted.
flavourText:
Such was her seductive power, every noble in the court fell
over themselves to do her bidding. Winning a single glance
away from her mirror meant more than their lives.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for curses you cast. The curses ignore the usual limit on how many can be on a target, they land 20% weaker, and each one is reflected back onto you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stacking curses past the normal limit is a large gain, but taking your own curses means the drawback scales with how much you use it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse-focused build that has built resistance to the curses it uses. It is a bad idea on a character with no answer to being cursed.

name: Atziri's Communion
stats: Supported Skills Reserve a percentage of your maximum
Life equal to 66% of base Spirit Reservation
description: Supports Persistent Skills, making them Reserve Life instead of Spirit. Cannot Support Skills which create Minions.
flavourText:
The Red Communion was meant to transcend the limits
of the soul, to transfigure the flesh, to bestow immortality.
It accomplished all of these things... most horribly.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that changes a persistent skill's reservation from spirit to life, reserving life worth two thirds of the original spirit cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spirit is the tight resource for most builds, so paying in life instead frees up room for another persistent skill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When you have spirit reserved to the limit and a large enough life pool to give some of it away permanently.

name: Atziri's Impatience
stats: Lose 25% of maximum Life, Mana, and Energy Shield when you use Supported Skills
Supported Skills have 100% increased cooldown recovery rate
description: Supports Skills you use yourself that have Cooldowns, dramatically increasing the rate at which those Cooldowns Recover, but causing you to lose Life, Mana, and Energy Shield when they are used. Cannot Support Meta Skills or Persistent Skills, or modify the Skills of Minions.
flavourText:
"Those who bored the Queen suffered an excessive punishment:
everyone they had ever known would be killed, effectively
erasing their life. So, no matter the cost... none kept her waiting."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that doubles the cooldown recovery rate of the supported skill, at the cost of a quarter of your life, mana and energy shield every time you use it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Halving the wait on a strong cooldown skill can define a build, but the self-damage makes every use a real decision.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a skill whose cooldown is the only thing holding your damage back, on a character that can restore a quarter of everything quickly.

name: Auto Reload
stats: Supported Skills reload automatically when Heavy Stunning an enemy with them
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, causing them to automatically reload when they Heavy Stun an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A crossbow support that reloads the skill by itself whenever it heavy stuns an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the reload from exactly the moment you want to keep attacking, which is right after you have staggered something.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on a heavy, high-stun crossbow skill. On a fast, light skill that rarely heavy stuns, it almost never triggers.

name: Barbs I
stats: Deal your Thorns damage to the next 4 enemies Hit by Supported Skills after you Retaliate with Thorns
description: Supports Melee Strike Skills. After you Retaliate with Thorns Damage, you also deal your Thorns damage to enemies you Hit with Supported Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee strike support. After you retaliate with thorns damage, the next four enemies your strike hits also take your thorns damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Thorns normally only punishes whoever hit you; this spreads that damage onto targets of your choosing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a thorns build that stands in packs and gets hit often. It does nothing until a retaliation has actually happened.

name: Barbs II
stats: Deal your Thorns damage to the next 6 enemies Hit by Supported Skills after you Retaliate with Thorns
description: Supports Melee Strike Skills. After you Retaliate with Thorns Damage, you also deal your Thorns damage to enemies you Hit with Supported Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved thorns-spreading support, carrying your thorns damage onto six enemies after a retaliation instead of four.
beginner.whyItMatters: Six targets covers most of a normal pack, so one retaliation can clear a group rather than a corner of it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Prefer it over the four-target version whenever you are clearing packs on a thorns character.

name: Barbs III
stats: Deal your Thorns damage twice to the next enemy Hit by Supported Skills after you Retaliate with Thorns
description: Supports Melee Strike Skills. After you Retaliate with Thorns Damage, you also deal your Thorns damage twice to enemies you Hit with Supported Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: The single-target version of the thorns-spreading support: after retaliating, the next enemy you strike takes your thorns damage two times over.
beginner.whyItMatters: Concentrating the whole payout onto one enemy is what you want against a boss, where there is nothing else to spread it to.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose this over the wider versions specifically for boss fights and other single-target situations.

name: Battershout
stats: Support
Supported Skills cannot Break Armour
Supported Skills Consume Fully Broken Armour on Enemies within range to Trigger Battershout
Battershout
Deals Physical Area Damage based off of the Broken Armour of the target which this explosion was Triggered from.
+5% to Critical Hit Chance
50% more damage against Unique enemies
Cannot Break Armour
Explosion radius is 2 metres
Deals Physical Damage equal to 20% Broken Armour of the target Triggered from
Does not take into account Overbroken Armour
description: Supports Warcry Skills. Supported Skills Consume Fully Broken Armour to trigger Physical Damage explosions on Enemies within their range but cannot themselves Break Armour.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support. The warcry can no longer break armour itself, but it consumes armour that is already fully broken on nearby enemies to set off physical explosions.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the payoff half of an armour-breaking plan, turning stripped armour into a burst of damage across a pack.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a build that already fully breaks armour with something else. Alone it removes your warcry's armour break and gives nothing back.

name: Behead I
stats: Killing Blows from Supported Strike Skills against Rare monsters grant one of their Modifiers for 20 seconds
description: Supports Strike skills, causing them to steal a Modifier from Rare monsters they kill.

beginner.whatItIs: A strike support. Killing a rare monster with the supported strike steals one of that monster's modifiers for you to use for twenty seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Rare monster modifiers are strong, and borrowing one for twenty seconds can carry you through the pack that rare was leading.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good in maps and other content dense with rare monsters. It is dead weight in a boss fight with no rares to kill.

name: Behead II
stats: Killing Blows from Supported Strike Skills against Rare monsters grant two of their Modifiers for 20 seconds
description: Supports Strike skills, causing them to steal two Modifiers from Rare monsters they kill.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded modifier-stealing support, taking two modifiers from each rare monster your strike kills.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two stolen modifiers at once make the buff swing whole encounters rather than just easing them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it in any content where rare monsters appear in numbers rather than one at a time.

name: Bhatair's Vengeance
stats: When you Freeze a target with Supported Skills, for each 2 Rage you have, you and Allies in your Presence gain 1% of Damage as Cold Damage for 15 seconds
description: Supports Attacks and Warcries you use yourself. Freezing an enemy with Supported Skills infuses you and your allies with Cold damage for a short time.
flavourText:
It is said that the Steward of Tales roams Wraeclast still,
lost in the form of a Wyvern, full of sorrow and fury at
the loss of his beloved pupils to the King in the Mists...

beginner.whatItIs: A support for attacks and warcries. Freezing an enemy with the supported skill grants you and nearby allies extra cold damage for fifteen seconds, scaled by how much rage you are holding.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties three separate things you were already doing together: building rage, freezing, and dealing cold damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage-generating build that also freezes. Without rage to spend the buff is close to nothing.

name: Bidding I
stats: Supported Minions have 20% increased Cooldown Recovery Rate for Command Skills
Supported Minions' Command Skills deal 20% more Damage
description: Supports Minion Skills. Supported Minions deal more damage and have increased Cooldown Recovery Rate with Command Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support that makes your minions' command skills deal 20% more damage and recover their cooldowns 20% faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Command skills are the minion abilities you actually control, so speeding them up gives you more say in a fight instead of watching.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it once you have minions whose command skills you use on purpose rather than leaving them to fight on their own.

name: Bidding II
stats: Supported Minions have 30% increased Cooldown Recovery Rate for Command Skills
Supported Minions' Command Skills deal 30% more Damage
description: Supports Minion Skills. Supported Minions deal more damage and have increased Cooldown Recovery Rate with Command Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: The middle minion command support, lifting both the damage and the cooldown recovery to 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra recovery means the command is ready again before the last one has finished paying off.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A straightforward upgrade over the first version for any command-driven minion build.

name: Bidding III
stats: Supported Minions have 80% increased Cooldown Recovery Rate for Command Skills
description: Supports Minion Skills. Supported Minions have significantly increased Cooldown Recovery Rate with Command Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: The top minion command support. It drops the damage bonus entirely and instead gives an 80% increase to command cooldown recovery.
beginner.whyItMatters: This version is about frequency rather than force, which suits commands whose value is the effect they cause rather than the damage they do.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it over the second version when your minion command is a utility button you want available constantly.

name: Biting Frost I
stats: Supported Skills cannot cause Freeze buildup
Supported Skills deal 20% more damage to Frozen Unique enemies
Supported Skills Consume Freeze on enemies to deal 40% more Damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing them to deal more damage to Frozen enemies but consume their Freeze. Cannot support skills that Consume Freeze.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops the skill building freeze, but makes it deal 20% more damage to frozen unique enemies and consume an existing freeze for 40% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the cashing-in half of a freeze build, spending a freeze another skill created for a large hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only alongside a second skill that does the freezing. Put it on a skill that has to freeze on its own and you have broken your own build.

name: Biting Frost II
stats: Supported Skills cannot cause Freeze buildup
Supported Skills deal 20% more damage to Frozen Unique enemies
Supported Skills Consume Freeze on enemies to deal 40% more Damage
Freezes Consumed by Supported Skills Chill the target
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing them to deal more damage to Frozen enemies but consume their Freeze, leaving them Chilled. Cannot support skills that Consume Freeze.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded freeze-consuming support, with the same damage bonuses plus a chill left on the target whenever it eats a freeze.
beginner.whyItMatters: The leftover chill keeps the enemy slowed after the freeze is spent, so you are not handing back all the control you just used.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it over the plain version on any build that freezes with one skill and detonates with another.

name: Blazing Critical
stats: Attacks Gain 15% of Damage as Fire Damage for 5 seconds on Critically Hitting with Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which Hit enemies. Critical Hits with Supported Skills imbue all of your Attacks with Fire damage for a duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes a critical hit with the supported skill grant all your attacks extra fire damage for five seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: The bonus spreads to every attack you make, not just the one that crit, so one lucky hit lifts your whole rotation.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with high critical hit chance that swings often enough to keep the five seconds refreshed.

name: Bleed I
stats: Supported Skills have 50% chance to inflict Bleeding
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to inflict Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving the skill a coin-flip chance to make enemies bleed when it hits them.
beginner.whyItMatters: Bleeding keeps damaging an enemy after you have moved on, which is how a character kills more than one thing at a time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An easy early pick on any physical attack. Its worth falls off if you later build around a different ailment.

name: Bleed II
stats: Supported Skills have 75% chance to inflict Bleeding
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to inflict Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: The middle bleed support, raising the chance to inflict bleeding to three hits in four.
beginner.whyItMatters: At this rate bleeding is on almost everything you touch, so you can plan damage around it rather than hoping for it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to run while levelling a physical build, until the guaranteed one is available.

name: Bleed III
stats: Supported Skills have 100% chance to inflict Bleeding
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to inflict Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: The guaranteed bleed support: every hit from the supported skill inflicts bleeding.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the chance removes the variance, which matters most on slow skills that only get a few hits in per fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The right choice for any build that treats bleeding as its main source of damage.

name: Bleed IV
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Melee Physical Damage against Bleeding enemies
Hits from Supported Skills inflict Incision
Supported Attacks cannot cause Bleeding
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal more Melee Physical Damage to Bleeding Enemies, but be unable to inflict Bleeding itself. Supported Skills also inflict Incision on Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: The payoff bleed support. The skill can no longer cause bleeding at all, but deals 30% more melee physical damage to already-bleeding enemies and inflicts incision on hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the other half of a bleed build, turning bleeding that another skill applied into a large hit rather than more bleeding.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a second skill, once something else in your setup reliably applies bleeding first.

name: Blind I
stats: Supported Skills Blind Enemies on Hit
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing them to Blind on Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that blinds enemies whenever the skill hits them.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blinded enemies miss you far more often, so this is defence bought with a support slot rather than gear.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Put it on whatever skill touches the most enemies, since blind is worth most when it is on the whole pack.

name: Blind II
stats: Supported Skills Blind Enemies on Hit
Blind inflicted with Supported Skills has 20% increased Effect
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing them to Blind on Hit with increased effect.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger blind support, which blinds on hit and makes that blind 20% more effective.
beginner.whyItMatters: A deeper blind means a larger share of incoming attacks miss, which compounds when you are surrounded.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take once available, especially on a character who fights inside packs rather than at range.

name: Blindside
stats: Supported Skills cannot inflict Blind
Supported Skills have 15% more Critical Damage Bonus with Hits against Blinded Enemies
Supported Skills have 15% more chance to Critically Hit Blinded Enemies
description: Supports Skills which can cause Damaging Hits. Supported Skills are more likely to Critically Hit Blinded Enemies, and deal more Damage with Critical Hits against Blinded Enemies, but cannot themselves inflict Blind.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops the skill blinding, and in exchange gives it 15% more critical hit chance and 15% more critical damage against enemies that are already blinded.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts blind from a defensive effect into a damage multiplier, but only if something else in your build is doing the blinding.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pair it with a separate blind source. On its own it takes away blind and gives you nothing to use.

name: Bloodlust
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Melee Physical Damage against Bleeding enemies
Supported Attacks cannot cause Bleeding
description: Supports Melee Attacks, causing them to deal more damage against Bleeding enemies, but preventing them from inflicting Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support giving 30% more melee physical damage against bleeding enemies, while preventing your attacks from causing bleeding.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a pure payoff support, trading the ability to start a bleed for a much bigger hit on one that already exists.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For the second skill in a bleed build. Never on the skill you rely on to apply the bleed.

name: Bone Shrapnel
stats: Supported Skills cannot cause Pin buildup
Supported Skills trigger Bone Shrapnel Explosions on killing Pinned Enemies
description: Supports Skills which Hit Enemies. Supported Skills trigger Bone Shrapnel explosions when killing Pinned Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops the skill building pin, but sets off a bone shrapnel explosion whenever it kills a pinned enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Kills on pinned enemies start chaining into the pack around them, which turns single kills into cleared rooms.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Works when another skill is doing the pinning. It gives nothing on a build with no pin in it.

name: Boundless Energy I
stats: Supported Skills gain 35% increased Energy
description: Supports Meta Skills. Supported Skills generate Energy significantly faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for meta skills that increases the energy they gain by 35%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Meta skills only act once they have banked enough energy, so faster energy directly means the automatic effect fires more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it into any meta skill whose triggered effect you want happening more frequently.

name: Boundless Energy II
stats: Supported Skills gain 45% increased Energy
description: Supports Meta Skills. Supported Skills generate Energy significantly faster.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger meta skill support, raising energy gained by 45%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra ten points compound over a fight, so a triggered skill lands several more times in a long encounter.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap it in the moment your gem tier reaches it; nothing about the setup changes except the number.

name: Bounty I
stats: Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 50% more Charm charges
Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 50% more Life Flask Charges
Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 50% more Mana Flask Charges
description: Supports any Skill that Hits Enemies, causing Enemies it kills to grant more Flask and Charm charges.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes enemies killed by the skill give half again as many life flask, mana flask and charm charges.
beginner.whyItMatters: Flasks are your emergency healing, and running out mid-fight is a common way to die; this keeps them topped up while you clear.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on the skill you clear packs with, since charges come from the volume of kills rather than from big ones.

name: Bounty II
stats: Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 100% more Charm charges
Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 100% more Life Flask Charges
Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 100% more Mana Flask Charges
description: Supports any Skill that Hits Enemies, causing Enemies it kills to grant more Flask and Charm charges.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger charge-generating support, doubling the flask and charm charges you get from enemies the skill kills.
beginner.whyItMatters: At double charges you can drink far more freely, which changes how aggressively you can play a dangerous map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it once flasks are how you survive rather than a convenience between fights.

name: Brambleslam
stats: Supported Slams create 3 Brambles
Brambles
Cooldown Time: 0.15 s
Hazardous thorns damage and Maim enemies with which they come in contact.
Attack Damage of this skill is 35% of Default Attack Damage
Increases and reductions to Thorns Damage apply to Hit Damage with this skill
Maim on Hit
80% less damage if destroyed within 0.5 seconds by something other than you
Bramble radius is 1 metre
Bramble duration is 8 seconds
description: Supports Slam Skills. Supported Skills create Hazardous Brambles on the ground that activate after a duration. Enemies which come in contact with these thorns take damage and are Maimed. A maximum of 20 Brambles are allowed at one time. Does not modify Skills used by Minions or Totems.

beginner.whatItIs: A slam support that scatters three hazardous brambles on the ground with each slam. Enemies that walk into them take damage and are maimed, and up to twenty can exist at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: It leaves damage behind you on the floor, so ground you have already fought over keeps working while you move on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Strong when enemies chase you through a space you have prepared. Weak against ranged enemies that never step into the brambles.

name: Branching Fissures I
stats: Supported Skills' Fissures branch 2 times
Supported Skills' Branched Fissures deal 40% less damage
Supported Skills' Branched Fissures have 35% less area of effect
description: Supports Skills which create Fissures in the ground, causing them to create additional secondary Fissures which branch off from the primary fissure, with lowered area of effect and Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for fissure skills. Each fissure splits twice into smaller branches that deal 40% less damage and cover 35% less area.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single narrow crack in the ground becomes a spreading web, so a skill aimed at one enemy touches the ones beside it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs with a fissure skill. The branches are too weak to matter against a single boss.

name: Branching Fissures II
stats: Supported Skills' Fissures branch 2 times
Supported Skills' Branched Fissures deal 30% less damage
Supported Skills' Branched Fissures have 35% less area of effect
description: Supports Skills which create Fissures in the ground, causing them to create additional secondary Fissures which branch off from the primary fissure, with lowered area of effect and Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded fissure-branching support, where the branches lose only 30% of their damage instead of 40%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stronger branches make the split worth taking even when some of the pack is tougher than a normal monster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the first version once available on any fissure-based clearing setup.

name: Breachlord's Amalgam
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills Return to you
Returning Projectiles from Supported Skills Pierce all targets
description: Supports Lightning or Cold skills you use yourself which fire Projectiles and do not already have cooldowns, adding a cooldown and making the Projectiles return, piercing through targets as they do so.
flavourText:
The flesh rejoiced. The melding began.
Then, fear. Something foreign within.
It was cast out too late. The unity was broken.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for lightning or cold projectile skills that have no cooldown of their own. It adds a cooldown, and makes the projectiles return to you, piercing everything on the way back.
beginner.whyItMatters: A returning projectile hits the same line twice, so each shot covers ground going out and coming back.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slower, harder-hitting elemental projectile skill. It is a poor fit for a rapid-fire skill that hates gaining a cooldown.

name: Breachlord's Rift
stats: Supported Skills Break 50% of Armour when Freezing or Electrocuting targets
Fully Broken Armour inflicted with Supported Skills also increases Cold and Lightning Damage Taken from Hits
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to Break Armour of enemies it Freezes or Electrocutes.
flavourText:
Our Broken Sun... it is no mere allegory. It is
the consequence of insolent disharmony.
For now, it is contained, but time is against us.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that breaks half the armour of any enemy the skill freezes or electrocutes, and makes fully broken armour also raise the cold and lightning damage that target takes.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links elemental control to armour breaking, so freezing something also makes your follow-up hits land harder.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold or lightning build that fights armoured enemies and can reliably freeze or electrocute them.

name: Brink I
stats: Stun buildup caused by Supported Skills cannot reach 100%
Hits with Supported Skills cause 30% more Stun buildup
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills build up Heavy Stun more quickly, but cannot themselves Heavy Stun.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support that raises stun buildup by 30% but prevents the skill from ever finishing a heavy stun itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stacks the enemy up to the edge of being stunned so a different, heavier skill can land the finishing blow.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a fast setup attack paired with a big second skill. On your only attack, it means nothing ever gets stunned.

name: Brink II
stats: Stun buildup caused by Supported Skills cannot reach 100%
Hits with Supported Skills cause 50% more Stun buildup
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills build up Stun more quickly, but cannot themselves Stun.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger stun-building support, raising stun buildup by 50% while still refusing to finish the stun.
beginner.whyItMatters: At half again as much buildup, the enemy reaches the brink in far fewer hits, tightening the setup-then-finish rhythm.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Upgrade from the first version on any two-skill stun combination.

name: Brittle Armour
stats: Hits against targets Frozen by Supported Skills Break Armour equal to 100% of Physical damage dealt
description: Supports Skills which can Hit enemies. Hits with Supported Skills which Freeze enemies cause Physical damage against them to Break their Armour while they remain Frozen.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where hits against an enemy your skill froze break armour equal to all of the physical damage dealt.
beginner.whyItMatters: Freezing already stops a monster acting; adding full armour breaking means the frozen window also softens it for everything after.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that mixes physical and cold damage and freezes things regularly.

name: Brutality I
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% more Physical Damage
Supported Skills deal no Chaos Damage
Supported Skills deal no Elemental Damage
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, boosting its Physical damage at the expense of all other Damage Types.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that gives 25% more physical damage but removes all elemental and chaos damage from the skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a clean trade only if the skill was pure physical to begin with; otherwise you are deleting a chunk of your own damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Check what your skill and your gear actually deal first. On a truly physical build it is one of the simplest gains available.

name: Brutality II
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Physical Damage
Supported Skills deal no Chaos Damage
Supported Skills deal no Elemental Damage
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, boosting its Physical damage at the expense of all other Damage Types.

beginner.whatItIs: The middle version of the physical-only support, raising the bonus to 30% more physical damage under the same restriction.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra five points come at no additional cost, since you have already given up the other damage types.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Once you have committed to physical damage, there is no reason to keep the weaker version in the socket.

name: Brutality III
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Physical Damage
Supported Skills deal no Chaos Damage
Supported Skills deal no Elemental Damage
Hits with Supported Skills have 20% chance to ignore Enemy Physical Damage reduction
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, boosting its Physical damage at the expense of all other Damage Types, as well as giving Hits from that skill a chance to ignore Physical Damage reduction.

beginner.whatItIs: The top physical-only support: 30% more physical damage, no elemental or chaos damage, and a 20% chance for hits to ignore the enemy's physical damage reduction.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ignoring damage reduction matters most against exactly the armoured targets that normally blunt a physical build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here on a pure physical character, particularly one fighting heavily armoured bosses.

name: Brutus' Brain
stats: Minions from Supported Skills cannot be Damaged
Minions from Supported Skills deal no Damage
description: Supports skills which create Minions, causing those Minions to be unable to deal or take Damage. Cannot support skills which create undamageable Minions.
flavourText:
Shavronne gleefully raised her arms to the sky as lightning
flashed. She'd done it! Her creation was perfect! Invincible.
Immortal! But she soon realized there was one piece missing...

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage minion support that makes the created minions unable to deal damage or take damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns minions into permanent fixtures that exist only for what their presence gives you, rather than fighters that die.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only for builds whose minions matter for an aura, a body block or a trigger. It removes the point of a minion meant to kill things.

name: Burgeon I
stats: Supported Skills deal 10% more Damage per second spent Channelling, up to 40%
description: Supports Channelling Skills you use yourself, causing them to deal more damage the longer they have been Channelled.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for channelled skills that adds 10% more damage for each second you keep channelling, up to 40%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Channelled skills ask you to stand still, and this makes that commitment pay off the longer you hold it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a channelled skill you use on bosses, where you have four seconds of safety to reach the cap.

name: Burgeon II
stats: Supported Skills deal 20% more Damage per second spent Channelling, up to 40%
description: Supports Channelling Skills you use yourself, causing them to deal more damage the longer they have been Channelled.

beginner.whatItIs: The faster version of the channelling ramp, gaining 20% more damage per second and reaching the same 40% cap in half the time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reaching full power in two seconds instead of four makes the ramp usable in ordinary fights, not just long ones.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Prefer it whenever you channel in short bursts between repositioning rather than holding for four seconds.

name: Burning Inscription
stats: Supported Skills trigger Burning Inscription after their Runic Inscriptions expire
Burning Inscription
Create Ignited Ground Igniting Enemies based on a percentage of your Maximum Mana.
Create Ignited Ground, Igniting enemies as though dealing Fire Damage equal to 20% of your Maximum Mana
Ignited Ground radius is 2 metres
Ignited Ground duration is 4 seconds
description: Supports any Skill which creates Runic Inscriptions when Cast, causing those Runic Inscriptions to trigger Burning Inscription when they expire. Burning Inscription is a Spell which creates Ignited Ground based off of your Maximum Mana.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for skills that leave runic inscriptions. When an inscription expires it creates ignited ground, with the burn scaled off your maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: Expiring inscriptions normally just disappear; this gives them a second life as a patch of burning floor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an inscription caster with a large mana pool, since the fire damage is measured against that pool.

name: Bursting Plague
stats: Support
Poison from Supported Skills also adds 100% of Damage per Second to Enemy as Plague, up to a maximum of 20% of Enemy's maximum Life
Plague Burst
Cooldown Time: 0.10s
Triggered when an enemy Poisoned by a supported skill dies, dealing Physical damage around them based on the built-up Plague.
+5% to Critical Hit Chance
Deals Physical Damage equal to 100% of Plague on Triggering Enemy
Has up to 100% more Area of Effect at maximum Plague
Burst radius is 1.8 metres
description: Supports skills that can Poison enemies, causing Poisoned enemies to gain Plague over time and explode in a Plague Burst on death. Cannot support the skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for poisoning skills. Poisoned enemies also build plague, and when one dies it bursts for physical damage based on the plague it had accumulated.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a poison build the pack-clearing explosion it usually lacks, since poison alone kills slowly and quietly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison build clearing groups. Against a single boss there is nothing for the burst to spread onto.

name: Cadence
stats: Supported Skills have 8% more Attack speed for each time they've been used Recently
Supported Skills are unusable for 10 seconds after being used 6 or more times within four seconds
description: Supports Attacks you use yourself. Supported Skills gain more Attack speed each time you use them, but will become unusable if used too frequently in a short time frame. Sustained Skills will instead gain Attack speed periodically while being used.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants 8% more attack speed for each recent use of the skill, but locks the skill out for ten seconds if you use it six or more times within four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a controlled rhythm and punishes mashing, so the skill becomes something you pace rather than spam.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Suits a deliberate, heavier attack. Avoid it on a skill you hold down, because the lockout will catch you mid-fight.

name: Caltrops
stats: Support
Projectiles from Supported Skills trigger Caltrops when they reach the end of their flight
Caltrops
Attack Time: 0.00 sec
Critical Hit Chance: 5.00%
Increases and reductions to Thorns Damage apply to Hit Damage with this skill
Maim on Hit
Caltrop radius is 0.5 metres
Caltrops land within a 3 metre radius of Projectile impact
Creates 1 Caltrop
Caltrop duration is 8 seconds
Deals 60% of your Dexterity as Physical Damage on Hit
description: Supports Ranged Spear Attacks. Supported Skills create Caltrops when Projectiles they create reach the end of their flight.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for ranged spear attacks that drops a caltrop wherever a projectile finishes its flight, damaging and maiming what walks over it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It puts a slowing hazard between you and whatever is chasing you, which is exactly what a ranged character needs.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Throw past enemies and back away over the caltrops. It does little if you are fighting at melee range anyway.

name: Cannibalism I
stats: 2% of maximum Life recovered on kill while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to recover Life on kill while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buff skills. While the buff is running, every kill restores 2% of your maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties healing to killing, so clearing a pack is also how you recover from the last one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character that kills steadily and has no other reliable recovery between fights.

name: Cannibalism II
stats: 3% of maximum Life recovered on kill while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to recover Life on kill while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger kill-healing support, restoring 3% of maximum life per kill while the supported buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Half again as much life per kill means a dense pack can fully heal you in the middle of fighting it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A clear upgrade over the first version for any build that stays alive by clearing quickly.

name: Catalysing Elements
stats: Supported Skills Trigger Catalysing Discharge when boosted by an Elemental Ground Surface
description: Supports Skills which are boosted by Elemental Ground Surfaces, Triggering Catalysing Discharge of the corresponding type when they are boosted by an allied Elemental Ground Surface.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for skills that get boosted by elemental ground. When the skill is boosted by friendly elemental ground, it triggers a catalysing discharge matching that element.
beginner.whyItMatters: It adds a free burst of damage on top of a bonus you were already collecting from standing on the right ground.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a build that actually creates elemental ground. Without it, the trigger condition is never met.

name: Catha's Brilliance
stats: Minions from Supported Skills Blind Enemies within a 2 metre radius
Minions from Supported Skills Ignite Enemies within a radius of 2 metres as though dealing Base Fire Damage equal to 10% of Minion's Maximum Life
description: Supports skills which create Companions, causing enemies near them to be Blinded and Ignited. The damage of the Ignite is based on the Life of the supported Minion.
flavourText:
"The yellow sap... the Vivid flow... it is the energy of
harmony between disparate forces. They call it the
Catha, an aspect of the Goddess. It is so much more."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for companion skills. Enemies near your companions are blinded and ignited, with the ignite scaled off the companion's own maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a companion a constant area effect just for standing there, so a tanky companion becomes an offensive tool too.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with a large, durable companion that stays in the middle of fights.

name: Catharsis
stats: Supported Skill requires 20 Volatility on you to use
Using Supported Skills will explode a random amount of Volatility on you
description: Supports any Skill you use yourself, causing supported Skill to detonate Volatility that is present on you. Supported Skill can only be used while you have a certain amount of Volatility and cannot support Skills which already have another Condition.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that requires 20 volatility on you to use the skill, and detonates a random amount of that volatility when you do.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a resource you accumulate into a burst, but it also locks the skill out entirely while you are below the threshold.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a build that generates volatility fast. Attach it to a skill you need on demand and it will be unavailable when you need it.

name: Chain I
stats: Supported Skills Chain +1 times
Supported Skills deal 30% less Damage with Hits
description: Supports Projectile skills and any other skills that Chain, causing them to Chain additional times.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that lets the skill chain to one more target, at the cost of 30% less hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: One extra bounce roughly widens what a single cast covers, which is worth more than raw damage while clearing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs. Take it off for boss fights, where the extra chain finds nothing and the damage loss is all you get.

name: Chain II
stats: Supported Skills Chain +2 times
Supported Skills deal 50% less Damage with Hits
description: Supports Projectile skills and any other skills that Chain, causing them to Chain additional times.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger chaining support, adding two chains but cutting hit damage by half.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two extra bounces can clear a whole room from one cast, provided the pack is large enough that the halved damage still kills.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best in dense content with many weak enemies. Against tougher packs the damage penalty starts leaving things alive.

name: Chain III
stats: Supported Skills Chain +2 times
Supported Skills deal 40% less Damage with Hits
description: Supports Projectile skills and any other skills that Chain, causing them to Chain additional times.

beginner.whatItIs: The final chaining support, adding two chains while costing 40% of the skill's hit damage instead of the 50% the earlier version charged.
beginner.whyItMatters: You keep the same reach as the middle version but hand back less damage, so packs of tougher monsters still die to the bounces.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The chaining support to settle on for mapping once your gem tier allows it.

name: Chaos Attunement
stats: Supported Attacks Gain 25% of Damage as extra Chaos Damage
Supported Attacks deal 50% less non-Chaos Damage
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to Gain Chaos Damage but deal less Damage of other Types.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that adds a quarter of your damage again as chaos damage, but cuts all your non-chaos attack damage in half.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage bypasses energy shield, so this is a way to make a physical or elemental attack threaten enemies that hide behind a shield.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only worth it if your build stacks chaos damage further. Attached to an ordinary attack, the halved base damage outweighs the gain.

name: Chaos Mastery
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Chaos Skills
description: Supports Chaos skills, granting them an additional level. Does not support skills which do not have levels.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants a chaos skill one extra gem level.
beginner.whyItMatters: An extra level raises everything about the skill at once, including damage and the numbers on its own effects, without any drawback.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A safe pick in any chaos build. It does nothing on skills that have no level, so check the skill first.

name: Chaotic Freeze
stats: Chaos damage Contributes to Freeze buildup for Hits against targets taking damage over time from Supported Skills
description: Supports Spells that deal non-Ailment Chaos damage over time. Enemies taking damage over time from Debuffs caused by supported skills will suffer Freeze build up from Chaos damage Hits from any source. Does not Support Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for chaos damage-over-time spells. Enemies suffering that damage begin building freeze from any chaos hit, from any source.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage normally cannot freeze at all, so this hands a chaos build a form of crowd control it otherwise has no access to.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a chaos caster who wants to lock enemies down as well as melt them, especially against packs that would otherwise reach you.

name: Charge Profusion I
stats: Supported Skills have 30% chance to grant an additional Charge
description: Supports skills that can generate Charges, giving them a chance to generate an additional Charge when they do so.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that gives skills which generate charges a 30% chance to produce one extra charge each time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Charges are the fuel behind most critical hit and defence bonuses, and this raises how quickly you reach maximum without changing your rotation.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Attach it to whichever skill already makes charges. It does nothing on a skill that generates none.

name: Charge Profusion II
stats: Supported Skills have 30% chance to grant an additional Charge
Supported Skills have 15% chance to grant an additional random Charge
description: Supports skills that can generate Charges, giving them a chance to generate an additional Charge when they do so, as well as a chance to generate an additional Charge of a random type.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded charge support, keeping the 30% chance for an extra charge and adding a 15% chance for one of a random type on top.
beginner.whyItMatters: The random charge often lands on a type you have no other way of generating, filling a gap rather than deepening a strength.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it on builds that benefit from more than one charge type, since the random charge fills a gap.

name: Charged Mark
stats: Supported Mark Skills Trigger Charged Mark when they are Activated
description: Supports Mark Skills, causing them to Trigger Charged Mark when they are Activated. Charged Mark creates Shocked Ground at the target's location.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for mark skills that lays down shocked ground where the mark is when it activates.
beginner.whyItMatters: Marks are usually a pure debuff on one target, and this turns each activation into a patch of ground that also hurts everything around it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that marks a target in the middle of a pack rather than picking off a lone enemy.

name: Charged Shots I
stats: One in every 3 shots with Supported Skills is a Charged Shot
Charged Shots with Supported Skills Gain 30% of Damage as extra Lightning Damage
Charged Shots with Supported Skills recover 100% of their Mana cost when used
description: Supports Bow Attacks. Every third shot with Supported Skills restores a portion of its Mana cost and Gains Damage as extra Lightning Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A bow support where every third shot becomes a charged shot, gaining extra lightning damage and refunding its full mana cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: The mana refund means a bow build can keep firing longer, and the lightning is a bonus attached to a rhythm you are already keeping.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Very good while levelling a bow character, where running out of mana is the usual thing that stops you attacking.

name: Charged Shots II
stats: One in every 3 shots with Supported Skills is a Charged Shot
Charged Shots with Supported Skills Gain 60% of Damage as extra Lightning Damage
description: Supports Bow Attacks. Every third shot with Supported Skills Gains Damage as extra Lightning Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger charged-shot support. Every third shot gains double the extra lightning damage, but the mana refund is gone.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades sustain for damage, which is the right way round once your mana problems are solved by gear instead.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap to this once mana is no longer a constraint on how often you can fire.

name: Cirel's Cultivation
stats: Supported Skills can only have one active Totem
Totems created by Supported Skills have 5% increased area of effect per allied Totem in effect radius
Totems created by Supported Skills deal 10% more damage per allied Totem in effect radius
Totems created by supported Skills regenerate 1% of maximum Life per second per allied Totem in effect radius
Supported Totems can gain benefits for having up to 5 Totems in effect radius
Counts allied Totems in radius of 4 metres
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, preventing you from having more than one of that Totem but granting significant benefits for Supported Totems based how many allied Totems are near them. Does not Support Skills used by Minions.
flavourText:
The oldest and greatest fortress on Wraeclast was grown, not built.
She Who Waited planted their seeds in a time of ash and snow.
Now, the gate of the Taisce is unassailable, yet open to all.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage totem support that limits you to a single totem of that kind, but rewards it heavily for standing near your other totems: more area, more damage and life regeneration per nearby ally totem, counting up to five.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a totem build from many weak posts into a deliberate cluster, where placement is the skill rather than volume.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a build running several different totems close together. With one totem alone it is a straight downgrade.

name: Clarity I
stats: 30% Increased Mana Regeneration Rate while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain increased Mana Regeneration while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buff skills that raises your mana regeneration by 30% while the buff is running.
beginner.whyItMatters: Mana regeneration is what lets you keep casting between packs, so this quietly raises how often you can use your expensive skills.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it into a buff you always have active, on any character that runs out of mana during a fight.

name: Clarity II
stats: 50% Increased Mana Regeneration Rate while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain increased Mana Regeneration while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger mana regeneration support, giving 50% increased regeneration while the supported buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Half again as much regeneration can be the difference between pausing to recover and simply continuing to cast.
