beginner.whenToUseIt: Upgrade from the first version whenever your gem tier allows, on any mana-hungry caster.

name: Clash
stats: Supported Skills deal 40% more Melee Damage against Enemies with a higher percentage of their Life remaining than you, but deal 20% less Melee Damage against Enemies with a lower percentage of their Life remaining than you
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills deal more Damage while you have a lower percentage of your Life remaining than the target struck, but less Damage when the reverse is true.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support that gives 40% more melee damage against enemies with a higher share of their life left than you, and 20% less against enemies with less.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays out exactly when you are hurt and the enemy is not, which is when you most need a fight to end quickly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character comfortable fighting at low life. If you stay topped up, the penalty is what you will see most often.

name: Close Combat I
stats: Supported Skills deal 20% more Attack Damage to enemies within 1 metre of you, scaling down to no bonus at 3.5 metres or further
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more damage to enemies based on how close they are to you.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support giving 20% more damage to enemies within a metre of you, fading to nothing at three and a half metres.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards standing in the enemy's face, which is where melee characters already are, so the bonus costs nothing to collect.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Excellent for melee. Almost worthless on a bow or crossbow build that fights from across the room.

name: Close Combat II
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Attack Damage to enemies within 1 metre of you, scaling down to no bonus at 3.5 metres or further
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more damage to enemies based on how close they are to you.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger proximity support, raising the point-blank bonus to 30% more attack damage over the same distance.
beginner.whyItMatters: The larger multiplier makes the risk of staying close worth taking even against enemies you would rather step away from.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to run once available on any committed melee build.

name: Cold Attunement
stats: Gain 25% of Damage as extra Cold Damage
Supported Skills deal 50% less Fire and Lightning Damage
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, causing them to Gain Cold Damage but deal less Fire and Lightning Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that adds a quarter of your damage again as cold damage while halving the fire and lightning damage the skill deals.
beginner.whyItMatters: Cold damage chills and freezes, so this converts raw damage into control as well as numbers.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build focused on cold. On a skill dealing all three elements it removes more than it adds.

name: Cold Exposure
stats: Supported Skills inflict Exposure for 8 seconds on Critical Hit with Cold Damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to inflict Exposure when it Critically Hits an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that applies cold exposure for eight seconds whenever the skill lands a critical hit with cold damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exposure lowers the target's cold resistance, so every cold hit you land afterwards is worth more than it was.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build with enough critical hit chance to apply it reliably. Without crits it will rarely trigger.

name: Cold Mastery
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Cold Skills
description: Supports Cold skills, granting them an additional level. Does not support skills which do not have levels.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants a cold skill one extra gem level.
beginner.whyItMatters: One level lifts the skill's whole stat line at once, which is usually a bigger gain than any single modifier you could add.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A dependable pick in any cold build once you can afford the tier. Skills without levels get nothing.

name: Cold Penetration
stats: Supported Skills Penetrate 30% Cold Resistance
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making those Hits Penetrate enemy Cold resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes the skill's hits ignore 30% of the enemy's cold resistance.
beginner.whyItMatters: Late-game monsters carry heavy resistances, and penetration is the direct answer to that rather than a way of piling on more damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Becomes important once you reach content where enemies resist cold. Early on, raw damage supports do more.

name: Combo Finisher I
stats: Supported Skills lose Combo if they generate no Combo for 4 seconds
Supported Skills deal 25% more Damage
Supported Skills require 3 Combo to use
description: Supports Melee Attacks you use yourself. Supported Skills cannot be used until enough Combo has been built up, but deal more damage. Cannot support skills which already Combo.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support that locks the skill until you have built three combo, then gives it 25% more damage. Combo is lost if you stop generating it for four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a normal attack into a finisher, forcing a build-up rhythm in exchange for a real damage multiplier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a second skill you save for the end of a combination. Attaching it to your main attack leaves you unable to open a fight.

name: Combo Finisher II
stats: Supported Skills lose Combo if they generate no Combo for 4 seconds
Supported Skills deal 40% more Damage
Supported Skills require 5 Combo to use
description: Supports Melee Attacks you use yourself. Supported Skills cannot be used until enough Combo has been built up, but deal massively more damage. Cannot support skills which already Combo.

beginner.whatItIs: The heavier combo finisher, demanding five combo before the skill can be used and giving 40% more damage in return.
beginner.whyItMatters: A steeper requirement for a much larger payout, which suits fights long enough to reach five combo before the target dies.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best against bosses. Against packs that die before you finish building, the earlier version is more usable.

name: Commandment
stats: Supported Minions have 100% increased Cooldown Recovery Rate for Command Skills
Supported Minions deal 100% less Damage with non-command Skills
description: Supports Minions which have Command Skills. Supported Minions have massively increased cooldown recovery speed for Command Skills they use, but deal no damage with non-Command Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support that doubles the cooldown recovery rate of your minions' command skills, but removes essentially all their damage from everything else they do.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes minions into command delivery systems rather than fighters, which is a total change of role rather than a tuning adjustment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when the command skill itself is your damage. If your minions kill things by attacking, this ruins them.

name: Commiserate
stats: When inflicting an Ailment with Supported Skill, remove that Ailment from yourself
Ailments inflicted by Supported Skills have 40% more Magnitude if you are afflicted with that Ailment when inflicting it
description: Supports Skills you use or Trigger yourself, which can cause Damaging Hits. Supported Skills inflict more powerful Ailments if you are afflicted with those Ailments when you inflict them, while also removing from you any Ailment that they inflict.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that strips an ailment off you when you inflict the same ailment on an enemy, and makes that ailment 40% stronger if you were suffering from it at the time.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns being ignited or chilled yourself from a straightforward problem into a temporary buff on your next hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character who regularly takes elemental ailments and has a skill that inflicts the same ones back.

name: Compressed Duration I
stats: Supported Skills have 30% less Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports any skill that has a duration making that duration shorter.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that shortens the skill's effect duration by 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shorter duration is a gain for skills that reapply as soon as the last one ends, because the whole cycle runs faster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a skill whose short duration is a benefit. On a buff or a lingering hazard, shortening it is a straight loss.

name: Compressed Duration II
stats: Supported Skills have 35% less Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports any skill that has a duration making that duration shorter.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger duration-shortening support, cutting effect duration by 35%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra reduction tightens the loop further on skills whose value comes from repeating rather than lasting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take on a build that is deliberately cycling a short-duration effect.

name: Concentrated Area
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Area Damage
Supported Skills have 50% less Area of Effect
description: Supports any skill with an area of effect, causing that area to be smaller but any area damage it deals to be higher.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that gives 30% more area damage while shrinking the area covered by half.
beginner.whyItMatters: It focuses an area skill onto a much smaller patch, which is what you want when everything you care about is standing in one place.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Strong on bosses and tight packs. Poor for clearing spread-out groups, where the missing area costs you more than the damage gains.

name: Concoct I
stats: Supported Skills consume 20% of your maximum Life Flask charges on use
Supported Skills have 3% more Magnitude of Bleeding they inflict per Life Flask charge consumed
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which Damage enemies with Hits. Supported Skills consume a percentage of your maximum Life Flask charges, inflicting more powerful Bleeding based on Life Flask charges consumed.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that burns a fifth of your life flask charges each use and makes the bleeding it inflicts stronger for every charge spent.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts flask charges, which do nothing while stored, into a bigger bleed on the enemy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a bleed build that kills fast enough to keep refilling life flask charges. Running the flask empty also removes your healing.

name: Concoct II
stats: Supported Skills consume 30% of your maximum Life Flask charges on use
Supported Skills have 3% more Magnitude of Bleeding they inflict per Life Flask charge consumed
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which Damage enemies with Hits. Supported Skills consume a percentage of your maximum Life Flask charges, inflicting more powerful Bleeding based on Life Flask charges consumed.

beginner.whatItIs: The heavier flask-burning bleed support, consuming 30% of your life flask charges per use for the same bonus per charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spending more charges each time means a larger bleed per swing, at the cost of emptying your healing flask sooner.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on a slow, heavy attack rather than something you swing constantly, or you will have no flask left when you need one.

name: Concussive Spells
stats: Supported Skills Daze on Critically Hitting enemies with Physical damage
description: Supports Spells which Hit enemies. Supported Skills Daze on Critically Hitting enemies with Physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support that dazes enemies whenever the spell lands a critical hit with physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Daze interrupts what a monster was about to do, so this adds defence to a spell that was only dealing damage before.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical caster with reasonable critical hit chance who wants to break up dangerous enemy attacks.

name: Considered Casting
stats: Supported Spell Skills have 15% less Cast Speed
Supported Spells deal 35% more Damage
description: Supports Spell Skills that Hit Enemies and you cast yourself, boosting Damage at the cost of Cast Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support giving 35% more damage in exchange for 15% less cast speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: The trade is favourable on paper, but slower casting also means more time standing still, which is its own risk.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on a spell you cast a few times per fight. Avoid it on a spell whose value is how quickly it repeats.

name: Controlled Destruction
stats: Supported Spells deal 25% more Hit Damage
Supported Skills cannot deal Critical Hits
description: Supports Spells that Hit enemies, boosting their damage but preventing them from dealing Critical Hits.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support giving 25% more hit damage while preventing the spell from ever landing a critical hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a clean gain for a build that has no critical hit investment, and a large loss for one that does.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Check your critical hit chance first. On a low-crit caster it is one of the simplest damage increases available.

name: Controlled Hazard
stats: Hazards cannot be triggered for 3 seconds after being created
description: Supports Skills which create Hazards, causing those Hazards to be unable to be triggered for 3 seconds after being created.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops hazards you create from being triggered for the first three seconds after they appear.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stops a hazard being set off by the first monster to wander in, so it is still there when the pack you actually wanted arrives.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For deliberately placing hazards ahead of a fight. It works against you when you need something to go off immediately.

name: Cool Headed
stats: 50% less Ignite duration on you while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing Ignite applied to you to last for a shorter duration while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs that halves how long ignites last on you while the buff is running.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being ignited is damage that keeps ticking after you have escaped the danger, and cutting the duration cuts that damage directly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth a slot in areas full of fire damage. Elsewhere it is a slot spent on a problem you do not have.

name: Cooldown Recovery I
stats: Supported Skills have 25% increased cooldown recovery rate
description: Supports skills with Cooldowns, increasing the rate at which those Cooldowns Recover. Cannot modify the skills of minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes the skill's cooldown recover 25% faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: For a skill whose only limit is how often you may use it, this is a direct increase to how much of it you get.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it into a strong skill with a long cooldown. It does nothing for a skill you can use freely.

name: Cooldown Recovery II
stats: Supported Skills have 30% increased cooldown recovery rate
description: Supports skills with Cooldowns, increasing the rate at which those Cooldowns Recover. Cannot modify the skills of minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger cooldown support, recovering cooldowns 30% faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: The additional recovery adds up across a long fight into several extra uses of an important skill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take once your gem tier allows, on the same cooldown-limited skills.

name: Corpse Conservation
stats: Corpses consumed by Supported Skills have 25% chance to not be destroyed
description: Supports skills that consume Corpses, giving them a chance to take effect without destroying the Corpse.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving corpses consumed by the skill a 25% chance to survive being used.
beginner.whyItMatters: Corpses are a limited resource in the middle of a fight, and a quarter of them coming back means fewer moments where the skill is unusable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that leans on corpse consumption. It is dead weight on anything that never touches a corpse.

name: Corrosion
stats: Poison applied by supported Skills also
Breaks Armour equal to 80% of Poison damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing Poison it applies to also Break enemy Armour. Cannot support skills that Consume Fully Broken Armour.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes poison the skill applies also break armour, worth 80% of the poison damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a chaos build a way to strip armour, which is normally a job for physical damage only.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison build fighting armoured enemies. Skip it if you are already breaking armour by hitting hard.

name: Corrupting Cry I
stats: Support
Supported Warcries have 30% less Area of Effect
Supported Skills Trigger Corrupted Cry for each enemy in range
Corrupted Cry
Level: This skill will copy the Level of the Gem it is Socketed in
Cost: 0 Mana
Covers the target in Corrupted Blood which damages them.
Corrupted Blood duration is 5 seconds.
Corrupted Blood deals (5.9-287) Physical damage per second
description: Supports Warcries, Triggering Corrupted Cry to inflict Corrupted Blood on enemies in their area of effect.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support that triggers a corrupted cry on every enemy in range, covering them in corrupted blood that deals physical damage over time. The warcry itself covers 30% less area.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a warcry from a pure buff into a source of damage on the whole pack you shouted at.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a warcry build that opens fights by shouting into a group. The smaller area means you need to be closer than usual.

name: Corrupting Cry II
stats: Support
Supported Skills Trigger Corrupted Cry for each enemy in range
Corrupted Cry
Level: This skill will copy the Level of the Gem it is Socketed in
Cost: 0 Mana
Covers the target in Corrupted Blood which damages them.
Corrupted Blood duration is 5 seconds.
Corrupted Blood deals (5.9-287) Physical damage per second
description: Supports Warcries, Triggering Corrupted Cry to inflict Corrupted Blood on enemies in their area of effect.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded corrupted cry support, applying the same corrupted blood without the area penalty.
beginner.whyItMatters: You keep the warcry's full reach and still get the damage, which removes the only reason to hesitate over the first version.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it in place of the area-penalised version on any warcry build.

name: Coursing Current
stats: Trigger Coursing Current when a Hit from Supported Skills Shocks
description: Supports Skills which Hit enemies. Shocking an enemy with Supported Skills Triggers Coursing Current, which sends Chaining Lightning Projectiles to nearby Drenched enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that triggers coursing current whenever the skill shocks something, sending chaining lightning projectiles at nearby drenched enemies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards combining water and lightning, which is a pairing many builds set up and then get nothing extra from.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when you have a way to drench enemies. Without water in the build the projectiles have nothing to seek out.

name: Crackling Barrier
stats: Gain 15% of your maximum Mana as Lightning Thorns Damage while Channelling Supported Skills
description: Supports Channelling Skills. While Channelling Supported Skills, you gain Lightning Thorns based off of your maximum Mana.

beginner.whatItIs: A channelling support that grants lightning thorns worth 15% of your maximum mana while you are channelling.
beginner.whyItMatters: Channelling normally means standing still and taking hits; this makes those incoming hits damage the attacker instead.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a large-mana caster who channels through packs. On a low-mana character the thorns damage is small.

name: Crater
stats: Supported Skills create 3 Fissures on landing
Fissures
Creates multiple Fissures when landing with Supported Skill.
Converts 80% of Physical Damage to Fire Damage
Attack Damage of this skill is 35% of Default Attack Damage
Fissure length is 1.5 metres
Fissure duration is 6 seconds
Limit 9 Fissures allowed
description: Supports Melee Skills that leap into the air, causing them to create Fissures when you land. Cannot Support Totem Skills, and does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support for leaping skills that creates three fire fissures where you land, up to nine at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: Landing from a leap is normally just movement, and this turns every landing into an area attack on the ground you chose.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that uses a leap skill to close distance regularly rather than as an occasional escape.

name: Crazed Minions
stats: Supported Minions deal 30% more Damage if they have Revived Recently
description: Supports Minion Skills which summon Reviving Minions. Supported Minions deal significantly more Damage if they have Revived Recently.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for reviving minions, giving them 30% more damage for a while after they come back.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards the moment your minions are usually at their weakest, so a wipe in the middle of a fight becomes a spike instead.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For minion builds whose minions revive rather than needing to be resummoned by hand.

name: Creeping Chill
stats: Consume a Power Charge to Trigger Creeping Chill on an Ice Crystal created by Supported Skills
description: Supports any Skill that creates Ice Crystals, causing that Skill to Consume a Power Charge if possible to create Chilled Ground around the Crystal.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for ice crystal skills. Each crystal consumes a power charge, if you have one, to lay chilled ground around itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chilled ground slows everything standing on it, so it converts spare power charges into crowd control.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build that generates power charges faster than it spends them elsewhere.

name: Crescendo I
stats: Final Strike of Supported Skills can be performed twice in succession
description: Supports Strikes that perform a Final Strike at the end of a combination of attacks, allowing you to use the Final Strike twice in succession.

beginner.whatItIs: A strike support that lets you perform the final strike of a combination twice in a row.
beginner.whyItMatters: The final strike is the strongest part of the sequence, so repeating it changes the shape of your damage without extra setup.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any melee build that runs a strike combination to its end rather than cancelling out of it.

name: Crescendo II
stats: Final Strike of Supported Skills can be performed twice in succession
Attacks with Supported Skills that are not Final Strikes have 15% more Attack Speed
description: Supports Strikes that perform a Final Strike at the end of a combination of attacks, allowing you to use the Final Strike twice in succession, and causing Non-Final Strike Attacks to be faster.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded combination support: the final strike still repeats, and every non-final attack in the sequence swings 15% faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster build-up means you reach the repeated finisher sooner, so the whole combination cycles more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A straight upgrade over the first version for any strike-combination build.

name: Crescendo III
stats: Final Strike of Supported Skill is Ancestrally Boosted
description: Supports Strikes that perform a Final Strike at the end of a combination of attacks, causing the Final Strike to be Ancestrally Boosted.

beginner.whatItIs: The final combination support. Instead of repeating the final strike, it makes that final strike ancestrally boosted.
beginner.whyItMatters: One boosted strike can land harder than two ordinary ones, which suits fights where a single big hit matters more than volume.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it over the repeating versions for boss damage; keep an earlier one for clearing packs.

name: Crystalline Shards
stats: Supported Skills cannot Extract Impale
Ice Crystals created by Supported Skills can Impale with Cold Damage as though it was Physical
Ice Crystals created by Supported Skills have 100% chance to Impale
description: Supports Skills which create Ice Crystals. Damaging Explosions caused by Ice Crystals from Supported Skills will Impale Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for ice crystal skills. Crystal explosions always impale, treating their cold damage as though it were physical, and the skill can no longer extract impale.
beginner.whyItMatters: Impale normally belongs to physical builds, and this hands a cold build access to it through the crystals it was already making.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build with ice crystals in it. The lost ability to extract impale only matters if you were doing that already.

name: Culling Strike I
stats: Supported Skills have Culling Strike against Rare or Unique Enemies
description: Supports Attack Skills, causing them to Cull Rare and Unique Enemies on Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that finishes off rare and unique enemies once a hit drops them below the culling threshold.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the last sliver of a tough monster's health bar, which is often the most dangerous stretch of a boss fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Valuable against bosses and rares. It does nothing for clearing ordinary monsters, which die outright anyway.

name: Culling Strike II
stats: Supported Skills have Culling Strike against Rare or Unique Enemies
Gain 20% increased Culling Strike Threshold for 20 seconds on Culling with Supported Skills
description: Supports Attack Skills, causing them to Cull Rare and Unique Enemies on Hit, and increasing the threshold at which they will Cull Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded culling support, which also raises your culling threshold by 20% for twenty seconds each time it triggers.
beginner.whyItMatters: The rising threshold means each cull makes the next one easier, so a room full of rares gets progressively faster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it in content dense with rare and unique enemies, where the rising threshold compounds.

name: Culmination I
stats: Supported Skills can gain up to 10 Combo
Supported Skills expend all Combo on use
Supported Skills lose Combo if they generate no Combo for 4 seconds
Supported Skills deal 3% more Damage per Combo expended
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills gain Combo when you successfully Strike Enemies with other Melee Attacks. Supported Skills reset their Combo on use, dealing more Damage the higher Combo you had on use. Cannot support skills which already gain Combo. Cannot modify the Skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support that builds combo from your other melee strikes, up to ten, then spends it all on use for 3% more damage per point.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns your ordinary attacks into charging time for one heavy blow, without needing a skill that generates combo itself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a two-skill melee rhythm where one attack sets up and the other cashes in. Combo drains if you stop striking for four seconds.

name: Culmination II
stats: Supported Skills can gain up to 10 Combo
Supported Skills expend all Combo on use
Supported Skills lose Combo if they generate no Combo for 6 seconds
Supported Skills deal 4% more Damage per Combo expended
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills gain Combo when you successfully Strike Enemies with other Melee Attacks. Supported Skills reset their Combo on use, dealing more Damage the higher Combo you had on use. Cannot support skills which already gain Combo. Cannot modify the Skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger combo-spending support, giving 4% more damage per combo point and allowing six seconds between strikes before combo drains.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer grace period means repositioning mid-fight no longer throws away everything you built up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take once available, particularly in fights where you have to move between exchanges.

name: Cursed Ground
stats: Supported Skills create Cursed Ground
Enemies on the Cursed Ground from a Supported Skill are Cursed while within it
Limit 2 areas of Cursed Ground
description: Supports Curse Skills. Supported Curse Skills create areas which Curse Enemies so long as they are within them.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support that lays down cursed ground, cursing any enemy standing in it, with up to two patches at a time.
beginner.whyItMatters: A curse that lives on the floor keeps working on everything that walks through, rather than expiring on one target.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best at a chokepoint or a doorway a pack must cross. Weaker against enemies that stay at range and never step in.

name: Danse Macabre
stats: Supported Offering Skills have 30% increased Buff effect
Supported Offering Skills target an additional skeletal Minion
Support Effects are only applied if an additional skeletal Minion is targeted
Supported Offering Skills deal 30% more Damage
description: Supports Offering Skills. Supported Skills have increased Buff effect and deal more damage, but will target an additional skeletal Minion when cast. If there is not an additional skeletal Minion to target, no damage or Buff effect will be granted.

beginner.whatItIs: An offering support giving 30% increased buff effect and 30% more damage, but the offering must target an extra skeletal minion. With no second skeleton, none of the bonus applies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a large boost with a hard requirement attached, so it either doubles down on a skeleton build or does nothing at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when you reliably have several skeletons up. On a thin minion count it silently gives you nothing.

name: Daresso's Passion
stats: Supported Skills require 50% less Glory to use
description: Supports Banner Skills, causing them to require significantly less Glory to use.
flavourText:
"I raised my eyes to look upon my death. Instead, I saw her.
Merveil. Fighting had always been about survival. Now the
fight became about something much greater... love."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage banner support that halves the glory a banner skill needs before you can use it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Glory is what gates banner skills, so cutting the requirement means the banner is available in far more fights.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any banner build where waiting to accumulate glory is what stops you using the skill.

name: Dauntless
stats: Supported Skills cannot be used unless you have been stationary for 1.5 seconds
This timer resets when you move
Supported Skills deal 3% more Damage with Hits for each quarter second you have been stationary, up to 45%
This Damage bonus resets when you move
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which can cause Damaging Hits. Supported Skills cannot be used unless you have been stationary for a certain duration, but deal increasingly more damage the longer you are stationary. Cannot support Skills which have a cooldown or another usage Condition.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that locks the skill until you have stood still for a second and a half, then gives 3% more hit damage for every quarter second you stay put, up to 45%. Moving resets everything.
beginner.whyItMatters: It offers a very large multiplier to a playstyle most characters cannot afford, since standing still is how you get hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a tanky build that holds its ground. On a character that survives by moving, the skill will often be unusable.

name: Deadly Herald
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage
description: Supports Herald Skills, making their triggered effects deal more damage at the expense of higher Spirit cost.

beginner.whatItIs: A herald support that makes the herald's triggered effect deal 30% more damage, at the cost of a higher spirit reservation.
beginner.whyItMatters: Heralds fire constantly as you clear, so a flat damage increase on them is a large share of your clearing speed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only if you have spirit to spare. If you are already reserving everything, something else has to come off first.

name: Deadly Poison I
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% less Damage with Hits
75% more Magnitude of Poison inflicted with Supported Skills
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal less damage but inflict more potent Poison.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that cuts the skill's hit damage by a quarter and makes the poison it applies 75% stronger.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shifts damage out of the moment of the hit and into the poison afterwards, which is the whole point of a poison build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when poison is your main damage. On a hit-based build you are giving away the damage you actually use.

name: Deadly Poison II
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% less Damage with Hits
100% more Magnitude of Poison inflicted with Supported Skills
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal less damage but inflict more potent Poison.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger poison support, doubling poison magnitude while cutting hit damage by 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The trade gets better the further you have committed to poison, since the hit damage you are losing matters less.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to run once poison is doing nearly all your damage.

name: Deadly Resolve
stats: Can Trigger Deadly Resolve once every 0.3 seconds
Stage duration is 10 seconds
Gain a stage every 1 second
3 maximum stages
description: Supports Channelling Skills you use yourself. While Channelling Supported Skills, periodically gain stages of Deadly Resolve. Expend a stage of Deadly Resolve when an enemy Hits you to Trigger a deadly slash towards that enemy, dealing more damage based on your Armour.

beginner.whatItIs: A channelling support that builds up to three stages while you channel. When an enemy hits you, it spends a stage to slash back at them, dealing damage based on your armour.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns being attacked mid-channel from a pure interruption into a counterattack, and scales that counterattack off a defensive stat.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavily armoured character who channels in melee. On a light, evasive build the counterattack hits for very little.

name: Deathmarch
stats: Minions from Supported Skills heal Allied Minions within 3 metres for 25% of Supported Minions' life on death, as well as removing all Ailments from those Minions
description: Supports Skills which create Persistent Minions. Supported Minions will restore Life to nearby Allied Minions on death, as well as removing Ailments from those Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent minions. When one dies, nearby allied minions are healed for a quarter of that minion's life and have their ailments removed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stops one minion death cascading into all of them, which is how minion armies usually collapse in a hard fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build fielding several minions that stand close together. It gives nothing to a single companion.

name: Decaying Hex
stats: Support
Supported Skills trigger Profane Decay on each target Cursed
Profane Decay
Level: (1-20)
This Skill will copy the Level of the Gem it is Socketed in
Cost: 0 Mana
Cast Time: 1.00 sec
Inflicts Decay on the target, dealing Chaos Damage over time
Decay deals (5.9-287) Chaos damage per second
Decay duration is 8 seconds
description: Supports Curse skills. Supported skill Trigger Profane Decay on each target they curse to inflict a damaging Debuff.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support that also inflicts profane decay on each target you curse, dealing chaos damage over eight seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Curses are usually pure setup, and this makes every application also a source of damage in its own right.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse build that wants its curses to kill as well as weaken, especially when you curse whole packs.

name: Deep Cuts I
stats: 75% more Magnitude of Bleeding inflicted with Supported Skills
Supported Skills deal 25% less Damage with Hits
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal less damage but inflict more potent Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that reduces hit damage by a quarter and makes bleeding you inflict 75% stronger.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the bleed equivalent of trading the swing for the wound, moving damage into an effect that keeps working after you move on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build where bleeding is the main damage. It is a loss on any build that kills with the hit itself.

name: Deep Cuts II
stats: 100% more Magnitude of Bleeding inflicted with Supported Skills
Supported Skills deal 30% less Damage with Hits
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal less damage but inflict more potent Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger bleed support, doubling bleed magnitude for a 30% cut to hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Doubling the bleed is a large step up for a build whose kills come from the bleed rather than the strike.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for a committed bleed character whose kills come from the wound rather than the swing.

name: Deep Freeze
stats: Supported Skills have 50% increased Freeze Duration on Enemies
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing Freeze it inflicts to last longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes freezes the skill causes last 50% longer.
beginner.whyItMatters: A frozen enemy is not attacking, so longer freezes are extra safety rather than extra damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build that freezes to survive. It gives nothing if your freezes are being consumed by another skill immediately.

name: Defy I
stats: Attack Damage with Hits with Supported Skills is Lucky while you are Surrounded
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself. Hit Damage from Supported Skills is Lucky if you are Surrounded.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that makes your hit damage lucky while you are surrounded, meaning the game rolls the damage twice and keeps the better result.
beginner.whyItMatters: It smooths out low damage rolls precisely when you are in the most danger, which makes surrounded fights less swingy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a melee character who wades into packs. If you fight one enemy at a time, the condition is never met.

name: Defy II
stats: Attack Damage with Hits with Supported Skills is Lucky while you are Surrounded
Insufficient Mana doesn't prevent the use of Supported Skills while Surrounded
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself. Hit Damage from Supported Skills is Lucky and Insufficient Mana doesn't prevent Supported Skills from being used if you are Surrounded.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded surrounded support: hit damage is still lucky, and while surrounded you can use the skill even without enough mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: Running out of mana in the middle of a pack is a common way to die, and this removes that failure exactly when it would happen.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Prefer it on any melee build that fights inside groups, where running dry on mana is the real risk.

name: Delayed Gratification
stats: Supported Conditional Skills can be used an additional time within 10 seconds of using them after meeting their requirements
Conditional requirements of Supported Skills are 150% harder to meet
description: Supports Skills which require some Condition to be met for use. Supported Skills can be used an additional time after their Condition has been met, but meeting that Condition is harder.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for conditional skills. Once you meet the condition you may use the skill an extra time within ten seconds, but the condition itself becomes 150% harder to meet.
beginner.whyItMatters: It concentrates a conditional skill into bursts of two uses spaced further apart, rather than a steady drip.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good when two quick uses back to back is what wins a fight. Bad when you need the skill available at all times.

name: Delayed Reaction
stats: Hazards created by Supported Skills cannot be triggered by enemies unless triggered immediately on creation
Hazards created by Supported Skills trigger at the end of their duration
Hazards created by Supported Skills deal 15% more Damage
Hazards created by Supported Skills have 70% less duration
description: Supports Skills which create Hazards, causing those Hazards to only be able to trigger immediately after creation or at the end of their duration. Created Hazards have significantly lowered duration, and deal more damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A hazard support. Hazards can only go off immediately on creation or at the very end of their life, they deal 15% more damage, and they last 70% less time.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a slow area-denial hazard into something closer to a delayed bomb, with a predictable moment of detonation.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For using hazards as damage rather than as a barrier. It removes their value as ground you are keeping enemies off.

name: Deliberation
stats: Supported Skills deal 20% more Damage
30% more Movement Speed penalty while using Supported Skills
description: Supports skills that can be used while moving, causing you to move slower while using them, but granting more damage in exchange.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for skills usable while moving. You move considerably slower while using them, and they deal 20% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The point of a moving skill is usually the movement, so this asks whether you would rather keep the mobility or the damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Reasonable on a durable character. Poor for a fragile one that relies on staying out of the way while attacking.

name: Derange
stats: Supported Skills gain an Energy Shield cost equal to your Intelligence
Supported Skills deal 8% more non-Ailment Damage over time per 100 Intelligence
description: Supports Skills which you use yourself which can deal damage. Supported Skills gain an Energy Shield cost equal to your Intelligence, while also dealing more non-Ailment Damage over time based off of your Intelligence. Cannot support Channelling Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that adds an energy shield cost equal to your intelligence, and gives 8% more non-ailment damage over time for every hundred intelligence you have.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a stat you may have stacked for other reasons directly into damage, paid for out of your shield rather than your mana.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-intelligence character with a large energy shield. On a low-intelligence build it costs more than it gives.

name: Dialla's Desire
stats: +5% to Quality of Supported Skills
+1 to Level of Supported Skill Gems
description: Supports any Skill which has levels, increasing the level and Quality, while reducing the cost and Reservation.
flavourText:
"I will become your Gemling Queen, my love, but not
with such dull stones. I want to give myself to you
for eternity. Surely we can seek perfection together?"

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that raises the supported gem by one level and 5% quality.
beginner.whyItMatters: Level and quality both lift the entire skill at once, which is a broad improvement rather than a narrow one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A safe slot in almost any build, on whichever skill you want to be strongest. Skills without levels get nothing.

name: Direstrike I
stats: Deal 50% increased Attack Damage while on Low Life while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to deal increased Attack Damage while on Low Life while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs that gives 50% increased attack damage while you are on low life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes the most dangerous part of a fight also the strongest, which suits builds that deliberately sit at low life.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only if your character can survive at low life on purpose. Otherwise the bonus is only up when you are about to die.

name: Direstrike II
stats: Deal 70% increased Attack Damage while on Low Life while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to deal increased Attack Damage while on Low Life while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger low-life support, giving 70% increased attack damage while the persistent buff is active and you are on low life.
beginner.whyItMatters: The larger bonus makes low life a genuine build plan rather than an accident you occasionally profit from.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to take once you have the recovery or defences to hold yourself at low life safely.

name: Doedre's Undoing
stats: Support
Supported Skills create Cursed Ground
Enemies on the Cursed Ground from a Supported Skill are Cursed while within it

Limit 2 areas of Cursed Ground
Dark Consequences

flavourText:
"Let the meat show us the way. Hail the meat, praise the
meat. The meat is both debasement and divinity alike. The
meat shall lead us down the path to true enlightenment."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage curse support that lays down cursed ground and spawns witchtoads in it. The toads leap at nearby enemies, preferring cursed ones, and explode for chaos damage on impact.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a curse into an active, self-driving source of damage rather than a debuff you apply and forget.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a chaos curse build fighting packs that come to you, since the toads need enemies to leap at.

name: Dominus' Grasp
stats: Supported Skills Chain 100% more times
description: Supports Projectile skills and any other skills that Chain, causing them to Chain more times.
flavourText:
The High Templar needed thousands of prisoners if his and
Piety's experiments were to succeed. Conspiring on the
matter, they decided to revive an age old tradition... exile.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that doubles the number of times a projectile or chaining skill chains, with no damage penalty attached.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaining supports normally charge you damage for extra bounces; this one does not, which changes what it is worth.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any chaining clear skill. It is still weak against a single boss, where the extra chains find no targets.

name: Double Barrel I
stats: Supported Skills have 30% less Reload Speed
Supported Skills load an additional bolt
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, causing them to load an extra bolt at the cost of reload speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A crossbow support that loads one extra bolt per magazine, at the cost of 30% reload speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: More bolts per magazine means fewer reloads, but each reload takes longer, so it only wins if you fire out the whole magazine.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a crossbow skill you empty into a fight. Poor if you reload after a couple of shots anyway.

name: Double Barrel II
stats: Supported Skills have 20% less Reload Speed
Supported Skills load an additional bolt
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, causing them to load an extra bolt at the cost of reload speed.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved extra-bolt support, with the reload penalty reduced from 30% to 20%.
beginner.whyItMatters: A smaller penalty makes the extra bolt closer to free, which is what turns this from a trade into an upgrade.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it in place of the heavier-penalty version once your gem tier reaches it.

name: Double Barrel III
stats: Supported Skills reload automatically when Heavy Stunning an enemy with them
Supported Skills have 20% less Reload Speed
Supported Skills load an additional bolt
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, causing them to load an extra bolt at the cost of reload speed. Supported Skills will also automatically reload when they Heavy Stun an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: The final extra-bolt support: an extra bolt, the same 20% reload penalty, and an automatic reload whenever the skill heavy stuns an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: The free reload on a heavy stun offsets the slower reload speed, so the drawback rarely gets paid.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for a heavy crossbow skill that stuns. On a light skill that never heavy stuns, the simpler version is fine.

name: Drain Ailments
stats: Supported Skills Consume all Ailments of a random type on the target when inflicting damage over time Debuffs, causing the Debuff to deal 35% more damage if any Ailments were consumed
description: Supports Spells that deal non-Ailment damage over time, causing them to consume Ailments on enemies it applies damage over time Debuffs to in order to deal substantially more damage over time.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for damage-over-time spells. When the spell applies its debuff, it consumes all ailments of one random type on the target, and the debuff deals 35% more damage if it consumed anything.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts ailments you have stacked into a stronger lingering effect, which is a way to spend control you no longer need.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that reliably inflicts ailments and then applies a damage-over-time spell on top.

name: Durability
stats: Objects created by Supported Skills can be Hit +2 times
description: Supports Skills which create objects that are destroyed after being Hit a number of times, allowing for them to last for additional Hits. Does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that lets objects the skill creates survive two more hits before being destroyed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Walls, totems and similar objects usually die to the first thing that attacks them, and two extra hits can double how long they help.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that relies on a created object staying up. It does nothing for skills that make no objects.

name: Echoing Cry
stats: Supported Skills become usable after you have moved 10 metres
Supported Skills become unusable again after use
Supported Skills have 50% less Area of Effect
Supported Skills deal 40% less Damage
Supported Skills count enemies as having 50% less Power
Supported Skills Echo 2 times, with a 1.3 second delay
Supported Skills have 100% more area of effect per time they have Echoed
description: Supports Warcries. Supported Skills Echo twice, and their area grows larger each time, but are less effective and require you to have travelled a certain distance before use.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support that makes the warcry echo twice with a growing area, but it deals 40% less damage, covers half the area at first, counts enemies as much weaker, and requires you to have moved ten metres before use.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a moving, roaming playstyle with a warcry that expands outward over several seconds instead of firing once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing while on the move. Against a stationary boss fight the movement requirement makes it awkward to use.

name: Efficiency I
stats: Supported Skills have 30% less Cost
description: Supports any skill, making it cost less to use. Cannot support skills which reserve Spirit.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes the skill cost 30% less to use.
beginner.whyItMatters: A cheaper skill is one you can use more often, which is frequently a larger real gain than a damage support on a skill you cannot afford to cast.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Very good while levelling, or on any expensive skill you find yourself rationing. It does not work on skills reserving spirit.

name: Efficiency II
stats: Supported Skills have 40% less Cost
description: Supports any skill, making it cost less to use. Cannot support skills which reserve Spirit.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger cost-reduction support, cutting the skill's cost by 40%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The deeper discount can take an unaffordable skill and make it your main attack.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take on a costly skill once your gem tier allows.

name: Einhar's Beastrite
stats: Supported Skills can only Damage Low Life Enemies
Killing Blows from Supported Strike Skills against Rare monsters grant two of their Modifiers for 300 seconds
description: Supports Melee Strike skills, causing them to steal a Modifier from Rare monsters they kill for a lengthy duration, while being unable to damage enemies not on low Life. Does not modify skills used by Minions.
flavourText:
"You must cut the beast, like this," he told the wide-eyed
and forgetful woman. "The juiciest parts are in the middle!"
She nodded, and began relearning the way of the wilds.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage strike support. Killing a rare monster steals two of its modifiers for a full five minutes, but the skill can only damage enemies that are already on low life.
beginner.whyItMatters: The stolen modifiers last long enough to carry across a whole area, at the price of needing a second skill to bring things down first.
beginner.whenToUseIt: As a dedicated finishing skill in a two-skill setup. It cannot function as your only attack.

name: Electrocute
stats: Supported Skills Cannot inflict Shock
Lightning Damage from Supported Skills Contributes to Electrocution Buildup
description: Supports any Skill which can deal Damage. Lightning Damage from Supported Skills can inflict Electrocute, but Supported Skills cannot inflict Shock.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that lets the skill's lightning damage build electrocution, but stops it inflicting shock.
beginner.whyItMatters: Electrocute and shock do different jobs, and this locks the skill into the heavier one that stuns rather than the one that amplifies damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that wants enemies disabled. Skip it if you rely on shock to make everything else hit harder.

name: Electromagnetism
stats: On Shocking an enemy where there are at least 3
Shocked enemies within 4 metres that are not already in a Shocking Rift, Supported Skills Consume Shock of all enemies within 4 metres to trigger Shocking Rift
description: Supports Skills that Hit enemies. When Supported Skills Shock an enemy that is nearby other Shocked enemies, trigger Electromagnetism, sucking in nearby enemies, Hindering them, and dealing Lightning damage at an interval.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that watches for a cluster of shocked enemies. Shock a target with at least three other shocked enemies within four metres and it consumes their shocks to pull them together, hinder them and deal lightning damage over time.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gathers a scattered pack into one spot, which makes every area skill you follow up with far more effective.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build clearing dense packs. Against a lone enemy the condition can never be met.

name: Elemental Armament I
stats: Supported Skills deal 20% more Elemental Attack damage
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more Elemental damage.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support giving 20% more elemental attack damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a plain increase with no drawback, which makes it an easy first pick while you learn what the rest of your build wants.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Any attack build whose damage is fire, cold or lightning. It does nothing for a pure physical attack.

name: Elemental Armament II
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% more Elemental Attack damage
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more Elemental damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version of the same support, giving 25% more elemental attack damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Still no drawback, just a larger number, which keeps it one of the least demanding supports to slot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it wherever the first version sat. Fire, cold and lightning attacks all qualify equally.

name: Elemental Armament III
stats: Supported Skills cannot inflict Elemental Ailments
Supported Skills deal 12% more Attack Damage for each Elemental Ailment on Enemies they Hit
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more Damage for each Elemental Ailment on Enemies they Hit. Supported Skills cannot themselves inflict Elemental Ailments.

beginner.whatItIs: The payoff version: 12% more attack damage for each elemental ailment on the enemy, but the skill can no longer inflict elemental ailments itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: With ignite, chill and shock all on a target this beats the flat versions comfortably, but it needs another skill to apply them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only in a build that already covers all three ailments elsewhere. As your only elemental skill, it removes its own condition.

name: Elemental Army
stats: Minions from Supported Skills have +30% to all Elemental Resistances
description: Supports skills which create Minions, bolstering the Elemental Resistances of those Minions. Cannot support skills which create undamageable Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support granting your minions 30% to all elemental resistances.
beginner.whyItMatters: Minions usually die to elemental damage first, so this addresses the actual reason a minion army falls apart in maps.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any minion build heading into content with heavy elemental damage.

name: Elemental Discharge
stats: Support
Supported Skills Cannot inflict Freeze, Shock or Ignite
Supported Skills Consume Freeze, Shock and Ignite on hit to trigger Elemental Discharge
Elemental Discharge
Cooldown Time: 1.00s
Cast Time: 1.00s
Critical Hit Chance: 10.00%
Consuming Freeze deals 80% to 120% of your Intelligence as Cold Damage
Consuming Ignite deals 40% to 60% of your Intelligence as Fire Damage
Consuming Shock deals 1% to 120% of your Intelligence as Lightning Damage
Discharge radius is 2 metres
description: Supports any Spell that Hits enemies, causing it to consume Elemental Ailments on hit to trigger an Elemental Discharge. Cannot support the skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support that stops the spell inflicting freeze, shock or ignite, and instead consumes those ailments on hit to trigger an elemental discharge scaled off your intelligence.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts ailments into an immediate burst, which is a way of getting damage now instead of over time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when another skill applies the ailments. On your only elemental spell it removes the ailments it needs to consume.

name: Elemental Focus
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% more Elemental Damage
Supported Skills cannot inflict Elemental Ailments
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal more Elemental Damage but be unable to inflict Elemental Ailments.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 25% more elemental damage, with the skill no longer able to inflict elemental ailments.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a clean gain if the skill was never going to ignite, chill or shock anything useful, and a real loss if your build wanted those ailments.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good on a hit-focused elemental skill. Keep it away from any skill whose job is applying ailments for something else to consume.

name: Embitter
stats: If Supported Skills would gain extra Damage of any Type other than Cold, they gain extra Cold Damage instead
description: Supports Skills which can Damage Enemies with Hits, causing all sources of Damage Gained to instead be treated as Damage Gained as extra Cold for Supported Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that redirects every source of gained extra damage into cold damage instead.
beginner.whyItMatters: Builds often collect gained damage of several types from gear and passives, and this funnels all of it into one element you can then scale.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build with scattered sources of gained damage. It does nothing if you gain no extra damage at all.

name: Empowered Sparks I
description: Supports Skills which generate Charges. When generating Power Charge with Supported Skills, Empower some of your Attacks to Trigger Spark Projectiles on use.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for charge-generating skills. Generating a power charge empowers some of your attacks so they trigger spark projectiles when used.
beginner.whyItMatters: It attaches a free source of lightning projectiles to something you were doing anyway, which is damage without a button.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that generates power charges frequently. If charges come slowly, the sparks rarely appear.

name: Empowered Sparks II
description: Supports Skills which generate Charges. When generating Power Charge with Supported Skills, Empower some of your Attacks to Trigger Spark Projectiles on use.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version of the spark support, empowering your attacks more readily when the supported skill makes a power charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: More empowered attacks means a steadier stream of sparks rather than an occasional one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take once your gem tier allows, in the same power-charge builds.

name: Encroaching Ground
stats: Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills gain 20% increased Area of Effect per second, up to a maximum of 100%
description: Supports Skills that create Ground Surfaces, causing those Surfaces to grow over time, up to a limit.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes ground surfaces you create grow by 20% each second, up to twice their starting size.
beginner.whyItMatters: A surface that spreads eventually covers a whole room, so it catches enemies who thought they were standing clear of it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best when a fight stays in one place long enough for the growth to happen. It gives nothing to a surface you leave behind immediately.

name: Enduring Impact I
stats: 30% chance to gain an Endurance Charge when Heavily Stunning a non-Unique Enemy with Supported Skills
Gain 1 Endurance Charge on Heavily Stunning a Unique Enemy with Supported Skill
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to gain an Endurance Charge when causing a Heavy Stun.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving a 30% chance at an endurance charge when you heavy stun an ordinary monster, and a guaranteed charge when you heavy stun a unique one.
beginner.whyItMatters: Endurance charges reduce the damage you take, so this makes staggering enemies into a defensive gain as well as a control one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy, slow attack that stuns. On a fast light attack that never heavy stuns, it will not fire.

name: Enduring Impact II
stats: 30% chance to gain an Endurance Charge when Heavily Stunning a non-Unique Enemy with Supported Skills
Gain 3 Endurance Charges on Heavily Stunning a Unique Enemy with Supported Skill
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to gain an Endurance Charge when causing a Heavy Stun.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving three endurance charges at once for heavy stunning a unique enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Three charges from one stun can fill your allowance in a single hit, which matters most at the start of a boss fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The upgrade to take for a stun build that spends time fighting bosses and unique monsters.

name: Energy Capacitor
stats: Supported Meta Gems have 80% increased Maximum Energy
description: Supports Invocation Skills which Trigger other Skills. Supported Skills have significantly higher Maximum Energy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for invocation skills that raises the maximum energy a meta gem can hold by 80%.
beginner.whyItMatters: A bigger energy pool means the triggered skill can be saved up for and released in a bigger burst rather than dribbling out.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a meta skill setup where you want a large payoff occasionally rather than a small one constantly.

name: Energy Retention
stats: Skills Triggered by Supported Meta Skills have 35% chance to refund half of their Energy cost
description: Supports Meta Skills. Supported Skills gain a chance to partially Refund a portion of Energy cost when Triggering or Invoking other Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for meta skills, giving triggered skills a 35% chance to refund half the energy they cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: Refunded energy directly means more triggers per fight, which compounds over a long encounter.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build leaning on triggered skills as a main damage source rather than as an occasional bonus.

name: Enraged Warcry I
stats: Supported Warcries spend 20 Rage to bypass their Cooldown, instead of an Endurance Charge
description: Supports Warcries, causing them to spend Rage to bypass their usual Cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support that lets you spend twenty rage to skip a warcry's cooldown, instead of spending an endurance charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: It changes which resource gates your warcries, which matters if you generate rage easily but hoard endurance charges for defence.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage-building warrior who wants to shout more often without giving up defensive charges.

name: Enraged Warcry II
stats: Supported Warcries spend 15 Rage to bypass their Cooldown, instead of an Endurance Charge
description: Supports Warcries, causing them to spend Rage to bypass their usual Cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, dropping the rage cost to bypass a warcry cooldown from twenty to fifteen.
beginner.whyItMatters: A cheaper bypass means more warcries per fight from the same rage generation.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth swapping in the moment you can, since cheaper bypasses mean more shouts from the same rage income.

name: Eonyr's Thunder
stats: Supported Skills Cannot inflict Shock
Lightning Damage from Supported Skills Contributes to Electrocution Buildup
description: Supports any Skill which can deal damage. Lightning Damage from Supported Skills can inflict Electrocute, but Supported Skills cannot inflict Shock. Enemies slain while Electrocuted by Supported Skills explode, dealing a percentage of their maximum Life as Lightning damage.
flavourText:
"How? Well, the Great Wyvern granted her passage, of course.
Eonyr and his flock soar the winds between us and the Moon.
The roar of the storm... that's them, as they hunt and call."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that lets lightning damage build electrocution instead of shock, and makes enemies killed while electrocuted explode for a share of their maximum life as lightning damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The corpse explosions chain through a pack, so an electrocute build gets the clearing speed it usually lacks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build clearing groups. Against a single boss there is nothing for the explosion to hit.

name: Escalating Poison
stats: Targets can be affected by +1 Poisons from Supported Skills at the same time
Supported Skills have 20% less Poison Duration
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, allowing it to inflict an extra Poison on enemies but shortening the duration of those Poisons.

beginner.whatItIs: A support allowing one extra poison stack on a target at a time, with each poison lasting 20% less long.
beginner.whyItMatters: Poison damage comes from how many stacks are running at once, so an extra concurrent stack is a direct increase even with the shorter life.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a poison build that applies poison quickly. On a slow attack the shorter duration can cost more than the extra stack gives.

name: Esh's Prowess
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Lightning Skills
Supported Skills only roll the minimum or maximum Damage value for Lightning Damage
description: Supports Lightning skills that Hit targets, granting them an additional level and causing them to only roll the minimum or maximum value for Lightning damage. Does not support skills which do not have levels.
flavourText:
Knowledge unending had transcended physical form.
Her minds raced through metal latticework as the
flesh of the melding reached up to contain her.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage lightning support granting one extra gem level, and making the skill only ever roll the lowest or highest possible lightning damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lightning damage normally rolls across a huge range, and this replaces that spread with a coin flip between the two extremes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that can afford swings between very low and very high hits. It makes your damage far less predictable.

name: Esh's Radiance
stats: Chaos Damage from Hits with Supported Skills also Contributes to Shock Chance
Supported Skills Gain 40% of Lightning Damage as Extra Chaos Damage
description: Supports Skills that can cause Damaging Hits, granting extra Chaos damage and causing Chaos damage to Contribute to Shock.
flavourText:
"Where life once thrived, now only metal grows, inching
like endless worms through the ash. Where silence fell,
now sourceless thought whispers numbers in the dark."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that adds 40% of your lightning damage again as chaos damage, and lets that chaos damage contribute to shock.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage normally cannot shock at all, so this keeps the shock scaling of a lightning build while adding a damage type that bypasses energy shield.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that wants an answer to enemies hiding behind energy shield without losing its shock.

name: Essence Harvest
stats: Recoup 8% of your maximum Mana when a Persistent Reviving Minion created by Supported Skill dies
description: Supports Skills which create Reviving Persistent Minions. When those Minions die, you Recoup a percentage of your maximum Mana.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for reviving persistent minions. Each time one dies you recoup 8% of your maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns minion deaths, which happen constantly, into the resource you need to keep casting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build with expensive spells and minions that die often enough to feed it.

name: Eternal Flame I
stats: Supported Skills have 100% increased Ignite Duration on Enemies
Supported Skills have 25% less Flammability Magnitude
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing its Ignites to be inflicted less often but last longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that doubles ignite duration while making the skill 25% less likely to ignite in the first place.
beginner.whyItMatters: Longer ignites deal their damage over more time, which suits a build that applies one big ignite rather than many small ones.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slow, heavy fire hit. On a rapid skill, losing ignite chance costs more than the duration returns.

name: Eternal Flame II
stats: Supported Skills have 100% increased Ignite Duration on Enemies
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing its Ignites to last longer.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, doubling ignite duration with no reduction to how often you ignite.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the drawback entirely, which makes it a straightforward gain for any ignite build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it instead of the version that costs you ignite chance, on any fire build.

name: Eternal Flame III
stats: Supported Skills have 20% chance to refresh Ignite duration on Critical Hit
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to refresh Ignites on Critical Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version, giving a 20% chance for a critical hit to refresh the ignite's duration rather than extending it outright.
beginner.whyItMatters: Refreshing keeps a strong ignite alive indefinitely as long as you keep landing crits, which suits a critical fire build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it over the duration versions only if you crit often. On a low-crit build the earlier versions are more reliable.

name: Eternal Mark
stats: Marks from Supported Skills are not Consumed the first time they Activate
description: Supports Mark Skills, causing them to not be Consumed the first time they are Activated.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops a mark being consumed the first time it activates.
beginner.whyItMatters: It effectively gives every mark two uses, which halves how often you have to spend time reapplying one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any mark build, especially in fights where you would rather be attacking than recasting.

name: Excise
stats: Supported Skills have 40% more chance to Critically Hit
Supported Skills have a Cooldown of 8 seconds
description: Supports any damaging Skill that you use yourself, granting it significantly higher chance to Critically Hit, but causing it to gain a long cooldown. Cannot support Skills which already have a cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 40% more critical hit chance while adding an eight second cooldown to the skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a skill you could spam into an occasional heavy blow, which only pays off if that blow lands hard.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a big single hit used to open on a tough target. Never on the skill you attack with continuously.

name: Execrate
stats: Supported Skills have 100% more chance to inflict Ailments
Supported Skills have a Cooldown of 8 seconds
description: Supports any damaging Skill that you use yourself, granting it significantly higher chance to inflict Ailments on hit, but causing it to gain a long cooldown. Cannot support Skills which already have a cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: A support doubling the skill's chance to inflict ailments, at the cost of an eight second cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a skill into a dedicated ailment applier used once per fight, rather than a source of steady damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pair it with a second skill that consumes or pays off ailments. It is a poor fit for your main attack.

name: Execute I
stats: Supported Skills deal 40% more Damage with Hits against Enemies that are on Low Life
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal more damage against enemies on Low Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 40% more hit damage against enemies already on low life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shortens the tail end of every fight, which is where a monster has the most chances left to kill you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An easy pick on almost any damaging skill. The bonus is simply absent until the enemy is hurt.

name: Execute II
stats: Supported Skills deal 50% more Damage with Hits against Enemies that are on Low Life
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal more damage against enemies on Low Life.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger finishing support, raising the low-life bonus to 50% more hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A bigger multiplier at the end means dangerous enemies spend even less time in the state where they can still fight back.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Straight replacement for the first version; there is no new condition to learn.

name: Execute III
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage with Hits while you are on Low Life
Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage with Hits against Enemies that are on Low Life
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal more damage against enemies on Low Life, as well as dealing more damage while you are on Low Life.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version, giving 30% more damage against low-life enemies and another 30% while you yourself are on low life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays out in two separate situations rather than one, so the total is often higher even though each half is smaller.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on a build that spends real time at low life. If you stay healthy, the second half never applies and the earlier versions beat it.

name: Expand
stats: Supported Skills have a maximum of 3 Seals
Supported Skills get 30% increased area of effect per Seal broken
Supported Spells gain a Seal every 0.2% of cast time
description: Supports Spells you cast yourself, Sealing them over time. The Seals are broken when cast, increasing area of effect. Cannot support Channelling Skills or Skills with a Cooldown or which already gain Seals.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support that seals the spell as you charge it, up to three seals, with each seal broken on cast adding 30% increased area of effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards waiting before you cast, turning a small spell into a room-covering one if you hold it long enough.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a spell you cast deliberately between fights. It cannot support channelled spells or ones with a cooldown.

name: Expanse
stats: Supported Skills have 50% increased Area of Effect
Supported Skills have a Cooldown of 8 seconds
description: Supports any Skill that you use yourself, granting it significantly higher Area of Effect but causing it to gain a long cooldown. Cannot support Skills which already have a cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 50% increased area of effect while adding an eight second cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: A much larger area on an occasional cast suits a set-piece skill rather than something you repeat.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an opening area skill fired into a big pack. Never on a skill you need available constantly.

name: Exploit Weakness
stats: Supported Skills cannot Break Armour
Supported Skills Consume Enemy Fully Broken Armour to deal 40% more Damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing them to deal more Damage against enemies with Broken Armour but preventing them from Breaking Armour themselves. Cannot support skills that Consume Broken Armour.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops the skill breaking armour, and instead consumes fully broken armour to deal 40% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the finisher half of an armour-break plan, spending the armour another skill stripped for a large hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only alongside a separate armour-breaking skill. On its own it removes your armour break and gets nothing back.

name: Exposing Cry
stats: Supported Skills apply Exposure on Hit for 5 seconds
description: Supports Warcries. Supported Skills apply Exposure on Hitting enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support that applies exposure for five seconds to every enemy the warcry hits.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exposure lowers enemy resistance, so shouting before a fight makes everything that follows land harder.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an elemental build with a warcry it uses to open on packs and bosses.

name: Extraction
stats: Supported Skills Gain 35% of Damage as extra Chaos Damage
Supported Skills Sacrifice 10% of Life on use
description: Supports Spell Skills which cause Damaging Hits. Using supported Spells will cause you to Sacrifice a portion of your Life on use, gaining extra Chaos Damage in exchange. Does not support Persistent Skills, Minion Skills, or Triggered Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support that sacrifices a tenth of your life each cast and gives 35% of your damage again as chaos damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a large damage increase paid for out of your health bar, so its safety depends entirely on how fast you recover.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster with strong life recovery. Without it, a long fight becomes a race against your own casting.

name: Fan The Flames I
stats: Trigger Fan the Flames when Hitting an Ignited enemy with Supported Skills
