description: Supports Wind Skills which Hit enemies. Hits with Supported Skills against Ignited enemies Trigger a fiery explosion, dealing damage to that enemy and enemies in a cone behind them.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for wind skills. Hitting an ignited enemy triggers a fiery explosion that also damages enemies in a cone behind them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a wind build a way to convert one ignited target into damage across the whole line behind it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a fire and wind combination where something else is igniting first. Without ignites it never triggers.

name: Fan The Flames II
stats: Trigger Fan the Flames when Hitting an Ignited enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports Wind Skills which Hit enemies. Hits with Supported Skills against Ignited enemies Trigger a fiery explosion, dealing damage to that enemy and enemies in a cone behind them. The explosion Spreads the initial enemy's Ignite to other enemies Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: The upgraded version, where the explosion also spreads the original enemy's ignite to everything it hits.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spreading the ignite means each explosion sets up the next one, so a single ignited enemy can light up a whole pack.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to take once available for any ignite-and-wind clearing setup.

name: Feeding Frenzy I
stats: Minions from Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage
Minions from Supported Skills take 20% more Damage
description: Supports skills which create Minions, making them deal and take more damage. Cannot support skills which create undamageable Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support giving your minions 30% more damage and making them take 20% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a straight trade of minion survivability for minion damage, which is fine while your minions are cheap to replace.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For minion builds that resummon easily. Avoid it on expensive minions you cannot afford to lose.

name: Feeding Frenzy II
stats: Minions from Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage
Minions from Supported Skills take 15% more Damage
description: Minions from Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage Minions from Supported Skills take 15% more Damage

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, with the same 30% more minion damage but only 15% more damage taken.
beginner.whyItMatters: The smaller penalty makes the same damage gain noticeably safer for your minions.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap it in wherever the first version was; your minions keep the damage and lose less durability.

name: Ferocity
stats: Supported Skills cannot generate Frenzy Charges
Supported Skills will consume a Frenzy Charge on use if possible
Supported Skills have 40% more Skill Speed when consuming Frenzy Charges
description: Supports Skills that you use yourself. Supported Skills will consume a Frenzy Charge on use if possible, and will gain significant Skill Speed if they do. Supported Skills cannot generate Frenzy Charges.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that consumes a frenzy charge on use for 40% more skill speed, and stops the skill generating frenzy charges of its own.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts stored frenzy charges directly into speed, but you need a separate way of making them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a two-skill setup where one skill builds frenzy charges and this one spends them.

name: Fiery Death
stats: Enemies Ignited by Supported Skills have 60% chance to explode on death
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing enemies it Ignites to have a chance to explode on death.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving enemies your skill ignited a 60% chance to explode when they die.
beginner.whyItMatters: Corpse explosions chain through packs, which is how an ignite build turns a slow burn into fast clearing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing groups with a fire build. It gives nothing in a fight against a single target.

name: Fire Attunement
stats: Gain 25% of Damage as extra Fire Damage
Supported Skills deal 50% less Cold and Lightning Damage
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, causing them to Gain Fire Damage but deal less Cold and Lightning Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support adding a quarter of your damage again as fire damage while halving cold and lightning damage dealt.
beginner.whyItMatters: Fire is the element that ignites, so this pushes a skill toward burning damage rather than raw hits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a fire-focused build. On a skill that already deals all three elements you are trading away more than you gain.

name: Fire Exposure
stats: Supported Skills inflict Exposure for 8 seconds on Igniting a target
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to inflict Exposure when Igniting.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that applies exposure for eight seconds whenever the skill ignites something.
beginner.whyItMatters: Since ignite is already the goal of a fire build, this attaches a resistance reduction to a step you were taking anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a fire build that ignites reliably. It never triggers on a skill that cannot ignite.

name: Fire Mastery
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Fire Skills
description: Supports Fire skills, granting them an additional level. Does not support skills which do not have levels.

beginner.whatItIs: A support granting a fire skill one extra gem level.
beginner.whyItMatters: A level raises every number on the skill at once, which is usually broader than any single modifier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A reliable pick in a fire build. Skills with no level gain nothing from it.

name: Fire Penetration I
stats: Supported Skills Penetrate 30% Fire Resistance
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making those Hits Penetrate enemy Fire resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: A support making the skill's hits penetrate 30% of enemy fire resistance.
beginner.whyItMatters: Once monsters carry heavy resistances, penetration does more for your damage than another multiplier would.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Becomes valuable in later content. Early on, enemies resist too little for it to be worth the slot.

name: Fire Penetration II
stats: Hits from Supported Skills ignore enemy Fire Resistance
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making those Hits ignore enemy Fire resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, where hits ignore enemy fire resistance entirely rather than penetrating a share of it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ignoring resistance completely removes the single biggest reason fire damage falls off in endgame content.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for a fire build fighting monsters whose resistances are what limit your damage.

name: Fist of War I
stats: Attacks with Supported Skill are Ancestrally Boosted, no more than once every 6 seconds
description: Supports Slams you use yourself, providing a powerful Ancestral Boost every few seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A slam support that ancestrally boosts your slam once every six seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slams are slow, so a periodic boost lines up naturally with how often you actually swing one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slam build with no other source of boosted hits. It costs the skill nothing.

name: Fist of War II
stats: Attacks with Supported Skill are Ancestrally Boosted, no more than once every 4 seconds
description: Supports Slams you use yourself, providing a powerful Ancestral Boost every few seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved slam boost, arriving once every four seconds instead of six.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two seconds sooner means the boost is available in most exchanges rather than only in longer ones.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it as soon as you can on the slam you actually spend your time swinging.

name: Fist of War III
stats: Attacks with Supported Skill are Ancestrally Boosted, no more than once every 14 seconds
Ancestral Boost has double effect on Supported Skills
description: Supports Slams you use yourself, providing a very powerful Ancestral Boost infrequently.

beginner.whatItIs: The final slam boost. It arrives only once every fourteen seconds, but the ancestral boost has twice the effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It concentrates the same idea into one huge hit rather than several moderate ones, which suits burst-window play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For boss fights where you can save the boosted slam for a moment that matters. For clearing, the faster versions are better.

name: Flamepierce
stats: Supported Skills cannot Ignite
Projectiles from Supported Skills Pierce Ignited Enemies
description: Supports Skills which can fire Projectiles. Initial Projectile created by Supported Skills will always Pierce Ignited Enemies, but Supported Skills cannot inflict Ignite themselves.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where the first projectile always pierces ignited enemies, but the skill can no longer ignite by itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: Piercing lets one shot travel through a whole line of burning enemies rather than stopping at the first.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when another skill does the igniting. On its own it removes the condition it needs.

name: Fluke
stats: Skills Triggered by Supported Skills deal between 40% less and 60% more Damage
Skills Triggered by Supported Skills recover between 0% and 20% of cost on use
description: Supports Skills which Trigger other Skills. Skills Triggered by Supported Skills have their Damage randomly raised or lowered when Triggered, as well as recovering a random amount of their cost when Triggered.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for triggering skills. Triggered skills deal anywhere from 40% less to 60% more damage at random, and refund up to a fifth of their cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: It widens your damage into a gamble, with the average tilted upward and part of your cost sometimes returned.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a trigger build that fires often enough for the swings to even out. Avoid it if you need each trigger to land for a set amount.

name: Focused Curse
stats: Curse zones from Supported
Skills erupt after 50% less delay
description: Supports Curse skills, causing them to Curse enemies more quickly after being cast.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support that halves the delay before a curse zone erupts after you cast it.
beginner.whyItMatters: A curse that lands twice as fast is one enemies cannot simply walk out of before it applies.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse build fighting moving enemies, where the delay is what makes curses miss.

name: Font of Blood
stats: Totems created by Supported Skills create a Blood Font with a radius of 4 metres
Allies in Blood Fonts Leech Life equal to 12% of Physical Damage dealt by Supported Totem
description: Supports Skills which create Totems. Totems created by supported Skills generate a Font of Blood which will Leech Life to Allies within it.

beginner.whatItIs: A totem support where each totem creates a four metre blood font, letting allies inside leech life from 12% of the totem's physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a totem from pure damage into a healing zone you can stand in, which is a defence layer with no cost to you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical totem build that fights near its totems rather than placing them and walking away.

name: Font of Mana
stats: Totems created by Supported Skills create a Mana Font with a radius of 4 metres
Allies in Mana Fonts Leech Mana equal to 12% of Physical Damage dealt by Supported Totem
description: Supports Skills which create Totems. Totems created by supported Skills generate a Font of Mana which will Leech Mana to Allies within it.

beginner.whatItIs: A totem support creating a four metre mana font, letting allies inside leech mana from 12% of the totem's physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It solves mana sustain for a caster by putting the fix on the ground rather than in the gear.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a mana-hungry build that can hold position near its totems while attacking.

name: Fork
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills Fork
Projectiles from Supported Skills deal
30% less Damage after Forking
description: Supports Projectile skills, making their Projectiles Fork.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support that makes projectiles fork into two on hit, with the forked projectiles dealing 30% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forking widens what a single shot covers, which is what turns a single-target skill into a clearing one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs. Take it off for boss fights, where the forks have nothing to hit.

name: Fortress I
stats: Supported Skills deal 40% less damage with Hits
Walls from Supported Skills are created in a Circle instead
description: Supports skills that create walls in a line, causing them to be created in a circle instead but deal less Hit damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that turns a wall skill's straight line into a circle, at the cost of 40% of its hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A circular wall surrounds you or an enemy instead of dividing a space, which is a completely different tactical tool.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For trapping a target or shielding yourself. Take a line wall instead if you are blocking a corridor.

name: Fortress II
stats: Supported Skills have 20% less Area of Effect
Supported Skills deal 30% less damage with Hits
Walls from Supported Skills are created in a Circle instead
description: Supports skills that create walls in a line, causing them to be created in a circle instead but deal less Hit damage and have lowered Area of Effect.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved circular wall support: only 30% less hit damage, with 20% less area of effect added.
beginner.whyItMatters: You keep more of the wall's damage in exchange for a tighter ring, which is often the better trade.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it when the wall's damage matters to you as much as its shape.

name: Freeze
stats: Supported Skills cause 50% more Freeze Buildup
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making it more effective at Freezing enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes the skill build freeze 50% faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Freezing is one of the strongest forms of control in the game, and this is the plainest way to reach it more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build that wants to lock enemies down rather than only damage them.

name: Freezefork
stats: Supported Skills Fork when hitting Frozen Enemies
Supported Skills cannot cause Freeze buildup
description: Supports Skills which can fire Projectiles. Projectiles from Supported Skills always Fork when the initial Projectile Hits Frozen Enemies, but Supported Skills cannot build up Freeze themselves.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where projectiles fork when they hit a frozen enemy, while the skill loses the ability to build freeze itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a build that freezes with one skill and then sprays through the frozen pack with another.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when another skill does the freezing. On its own it can never meet its own condition.

name: Frenzied Riposte
stats: Supported Skills Consume Parried Debuff on Hit to grant a Frenzy Charge
description: Supports Attacks you use or Trigger yourself, causing them to Consume the Parried Debuff on Hit to grant you a Frenzy Charge. Cannot support Skills which already Consume the Parried Debuff.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that consumes the parried debuff on hit to grant you a frenzy charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts successful defence into offensive resource, so blocking and countering feeds your damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a parrying build that wants frenzy charges without a separate charge-generating skill.

name: Fresh Clip I
stats: Supported Crossbow Skills deal 1% more Damage for each bolt Reloaded by that skill in the past 6 seconds
description: Supports Crossbow Skills, granting them more damage for each bolt reloaded by that Skill in the last 6 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: A crossbow support giving 1% more damage for each bolt the skill reloaded in the last six seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards keeping a full magazine loaded, so reloading stops feeling like wasted time and becomes part of your damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a crossbow build with a large magazine that reloads in bulk.

name: Fresh Clip II
stats: Supported Crossbow Skills deal 1% more Damage for each bolt Reloaded by that skill in the past 8 seconds
description: Supports Crossbow Skills, granting them more damage for each bolt reloaded by that Skill in the last 8 seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, counting bolts reloaded over the last eight seconds instead of six.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer window means the bonus survives across a pause in shooting rather than draining away.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth taking the moment it is available, especially if you fight in bursts with pauses between them.

name: Frost Nexus
stats: Supported Skills create Chilled Ground for 8 seconds when they Freeze an Enemy
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to create patches of Chilled Ground around Frozen enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that creates chilled ground for eight seconds around any enemy the skill freezes.
beginner.whyItMatters: The chilled patch slows everything nearby, so one freeze becomes crowd control on the whole group around it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build fighting packs that press in on you.

name: Frostfire
stats: 50% more Magnitude of Ignite inflicted on Frozen targets with Supported Skills
Supported Skills cannot cause Freeze buildup
Supported Skills Consume Freeze from Enemies they Ignite
25% more Magnitude of Ignite inflicted on Frozen Unique enemies with Supported Skills
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to Consume Freeze on Igniting a Frozen enemy to boost the effect of the Ignite.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops the skill building freeze, and instead consumes an existing freeze when igniting a frozen enemy to make that ignite 50% stronger.
beginner.whyItMatters: It bridges cold and fire, spending a freeze you no longer need for a burn that keeps working.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that freezes with one skill and ignites with another. Alone it can neither freeze nor pay off.

name: Frozen Spite
stats: Supported Skills trigger Ice Fragments on killing Frozen Enemies
description: Supports Attack Skills, causing them to create Ice Fragments on killing Frozen Enemies. Cannot Support Totem Skills and does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that creates ice fragments whenever you kill a frozen enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: The fragments carry damage on into the pack, so a frozen kill becomes the start of a chain rather than the end of one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold attack build clearing groups it freezes. It does nothing against a single boss.

name: Gambleshot
stats: Projectiles fired by Supported Skills Fork, Chain an additional time, or Pierce an additional time at random
Projectiles from Supported Skills deal 15% less Damage
description: Supports Skills which fire Projectiles that are not ground targeted. Projectiles from Supported Skills randomly Fork, Chain or Pierce.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support where each projectile randomly forks, chains an extra time or pierces, at the cost of 15% of its damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It buys extra coverage cheaply, but which kind of coverage you get is out of your hands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing with a projectile skill when you would rather have any extra reach than none. A dedicated fork or chain support is more predictable.

name: Garukhan's Resolve
stats: Maximum Critical Hit chance with Supported Skills is 50%
Attack Critical Hit Chance with Supported Skills Bifurcates
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself which do not already have some Condition for use. Supported Skills have a maximum Critical Hit chance, but will Bifurcate Critical Hit Chance.
flavourText:
At the last, her hope gone - but not her resolve - she threw her
beloved Tangletongue. That was the day a god bled. For this, the
Great Roc graced a Maraketh warrior with a feather for the first time.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage attack support that caps your critical hit chance at 50% and makes the skill's attack critical chance bifurcate.
beginner.whyItMatters: It reshapes how your crits are distributed rather than adding damage, so its value depends entirely on what the rest of your build does with crits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical attack build built around bifurcation. It is a downgrade for a build already above the cap.

name: Glacier
stats: Ice Crystals created by Supported Skills have 100% more Life
description: Supports any Skill which creates Ice Crystals, causing them to be created with higher Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that doubles the life of ice crystals the skill creates.
beginner.whyItMatters: Crystals that survive longer keep doing their job through a fight instead of shattering in the first exchange.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build using ice crystals as barriers or as a lasting presence on the field.

name: Gorge
stats: Supported Skills grant 10 Life Flask Charges for each Corpse Consumed
Supported Skills grant 10 Mana Flask Charges for each Corpse Consumed
description: Supports skills that consume Corpses. Consuming Corpses with supported skills grants Flask charges.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants ten life flask charges and ten mana flask charges for each corpse the skill consumes.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns corpse consumption into refilled flasks, which is sustain for both your health and your casting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a corpse-consuming build that struggles to keep flasks charged in long fights.

name: Guatelitzi's Ablation
stats: When an Offering from Supported Skills dies, Regenerate 5% of your Life and Mana per second, for as long as that Offering was alive
Supported Skills Sacrifice 25% of Life on use
Offerings from Supported Skills grant you a Power Charge every 4 seconds
description: Supports Offering Skills. Supported Skills Sacrifice a portion of your life on use. While Offering spikes from Supported Skills persist, you are periodically granted a Power Charge. When spikes from Supported Skills die, Regenerate a percentage of your maximum Life and Mana per second based on the duration the Offering persisted.
flavourText:
Young Guatelitzi was found moving among the prisoners,
preparing their living bodies for sacrifice. The High Priests
recognised his inclinations, and gave him a higher calling.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage offering support. It sacrifices a quarter of your life on use, grants a power charge every four seconds while the offering's spikes are alive, and regenerates 5% of your life and mana per second for as long as that offering lasted once it dies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It front-loads a heavy cost and pays it back afterwards, so the whole cycle is a bet on the offering surviving.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an offering build that can absorb a large life hit up front and wants charges and recovery for the rest of the fight.

name: Haemocrystals
stats: Supported Attacks cannot cause Bleeding
Supported Skills Consume Bleeding on Enemies they Hit, creating 4 Haemocrystals
Supported Skills create 2 additional Haemocrystals when Consuming Aggravated Bleeding
Maximum 20 active Haemocrystals
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself which can cause Damaging Hits. Supported Skills Consume Bleeding on Hit to create explosive blood-filled crystals, but cannot themselves inflict Bleeding. Cannot Support Skills which already Consume Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that consumes bleeding on hit to create four explosive blood crystals, six against aggravated bleeding, up to twenty at once. The skill can no longer inflict bleeding.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts bleeding into immediate explosive damage rather than a slow drain, which is a very different way to use a bleed build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only alongside another skill that applies bleeding. It removes its own source otherwise.

name: Hardy Totems I
stats: Totems created by Supported
Skills have 40% more maximum Life
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, causing those Totems to have more Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A totem support giving your totems 40% more maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: Totems that die immediately deal no damage at all, so survivability is often worth more to them than a damage multiplier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any totem build whose totems keep getting destroyed before they finish attacking.

name: Hardy Totems II
stats: Totems created by Supported
Skills have 50% more maximum Life
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, causing those Totems to have more Life.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving totems 50% more maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra life keeps totems standing in harder content, where the first version starts to fall short.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once your totems are still dying in the content you are running.

name: Harmonic Remnants I
stats: Remnants created by Supported Skills can be collected from 35% further away
description: Supports Skills which create Remnants, allowing those Remnants to be collected from further away.

beginner.whatItIs: A support letting remnants the skill creates be collected from 35% further away.
beginner.whyItMatters: Remnants you cannot reach are wasted, so extending the pickup range converts them from a chore into something automatic.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a remnant build where you find yourself walking back for pickups instead of fighting.

name: Harmonic Remnants II
stats: 20% chance for Supported Skills to create an additional Remnant
Remnants created by Supported Skills can be collected from 35% further away
description: Supports Skills which create Remnants, allowing those Remnants to be collected from further away, with a chance to create an additional Remnant.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, keeping the extended pickup range and adding a 20% chance to create an extra remnant.
beginner.whyItMatters: More remnants plus a wider reach means noticeably more of them actually reach you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once your gem tier reaches it; the extra remnants come at no cost.

name: Hayoxi's Fulmination
stats: Supported Skills create Cursed Ground
Enemies on the Cursed Ground from a Supported Skill are Cursed while within it
Maximum 2 areas of Cursed Ground
Trigger Annihilation when Cursed Ground from Supported Skills have persisted for 7 seconds
Annihiliation
This Skill will copy the Level of the Gem it is Socketed in
Deals (25-#) to (37-#) Physical Damage
Impact radius is 1.7 metres
Hits a total of 6 times over 2 seconds
100% of Physical Damage Converted to other Damage Types matching the Supported Curse Gem's Tags
description: Supports Curse Skills. Supported Curse Skills create areas which Curse enemies so long as they are within them. Cursed areas from Supported Skills gather power before erupting in a column of annihilating light after a moderate delay.
flavourText:
The Architect of Destruction slipped explosive powder
under the royal temple one pinch at a time. For years,
he clung to that, never finding the courage to light it.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage curse support that lays down cursed ground, and after seven seconds triggers a column of light that hits six times over two seconds, converting its physical damage to match the curse gem's own damage types.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a curse build a heavy delayed detonation, so cursing a spot is also planting a bomb in it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse build fighting stationary targets or in a place enemies must stay. Seven seconds is a long wait against anything mobile.

name: Healing Runes
stats: Lose up to 10% of your maximum Runic Ward every 5 seconds to heal nearby allies for a total of 200% of the amount of Ward lost
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to lose Runic Ward and heal nearby allies based on the Ward lost. Healing done is split between allies who are not on full Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs. Every five seconds you lose up to a tenth of your runic ward to heal nearby allies for twice the ward you gave up.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a personal defensive resource into party healing at a favourable rate, which is a role few supports fill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a group or a minion build with allies to heal. Solo, you are spending ward for nothing.

name: Heavy Swing
stats: Supported Skills deal 35% more Melee Physical Damage
Supported Skills have 10% less Attack Speed
description: Supports Melee Attacks, boosting their Physical damage at the cost of Attack Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support giving 35% more melee physical damage for 10% less attack speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: The damage gained far outweighs the speed lost on paper, though slower swings also mean fewer chances to apply anything on hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good on a heavy physical attack. Less appealing if your build depends on hit frequency for ailments or leech.

name: Heft
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Maximum Physical Hit Damage
description: Supports Skills which deal Damage, increasing the maximum Physical Damage of their Hits.

beginner.whatItIs: A support raising the maximum physical damage of the skill's hits by 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It widens the top end of your damage range rather than lifting the whole thing, so your best hits get better while your worst stay the same.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical build that already rolls high, particularly one relying on big hits to stun or shatter.

name: Heightened Accuracy I
stats: Supported Skills have 50% more Accuracy Rating
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to gain Accuracy.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support giving 50% more accuracy rating.
beginner.whyItMatters: A missed attack does nothing at all, so accuracy is often the cheapest real damage increase available to an attack build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Any time you are missing noticeably. If you already hit reliably, spend the slot on damage instead.

name: Heightened Accuracy II
stats: Supported Skills Always Hit Enemies on full Life
Supported Skills have 50% more Accuracy Rating
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to gain Accuracy, and never miss against Enemies on full Life.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger accuracy support, keeping the 50% more accuracy and guaranteeing hits against enemies on full life.
beginner.whyItMatters: The guaranteed opening hit means the first strike of every fight always lands, which matters most when that strike sets up everything else.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier version once available, and prioritise it if you open fights with a single big strike.

name: Heightened Charges
stats: Benefits from consuming Charges for Supported Skill have 20% chance to be doubled
description: Supports any Skill that Consumes Charges, granting a chance for benefits of that Consumption to be doubled.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving a 20% chance for the benefit of consuming a charge to be doubled.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stretches the value of a resource you were already spending, without needing you to generate any more of it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that consumes charges as part of its rotation. It gives nothing if you simply hold your charges.

name: Heightened Curse
stats: Supported Curses have 25% increased Magnitudes
description: Supports Curse Skills, magnifying their power.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support giving 25% increased curse magnitude.
beginner.whyItMatters: Deeper curses mean every attack you make afterwards is worth more, so it multiplies your build rather than adding to it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A safe pick on any curse skill you actually maintain on your targets.

name: Helbrym's Hide
stats: Gain Helbrym's Composure for 2 seconds when Supported Skills cause you to Shapeshift
description: Supports Shapeshifting Skills, causing them to grant Helbrym's Composure for a brief duration when they cause you to Shapeshift. Shapeshifting into a different form before the Buff expires causes it to be removed without effect.
flavourText:
Surrounded by abominations, Lysanda of Myr expected her
time had come to an end. Helbrym of Tarth charged from
the trees, breaking his oath, to save the Ezomyte Queen.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage shapeshifting support that grants Helbrym's Composure for two seconds each time the skill shifts your form. Shifting again before it expires removes it without effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards holding a form for a moment rather than flickering between them, which shapes how a shapeshifting build is played.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a shapeshifter who shifts deliberately. It gives nothing to a build that changes form constantly.

name: Her Declaration
stats: Enemies entering your Presence while a Supported Skill is active are Intimidated for 4 seconds
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing enemies that enter your Presence to become Intimidated while the Skill is active.
flavourText:
"The laws are binding. They are absolute. If they believe
it is their choice to enforce them, all the better.
Upholding our solemn duty is imperative."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for persistent buffs that intimidates enemies for four seconds as they enter your presence.
beginner.whyItMatters: Intimidated enemies take more damage, and this applies it automatically to everything that walks up to you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a character who lets packs come to them. It is weaker when you are the one running past enemies.

name: Herbalism I
stats: 30% Increased Recovery from Life Flasks while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain increased Life recovery from Flasks while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs giving 30% increased recovery from life flasks while active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Flasks are your emergency heal, and a bigger heal from the same charge means fewer moments where the flask was not enough.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that survives on flask healing rather than regeneration or leech.

name: Herbalism II
stats: 50% Increased Recovery from Life Flasks while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain increased Life recovery from Flasks while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger flask recovery support, giving 50% increased recovery from life flasks while the buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Half again as much healing from each charge stretches a limited flask supply much further in a hard fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move to it once flask charges rather than flask size are what limits your healing.

name: Hex Bloom
stats: Curses from Supported Skills spread to enemies within 3 metres when a Cursed enemy dies
description: Supports Curses, spreading their effects when a Cursed enemy dies.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support that spreads the curse to enemies within three metres when a cursed enemy dies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It means you only need to curse one enemy in a pack, and the curse handles the rest as they die.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse build clearing groups. Against a single boss there is nothing for the curse to spread onto.

name: Hit and Run
stats: Supported Skills become usable after you have moved 10 metres
Supported Skills become unusable again after use
Supported Skills have 40% more Skill Speed
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself which do not already have some Condition for use. Supported Skills can only be used after you have moved a certain distance, but have massively increased Skill Speed. Cannot support Skills which have a cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that locks the skill until you have moved ten metres, then gives 40% more skill speed for that one use.
beginner.whyItMatters: It suits a hit-and-move rhythm, paying you for repositioning rather than punishing it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a mobile attacker. It is a poor fit for a stationary fight where you never travel far enough to unlock it.

name: Holy Descent
stats: Supported Skills create Consecrated Ground for 4 seconds on landing
Supported Skills create Consecrated Ground in an area of 2.2 metres
description: Supports Skills that leap into the air, causing them to create Consecrated Ground when you land.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for leaping skills that creates consecrated ground where you land, lasting four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It means every landing gives you a small safe patch to fight from, which turns movement into a defensive action.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that leaps into fights regularly and benefits from consecrated ground.

name: Hourglass
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage
Supported Skills have a Cooldown of 10 seconds
description: Supports any damaging skill that you use yourself, causing it to deal significantly more damage but gain a long cooldown. Cannot support Skills which already have a cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 30% more damage while adding a ten second cooldown to the skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a repeatable skill into a once-per-fight hammer, so the damage only counts if you time the use well.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy opener or a finisher. Never on the skill you rely on to keep attacking.

name: Hulking Minions
stats: Minions from Supported Skills are Gigantic
description: Supports Skills which summon Persistent Minions. Supported Minions are larger, have more Life, and deal more Damage, but cost significantly more Spirit.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes persistent minions gigantic, giving them more life and damage in exchange for a much higher spirit reservation.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades minion count for minion quality, which changes a swarm build into a bodyguard build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When you have spirit to spare and want fewer, tougher minions. Skip it if your spirit is already fully committed.

name: Ice Bite I
stats: Gain 25% of Damage as Cold Damage for 5 seconds on Freezing an enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports damaging skills and Warcries you use yourself. Freezing an enemy with supported skills infuses your damage with Cold damage for a short time.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where freezing an enemy grants you 25% of your damage again as cold damage for five seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards freezing with more damage, so a control action also becomes an offensive one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build that freezes often enough to keep the five seconds refreshed.

name: Ice Bite II
stats: Gain 30% of Damage as Cold Damage for 6 seconds on Freezing an enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports damaging skills and Warcries you use yourself. Freezing an enemy with supported skills infuses your damage with Cold damage for a short time.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, granting 30% of damage as cold damage for six seconds when you freeze.
beginner.whyItMatters: More damage over a longer window means the buff is far easier to keep running continuously.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it as soon as you can if you freeze at least once every few seconds.

name: Icicle
stats: Ice Crystals created by Supported Skills have 50% less Life
description: Supports any Skill which creates Ice Crystals, causing them to be created with lower Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that halves the life of ice crystals the skill creates.
beginner.whyItMatters: It exists for builds that want crystals to shatter quickly, since a fragile crystal reaches its payoff sooner.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when breaking your own crystals is part of the plan. As a survivability change it is a straight downgrade.

name: Ignite I
stats: Supported Skills have 100% more Flammability Magnitude
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making it more likely to Ignite.

beginner.whatItIs: A support doubling the skill's flammability magnitude, making it much more likely to ignite.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ignite is where a fire build's damage really lives, so raising how often you apply one is a direct increase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An easy early pick for any fire build that is failing to ignite consistently.

name: Ignite II
stats: Supported Skills have 150% more Flammability Magnitude
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making it more likely to Ignite.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger ignite support, raising flammability magnitude by 150%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Higher flammability means even weaker hits start igniting, which matters on a fast skill with small individual hits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it in place of the first version once your fire build is past the early levels.

name: Ignite III
stats: Ignites from Supported Skills deal Damage 15% faster
Supported Skills have 200% more Flammability Magnitude
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making it more likely to Ignite and causing inflicted Ignites to deal their damage more quickly.

beginner.whatItIs: The final ignite support: 200% more flammability magnitude, and ignites deal their damage 15% faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster ignite damage means the burn finishes before the enemy walks out of the fight, which is where slow ignites lose their value.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to settle on for a fire build, especially one clearing quickly rather than fighting long.

name: Immolate
stats: Supported Skills cannot Ignite
Supported Attacks Gain 30% of Damage as extra Fire Damage against Ignited enemies
description: Supports Attacks, granting them extra Fire damage against Ignited enemies but making them unable to Ignite enemies themselves.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support giving 30% of damage again as fire damage against ignited enemies, while stopping the attack igniting anything itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the payoff half of a fire build, cashing in an ignite that another skill applied.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when something else is igniting. Attached to your only fire skill, it removes the condition it needs.

name: Impact Shockwave
stats: Supported Skills cause an Aftershock when they Heavy Stun an enemy, Damaging other enemies within 1.5 metres
Aftershocks caused this way cannot Stun
description: Supports Melee Strike Skills and Wind Attack Skills, causing them to create an Aftershock that damages enemies around the target when they Heavy Stun an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for melee strikes and wind attacks that sends out an aftershock damaging everything within 1.5 metres whenever you heavy stun an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It spreads a single-target stun into area damage, so staggering one monster hurts the pack around it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy strike build that reliably heavy stuns. On a light, fast skill the trigger rarely happens.

name: Impale
stats: Supported Skills cannot Extract Impale
Supported Skills Impale Enemies on Hit
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to Impale on Hit but making them unable to Extract Impale themselves.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that impales on hit, while stopping the skill extracting impale itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: Impale stores a share of your damage on the enemy to be dealt later, so it builds up over a fight rather than paying out immediately.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical attack build with a separate way to extract impale, or one that fights long enough for the stacks to pay out.

name: Impending Doom
stats: Support
Trigger Doom Blast when Curses from Supported Skills expire
Doom Blast
Cooldown Time: 0.15s (3 uses)
Cast Time: 1.00s
Critical Hit Chance: 7.00%
Deal Chaos damage in an area around the previously Cursed enemy.
Deals base Chaos Damage equal to 15% of your Current Mana
Blast radius is 2 metres
description: Supports Curse skills you cast yourself, causing them to trigger Doom Blast on Cursed enemies when the Curse expires.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support that triggers a doom blast on the cursed enemy when the curse expires, dealing chaos damage based on your current mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives curses a delayed detonation, so a curse you cast and forget still ends in damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse caster with a large mana pool, since the blast is measured against the mana you are holding.

name: Incision
stats: Hits from Supported Skills inflict Incision
3% more Magnitude of Bleeding inflicted with Supported Skills per Incision consumed Recently, up to 30%
description: Supports Attack Skills. Supported Skills inflict Incision on Hit, which causes Enemies to be increasingly more likely to be inflicted with Bleeding. All Incision is removed from a target on inflicting it with Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that inflicts incision on hit, making the enemy progressively easier to make bleed. Bleeding removes all incision and each stack consumed adds 3% more bleed magnitude, up to 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties the setup and the payoff together, so hits that fail to bleed still make the next one land harder.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a bleed build with a fast attack that stacks incision before the bleed lands.

name: Inexorable Critical I
stats: Supported Skills gain 10% increased Critical Hit Chance each second, up to 100%. This Critical Hit Chance is lost whenever a skill supported by Inexorable Critical Critically Hits
description: Supports any skill you use yourself that Hits enemies, causing it to accumulate Critical Hit chance over time.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that adds 10% increased critical hit chance every second, up to 100%, all of which is lost the moment the skill lands a critical hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It guarantees that a slow skill eventually crits, which suits a build that swings rarely and wants each swing to count.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy, slow skill. On a fast skill you will crit before the bonus has built up to anything.

name: Inexorable Critical II
stats: Supported Skills gain 40% increased Critical Hit Chance each second, up to 200%. This Critical Hit Chance is lost whenever a skill supported by Inexorable Critical Critically Hits
Supported Skills gain 10% less Critical Damage Bonus each second, up to 50%. This Critical Damage Bonus is lost whenever a skill supported by Inexorable Critical Critically Hits
description: Supports any skill you use yourself that Hits enemies, causing it to accumulate Critical Hit chance over time, but also reduce your Critical Damage Bonus.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, building 40% increased critical chance per second up to 200%, while also shedding up to 50% of your critical damage bonus over the same period.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ramps to a near-certain critical hit far faster, but the longer you wait the less that critical hit is worth.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When landing a crit at all matters more than how hard it lands, such as for triggering an on-crit effect.

name: Infernal Legion I
stats: Minions from Supported Skills take 10% of their maximum Life as Fire Damage per second
Minions from Supported Skills Ignite Enemies within a radius of 1.5 metres as though dealing Base Fire Damage equal to 10% of Minion's Maximum Life
description: Supports skills which create Minions which can be damaged, causing them and enemies near them to Ignite. The damage of the Ignite is based on the Life of the supported Minion.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support where your minions burn themselves for 10% of their life per second and ignite enemies within 1.5 metres of them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns minions into moving fire hazards, dealing damage just by standing near enemies, at the cost of their own lives.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a swarm of cheap, replaceable minions. It will kill expensive minions you were trying to keep.

name: Infernal Legion II
stats: Minions from Supported Skills take 10% of their maximum Life as Fire Damage per second
Minions from Supported Skills have +20% to Fire Resistance
Minions from Supported Skills Ignite Enemies within a radius of 2 metres as though dealing Base Fire Damage equal to 10% of Minion's Maximum Life
description: Supports skills which create Minions which can be damaged, causing them and enemies near them to Ignite. The damage of the Ignite is based on the Life of the supported Minion.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved burning-minion support, with a two metre radius and 20% fire resistance granted to the minions to offset their own burn.
beginner.whyItMatters: The resistance makes the minions last much longer while burning, so the same idea stops being self-defeating.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth the swap as soon as it is available, since the resistance keeps your minions alive far longer.

name: Inhibitor
stats: Supported Skills cannot consume Infusions
Supported Skills cannot consume Charges
Supported Skills deal 4% more Damage per different type of Charge or Infusion on you
description: Supports any Skill you use or Trigger yourself. Supported Skills cannot consume Charges or Infusion by any means. Cannot Support Skills which require Charges or Infusion to be used.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that stops the skill consuming charges or infusions, and gives 4% more damage for each different type of charge or infusion you are holding.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays you for hoarding charges rather than spending them, which is the opposite of how most charge supports work.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that maintains several charge types at once. It gives nothing if you keep only one kind.

name: Innervate
stats: Gain 25% of Damage as Lightning Damage for 5 seconds on killing a Shocked enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports damaging skills you use yourself. Killing a Shocked enemy with supported skills imbues your damage with Lightning damage for a short time.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where killing a shocked enemy grants you 25% of your damage again as lightning damage for five seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards clearing shocked packs by making the next few kills faster, so momentum builds through a fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that shocks and then kills quickly. It never triggers if nothing you kill is shocked.

name: Intense Agony
stats: Damage over time with non-Ailment Debuffs inflicted on full-life enemies by Supported Skills deal 50% more damage
Supported Skills have 25% less Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports Spells that deal non-Ailment damage over time, causing them to have a shorter duration but deal substantially more damage over time with Debuffs inflicted against enemies on full life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for damage-over-time spells that shortens the effect duration by a quarter and gives 50% more damage when the debuff is applied to a full-life enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards opening on a healthy target, which is exactly when you want a damage-over-time effect to be at its strongest.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster who applies a lasting debuff at the start of each fight rather than reapplying it constantly.

name: Ixchel's Torment
stats: Skills Triggered by Supported Skills have between 40% less and 50% more Area of Effect
Skills Triggered by Supported Skills have between 40% less and 50% more Projectile Speed
Skills Triggered by Supported Skills deal between 40% less and 60% more Damage
Skills Triggered by Supported Skills recover between 0% and 20% of cost on use
description: Supports Skills which Trigger other Skills. Skills Triggered by Supported Skills have their Damage, Area of Effect, and Projectile Speed randomly raised or lowered when Triggered, as well as recovering a random amount of their cost when Triggered.
flavourText:
Few mortals can comprehend the horror of experiencing
every possibility. Chaos alone takes joy in the
unthinkable and the unimaginable made manifest.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for triggering skills. Every trigger randomises its damage, area of effect and projectile speed within a wide range, and refunds up to a fifth of its cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes each trigger unpredictable in three dimensions at once, tilted slightly in your favour on average.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a trigger build that fires often enough for the randomness to average out. Poor if you need consistency.

name: Jagged Ground I
stats: Supported Skills consume an Endurance Charge on Use
Supported Skills create Jagged Ground when consuming an Endurance Charge
Jagged Ground lasts 4 seconds
description: Supports Slam skills. Supported Skills will consume Endurance Charges on use to create Jagged Ground.

beginner.whatItIs: A slam support that consumes an endurance charge on use to create jagged ground lasting four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a defensive charge into ground control, which is a way of spending a resource you may otherwise sit on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slam build that generates endurance charges faster than it needs them for defence.

name: Jagged Ground II
stats: Aftershocks caused by Supported Skills create Jagged Ground
Jagged Ground lasts 4 seconds
description: Supports Slam skills. Aftershocks caused by Supported Slam Skills always create patches of Jagged Ground.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, where aftershocks from your slams always create jagged ground with no charge spent.
beginner.whyItMatters: It costs you no resource at all, so the ground appears as a free consequence of slamming rather than a trade.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Better than the first version on any slam build that already causes aftershocks.

name: Kalisa's Crescendo
stats: Enemies affected by Curses from Supported Skills are Pacified for the final 30% of Supported Curse's duration
Enemies Pacified this way cannot be Pacified again for 8 seconds
description: Supports Curse Skills. Enemies Cursed by Supported Skills are Pacified for the final portion of the Supported Curse's duration.
flavourText:
"Her voice reached into my chest and plucked my beating
heart from its cage. By the wide, glistening eyes of my
fellow punters, I knew that they felt it, too."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage curse support that pacifies cursed enemies for the last 30% of the curse's duration, with an eight second gap before the same enemy can be pacified again.
beginner.whyItMatters: It attaches a window of safety to the end of every curse, so curses become crowd control as well as a debuff.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a curse build that wants breathing room in a fight rather than simply more damage.

name: Kaom's Madness
stats: Supported Skills create 3 additional fissures
Supported Skills deal 20% less Damage
Supported Skills have 20% less Skill Speed
Supported Skills have 30% less Area of Effect
description: Supports Skills which create fissures in the ground, causing them to create many additional fissures at the cost of damage, speed, and area of effect.
flavourText:
As King Kaom delved further into Wraeclast, so, too, did he
draw closer to the Beast. One night, in a nightmarish fit, he
swung his axe at his own men, slaughtering hundreds.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for fissure skills, creating three extra fissures at the cost of 20% damage, 20% skill speed and 30% area of effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades quality for quantity, covering far more ground with weaker, slower cracks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing wide areas with fissures. Against a single target the extra fissures do nothing and the penalties all apply.

name: Khatal's Rejuvenation
stats: Remnants created by Supported Skills grant Khatal's Rejuvenation when collected
description: Supports Skills that generate Remnants. Picking up Remnants from Supported Skills grants Khatal's Rejuvenation.
flavourText:
The surging geysers flooded the tunnels of the ancient
enemy, destroying whole legions. His akhara turned to
praise the tale-man Khatal, but he was dust on the wind.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for remnant skills, granting Khatal's Rejuvenation whenever you pick up one of the remnants it created.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns collecting remnants, which you were doing anyway, into a recurring buff on yourself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a remnant build that generates and collects them steadily throughout a fight.

name: Knockback
stats: Supported Skills Knock Enemies Back on Hit
Supported Skills have 40% more Knockback Distance
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to Knock Back enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that knocks enemies back on hit, with 40% more knockback distance than normal.
beginner.whyItMatters: Pushing enemies away buys you space, which is defence for a character who cannot afford to be surrounded.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good for fragile ranged builds. It works against you in melee, where you have to chase what you just pushed.

name: Kulemak's Dominion
stats: Spells you cast which affect an area around you or a targeted location also affect an area around Supported Offerings
Spells deal 50% less damage when affecting areas around Offerings this way
description: Supports Offering Skills, causing your Cascadable Spells to Cascade to the locations of Supported Offerings.
flavourText:
Still a shadow of his former self, Kulemak turned to deception.
He promised Ahn untold power and mastery, in exchange for
a single golem. "After all, what harm could one servant do?"

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage offering support that makes your cascadable spells also cascade to wherever your offerings are, at 50% less damage in those extra areas.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets one cast cover several places at once, using your offerings as remote casting points.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster running offerings across the field. Without offerings placed there is nowhere for the spell to cascade to.

name: Kurgal's Leash
stats: Gain Unholy Might for 15 seconds on Commanding Minions from Supported Skills
Minions from Supported Skills gain Unholy Might for 15 seconds when Commanded
description: Supports Commandable Minions causing you and the Supported Minion to gain Unholy Might when you Command them.
flavourText:
Kurgal's first body was a mere stone golem, enslaved by a
collar. He found such ecstasy in the power of dominion,
he clawed his way free... and soon, supplanted a Lich Lord.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for commandable minions. Commanding one grants both you and that minion unholy might for fifteen seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes commanding a minion a buff for you as well as them, so the button is worth pressing even when the command itself is minor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build that uses commands actively rather than leaving minions to fight on their own.

name: Last Gasp
stats: Minions from Supported Skills die 4 seconds after their Life is reduced to 0
description: Supports Skills that create Persistent Minions, causing those Minions to fight on when they are fatally wounded, dying after a short duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent minions that lets them fight on for four seconds after their life reaches zero.
beginner.whyItMatters: Four extra seconds of a minion attacking is often enough to finish the pack that killed it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For minion builds in dangerous content where minions die faster than you can replace them.

name: Lasting Ground
stats: 50% increased duration of Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills that create Ground Surfaces, causing those surfaces to last longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving ground surfaces you create 50% increased duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ground surfaces only work while they exist, so extending them is the direct way to get more out of each cast.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that fights on top of surfaces it laid down, rather than one that runs past them.

name: Lasting Shock
stats: Supported Skills have 100% increased Shock Duration
Supported Skills have 30% less chance to Shock
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies or inflicts Shock, causing its Shocks to be inflicted less often but last longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A support doubling shock duration while cutting your chance to shock by 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shock raises the damage everything takes, so a longer shock from fewer applications suits slow, heavy hitters.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that lands one big lightning hit. On a rapid skill the lost shock chance costs more than the duration returns.

name: Life Bounty
stats: Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 100% more Life Flask Charges
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing enemies it kills to grant more Life Flask charges.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that doubles the life flask charges you gain from enemies the skill kills.
beginner.whyItMatters: It focuses entirely on your healing flask, which is the resource that decides whether a bad moment kills you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that leans on life flasks and clears enough monsters to keep them charged.

name: Life Drain
stats: Recover 12% of maximum Life over four seconds when Supported Skills Cull an Enemy
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing you to recover Life when it Culls an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that recovers 12% of your maximum life over four seconds whenever the skill culls an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pairs finishing off rares with a substantial heal, so the end of a dangerous fight is also where you recover from it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that already has culling. Without a culling source there is nothing to trigger the heal.

name: Life Leech I
stats: Leech 12% of Physical Attack Damage from Supported Skills as Life
description: Supports Attacks, causing their Physical damage to Leech Life.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that leeches 12% of the skill's physical attack damage back as life.
beginner.whyItMatters: Leech turns attacking into healing, which is the most reliable form of recovery for a melee character in a long fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any physical attack build. It gives nothing to a skill that deals no physical damage.

name: Life Leech II
stats: Leech 16% of Physical Attack Damage from Supported Skills as Life
description: Supports Attacks, causing their Physical damage to Leech Life.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger leech support, recovering 16% of the skill's physical attack damage as life.
beginner.whyItMatters: A third more healing from the same swings means you can hold your ground in fights the first version could not carry.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once you are taking enough damage that the first version's healing no longer keeps pace.

name: Life Leech III
stats: Leech 16% of Physical Attack Damage from Supported Skills as Life
Life Leeched by Supported Skills is not removed at full Life
description: Supports Attacks, causing their Physical damage to Leech Life and preventing Leech gained this way from being removed at full Life.

beginner.whatItIs: The final leech support: the same 16% recovery, and the leech is no longer cancelled when you reach full life.
beginner.whyItMatters: Leech that survives being at full life keeps working through a spike of damage, which is exactly when the earlier versions cut out.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for a physical build that takes damage in sudden bursts rather than a steady trickle.

name: Lifetap
stats: Supported Skills have Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs
description: Supports any Skill, turning its Mana cost into a Life cost. Does not support Skills which reserve Spirit.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that converts the skill's mana cost into a life cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: It frees you from mana entirely on that skill, at the price of paying for it out of the resource that keeps you alive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with strong life recovery and a permanent mana shortage. It does not work on skills reserving spirit.

name: Lightning Attunement
stats: Gain 25% of Damage as extra Lightning Damage
Supported Skills deal 50% less Cold and Fire Damage
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, causing them to Gain Lightning Damage but deal less Cold and Fire Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support adding a quarter of your damage again as lightning damage while halving cold and fire damage dealt.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lightning shocks, which raises the damage everything else does, so this converts raw output into amplification.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning-focused build. On a skill dealing all three elements it removes more than it adds.

name: Lightning Exposure
stats: Supported Skills inflict Exposure for 8 seconds on Shocking a target
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to inflict Exposure when inflicting Shock.

beginner.whatItIs: A support applying exposure for eight seconds whenever the skill shocks an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shock and exposure stack differently, so this makes an already-shocked target take considerably more from every follow-up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that shocks reliably. It never fires on a skill that cannot shock.

name: Lightning Mastery
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Lightning Skills
description: Supports Lightning skills, granting them an additional level. Does not support skills which do not have levels.

beginner.whatItIs: A support granting a lightning skill one extra gem level.
beginner.whyItMatters: One level lifts the whole skill at once, which is usually a wider gain than any single modifier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A dependable pick in a lightning build. Skills without levels gain nothing.

name: Lightning Penetration
stats: Supported Skills Penetrate 30% Lightning Resistance
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making those Hits Penetrate enemy Lightning resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: A support making the skill's hits penetrate 30% of enemy lightning resistance.
beginner.whyItMatters: In later content, resistance is the main thing blunting your damage, and penetration attacks it directly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it once you reach content where enemies resist lightning heavily.

name: Living Lightning I
stats: Trigger Living Lightning on dealing Lightning Damage with Supported Skill
Living Lightning
Cooldown Time: (0.20 s (5 Times))
This Skill is Triggered on dealing Lightning Damage with Supported Skill
Creates 1 Minion
Level of Minions is based on Level of Triggering Skill
Minion duration is 30 seconds
Limit 5 Minions
Minions convert 100% of Physical damage to Lightning damage
Minions Attack every 0.14 seconds
Minions disperse after 3 Attacks
description: Supports Skills which cause Damaging Hits. Living Lightning Minions are created when dealing Lightning damage with Supported Skills - bundles of living electricity that target nearby enemies with Chaining Attacks. Enemies will not directly engage these Minions, and can pass through them. Does not modify skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that spawns a living lightning minion whenever the skill deals lightning damage. Up to five exist at once, each attacking rapidly and dispersing after three attacks. Enemies ignore them and pass through.
beginner.whyItMatters: It adds a stream of free attackers that cost nothing to maintain and cannot be killed by the enemy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that hits often enough to keep the limit topped up.

name: Living Lightning II
stats: Trigger Living Lightning on dealing Lightning Damage with Supported Skill
Living Lightning
Cooldown Time: (0.20 s (5 Times))
Minions from this skill have 1% increased Attack Speed per 10 of your Dexterity
Minions from this skill have 1% increased Damage per 5 of your Strength
This Skill is Triggered on dealing Lightning Damage with Supported Skill
Creates 1 Minion
Level of Minions is based on Level of Triggering Skill
Minion duration is 30 seconds
Limit 8 Minions
Minions convert 100% of Physical damage to Lightning damage
Minions Attack every 0.14 seconds
Minions disperse after 3 Attacks
description: Supports Skills which cause Damaging Hits. Living Lightning Minions are created when dealing Lightning damage with Supported Skills - bundles of living electricity that target nearby enemies with Chaining Attacks. Enemies will not directly engage these Minions, and can pass through them. Does not modify skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, allowing eight living lightning minions at once and scaling their attack speed off your dexterity and their damage off your strength.
beginner.whyItMatters: More of them at once and a link to your own attributes turns a small bonus into a real second damage source.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it as soon as you can, and prioritise it if your character already carries high strength or dexterity.

name: Lockdown
stats: Supported Skills have 120% more Pin Buildup against enemies within 2 metres of you, scaling to no change at 12 metres
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing any Pin buildup it inflicts to be stronger the closer the enemy is to you.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 120% more pin buildup against enemies within two metres, fading to nothing at twelve metres.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes pinning practical at melee range, where pinning is most useful because the enemy is already on top of you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a melee build using pin as control. It is almost worthless at range.

name: Long Fuse I
stats: Supported Skills have 50% increased Detonation Time
Grenades from Supported Skills cannot explode before the end of their Detonation Time
Detonations from supported Skills deal 30% more Damage
description: Supports Skills which have a Detonation Time, causing those Skills to have much higher Detonation Time and detonation damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that lengthens detonation time by half, stops grenades exploding early, and gives detonations 30% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer fuse is the price for a much bigger blast, and forcing grenades to run their full timer makes the delay predictable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For throwing grenades ahead of a pack you know is coming. Poor when you need something to explode right now.

name: Long Fuse II
stats: Supported Skills have 70% increased Detonation Time
Grenades from Supported Skills cannot explode before the end of their Detonation Time
Detonations from supported Skills deal 35% more Damage
description: Supports Skills which have a Detonation Time, causing those Skills to have much higher Detonation Time and detonation damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, with a 70% longer detonation time and 35% more detonation damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pushes further in the same direction: a longer wait for a bigger explosion.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a grenade build that plants ahead of a fight rather than reacting inside one.

name: Longshot I
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% more Attack Damage to enemies further than 7 metres from you, scaling down to no bonus at 3.5 metres or closer
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more damage from farther away.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support giving 25% more damage to enemies more than seven metres away, fading to nothing within three and a half metres.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays a ranged character for keeping the distance they wanted to keep anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For bow and crossbow builds. It gives melee nothing at all.

name: Longshot II
stats: Supported Skills deal 35% more Attack Damage to enemies further than 7 metres from you, scaling down to no bonus at 3.5 metres or closer
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to deal more damage from farther away.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger distance support, raising the far-range bonus to 35% more attack damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A larger bonus makes holding your distance worth more than closing in for a safer shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once available, provided you are genuinely fighting beyond seven metres most of the time.

name: Loyalty
stats: 10% of Damage from Hits is taken from Supported Companion's Life before you
Minions from Supported Skills have 30% less maximum Life
description: Supports Skills that create Companions which can be damaged. Minions created by Supported Skills take a portion of Hit Damage you would otherwise have taken, but have lowered maximum Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where your companion absorbs a tenth of the hit damage you would have taken, in exchange for 30% less maximum life of its own.
beginner.whyItMatters: It moves damage off you and onto a minion, which is a defensive layer paid for with something replaceable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with a companion you can resummon. It is a poor trade if losing the companion costs you a long recast.

name: Magnetic Remnants
stats: Remnants created by Supported Skills can be collected from 35% further away
description: Supports Skills which create Remnants, allowing those Remnants to be collected from further away.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that widens the range at which you can pick up remnants the skill made, by 35%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the walking that remnant builds otherwise spend time on, which keeps you fighting instead of tidying up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any remnant build where pickups are falling out of reach.

name: Magnified Area I
stats: Supported Skills have 35% increased Area of Effect
description: Supports any skill with an area of effect, making it larger.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 35% increased area of effect with no drawback.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider area means each cast catches more of a pack, which is the simplest way to clear faster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An easy pick on any area skill used for clearing. Less useful on a single-target skill.

name: Magnified Area II
stats: Supported Skills have 45% increased Area of Effect
description: Supports any skill with an area of effect, making it larger.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger area support, giving 45% increased area of effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: Still no drawback, just more coverage, which keeps it one of the least demanding supports to slot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier version once your gem tier allows; there is nothing to weigh up.

name: Maim
stats: Supported Attacks always Maim on Hit
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to Maim enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support that always maims enemies on hit, slowing them down.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slowed enemies reach you later and leave your area skills sooner, which is defence and damage at the same time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any attack build that wants control from its ordinary hits without spending a skill slot on it.

name: Malady
stats: Chance to inflict Bleeding with Supported Skills is calculated from their base chance to Poison instead
Chance to Poison with Supported Skills is calculated from their base chance to inflict Bleeding instead
description: Supports Skills which can cause Damaging Hits, causing base chance to inflict Bleeding with Supported Skills to instead apply to base chance to Poison, and causing base chance to Poison to instead apply to Bleeding.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that swaps the skill's base chances around: its bleed chance is calculated from its poison chance, and its poison chance from its bleed chance.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a skill built to cause one ailment cause the other instead, which opens up skills your build could not otherwise use.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When a skill you like has the wrong ailment attached for your build. It does nothing if the skill has neither chance.

name: Mana Bounty
stats: Enemies killed by Hits from Supported Skills grant 100% more Mana Flask Charges
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing enemies it kills to grant more Mana Flask charges.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that doubles the mana flask charges gained from enemies the skill kills.
beginner.whyItMatters: It keeps a caster's mana flask topped up through clearing, so you rarely reach a fight with an empty one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a mana-hungry build that clears packs steadily.

name: Mana Flare
stats: Support
Supported Skills trigger Mana Flare on Critical Hit
Mana Flare
Cooldown Time: 1.00 sec
Cast Time: 1.00 sec
Critical Hit Chance: 7.00%
Consumes 25% of current Mana to deal that much Fire damage
Flare radius is 2 metres
description: Supports any Spell that Hits enemies, causing it to trigger a Mana Flare on Critical Hit. The Mana Flare consumes your Mana to deal Fire damage. Cannot support the skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support that triggers a mana flare on a critical hit, consuming a quarter of your current mana to deal that much fire damage in an area.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts your mana pool directly into burst damage, so a large pool becomes an offensive stat.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-mana critical caster. On a low-mana build the flare barely registers.

name: Mana Leech
stats: Leech 8% of Physical Attack Damage from Supported Skills as Mana
description: Supports Attacks, causing their Physical damage to Leech Mana.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support leeching 8% of the skill's physical attack damage back as mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: It solves mana sustain through attacking rather than through gear, which frees up other parts of your build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical attacker running expensive skills. It gives nothing to a skill with no physical damage.

name: Mark for Death I
stats: Hits against targets Marked by Supported Skills Break Armour equal to 10% of Physical damage dealt
description: Supports Mark Skills. Enemies affected by Supported Marks will have their Armour Broken by Physical Damage they take.

beginner.whatItIs: A mark support where any physical damage a marked enemy takes breaks 10% of that damage as armour.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a mark do armour breaking passively, including from your allies and minions, rather than needing you to strip it yourself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical build fighting armoured bosses, where marking the target sets up everything that follows.

name: Mark for Death II
stats: Hits against targets Marked by Supported Skills Break Armour equal to 15% of Physical damage dealt
description: Supports Mark Skills. Enemies affected by Supported Marks will have their Armour Broken by Physical Damage they take.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, breaking 15% of physical damage taken as armour on marked targets.
beginner.whyItMatters: The higher rate strips a boss's armour noticeably faster from the same amount of fighting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move to it once you are fighting bosses whose armour the first version was stripping too slowly.

name: Mark of Siphoning I
stats: Enemies Marked by Supported Skills cause you to Leech Mana equal to 8% of Physical Attack Damage they take from your Hits
description: Supports Mark Skills, causing enemies they Mark to Leech Mana to you when you Hit them with Attacks.

beginner.whatItIs: A mark support where hitting a marked enemy with attacks leeches mana to you equal to 8% of the physical damage it takes.
