beginner.whyItMatters: It ties mana recovery to a target you were focusing anyway, which is a clean fix for casting between attacks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical attacker who marks a boss and fights it for a long time.

name: Mark of Siphoning II
stats: Enemies Marked by Supported Skills cause you to Leech Mana equal to 8% of Physical Attack Damage they take from your Hits
Enemies Marked by Supported Skills cause you to Leech Life equal to 8% of Physical Attack Damage they take from your Hits
description: Supports Mark Skills, causing enemies they Mark to Leech Life and Mana to you when you Hit them with Attacks.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, leeching both life and mana at 8% of the physical damage a marked enemy takes from your hits.
beginner.whyItMatters: Adding life leech on the same condition turns a mana fix into a survivability fix as well.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it over the earlier one when survivability, not just mana, is what your marked fights are testing.

name: Meat Shield I
stats: Minions from Supported Skills deal 35% less Damage
Minions from Supported Skills take 35% less Damage
description: Supports skills which create Minions, granting them less damage taken but making them deal less damage. Cannot support skills which create undamageable Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support where minions take 35% less damage and deal 35% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts minions from attackers into a wall, which is what you want if their job is standing between you and the enemy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build where your minions block rather than kill. Avoid it if the minions are your damage.

name: Meat Shield II
stats: Minions from Supported Skills deal 40% less Damage
Minions from Supported Skills take 40% less Damage
description: Supports skills which create Minions, granting them less damage taken but making them deal less damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, with minions taking and dealing 40% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The deeper trade makes minions harder still to kill, at the cost of nearly half of what they contribute offensively.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a purely defensive minion setup where survival is all you need from them.

name: Medved's Felling
stats: Lose 1% of Maximum Life per 5 Rage when you use Supported Skills
Supported Skills grant 10% of Maximum Rage on Melee hit
Supported Skills have 5% increased Attack Speed per 5 Rage
description: Supports Melee Attacks you use yourself, causing them to attack faster the more Rage you have and grant Rage on Hit, but also making you lose Life based on your Rage when using them.
flavourText:
"There is no zealotry like that of a mystic roused
to battle. He broke his own code, wielding weapons
long forbidden, to defend that which he loved."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage melee support that grants rage on hit, attacks 5% faster for every five rage you hold, and costs you 1% of maximum life per five rage each time you use it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes rage a double-edged resource, speeding you up and draining you at the same rate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage build with strong life recovery. Without recovery, high rage becomes lethal to you rather than the enemy.

name: Minion Instability
stats: Minions from Supported Skills explode when reduced to Low Life, dealing 15% of their maximum Life as Fire Damage to surrounding Enemies
description: Supports skills which create Minions, causing them to violently explode when reduced to Low Life.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support where minions explode for 15% of their maximum life as fire damage once they drop to low life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes a dying minion useful, which suits a swarm build where minions are always dying anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For cheap, numerous minions. It wastes a slot on a build with one durable companion.

name: Minion Mastery
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Minion Skills
description: Supports Minion skills, granting them an additional level. Does not support skills which do not have levels.

beginner.whatItIs: A support granting a minion skill one extra gem level.
beginner.whyItMatters: A level raises minion life and damage together, which is broader than adding one or the other.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A dependable pick in any minion build. Skills without levels gain nothing.

name: Minion Pact I
stats: Supported Skills remove 100% of your maximum Life from a nearby Minion on use to deal 30% more damage
description: Supports damaging skills you use yourself, draining the life from one of your Minions on use in order to boost the skill's damage. Only takes effect if you have a Minion with enough life to drain the full amount.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that drains life from a nearby minion equal to your own maximum life each use, in exchange for 30% more damage. It only works if a minion has enough life to give.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts your minions into fuel for your own damage, which is a very different use for them than fighting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with high-life minions you can afford to burn. With small minions the condition often fails silently.

name: Minion Pact II
stats: Supported Skills remove 150% of your maximum Life from a nearby Minion on use to deal 35% more damage
description: Supports damaging skills you use yourself, draining the life from one of your Minions on use in order to boost the skill's damage. Only takes effect if you have a Minion with enough life to drain the full amount.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, draining one and a half times your maximum life from a minion for 35% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The larger drain demands tougher minions, so it narrows which builds can meet the condition at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only with substantial minions. On a thin minion pool the skill simply gets no bonus.

name: Minion Splash I
stats: Supported Minions' Strikes have Melee Splash
description: Supports Skills which create Minions which Strike, causing those Minions' Strikes to have Melee Splash.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving your minions' strikes melee splash, so their attacks damage enemies around the target.
beginner.whyItMatters: Minions that hit one target at a time clear packs slowly, and splash fixes that without any change to their damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a striking minion build clearing groups.

name: Minion Splash II
stats: Minions have 20% increased Area of Effect
Supported Minions' Strikes have Melee Splash
description: Supports Skills which create Minions which Strike, increasing their Area of Effect and causing those Minions' Strikes to have Melee Splash.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, adding melee splash plus 20% increased minion area of effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: The wider area means the splash reaches further, catching enemies that were standing just clear of it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth swapping in once packs are spread widely enough that plain splash keeps missing the edges.

name: Mobility
stats: 25% less Movement Speed penalty while using Supported Skills
description: Supports skills that can be used while moving, allowing you to move faster while using them.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that reduces the movement speed penalty of skills usable while moving by 25%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Moving while attacking is how a fragile character survives, and this makes the movement half of that actually fast.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a kiting build. It gives nothing to a skill that roots you in place.

name: Momentum
stats: After moving at least 2 metres during a single use of a Supported Skill, the rest of that use deals 40% more Damage
description: Supports any damaging skill that you use yourself, causing it to deal more damage if you move a sufficient distance while using the skill. Teleportation does not count towards the distance travelled.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 40% more damage for the remainder of a use once you have moved two metres during it. Teleporting does not count.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards attacking on the move rather than standing still, which suits skills you can walk through.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a mobile attacker with a skill that lasts long enough to move during it.

name: Morgana's Tempest
stats: Supported Skills have 25% less area of effect
Supported Skills have 35% less damage
Supported Skills have 60% more Storm travel speed
Supported Storm Skills have +1 to Limit
Supported Skills originate from the player and move towards the target location
description: Supports Storm skills, increasing their Limit and causing them to move quickly from the user to the target location, but become less effective. Cannot Support Triggered Skills.
flavourText:
On the nights the fugue would come over her, the Ezomytes would
gather below, begging her to bring the rains. Atop the Taisce,
wailing with unknown sorrows, her cries made the skies rage.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage storm support that raises the storm limit by one and makes storms travel 60% faster from you to the target, at the cost of 25% area and 35% damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades power for reach and speed, so your storms arrive quickly and you can have more of them running.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a storm build that wants coverage across a fight rather than one heavy storm on a target.

name: Mórrigan's Insight
stats: Supported Skills trigger Nature's Exchange when Consuming Freeze
Supported Skills cannot cause Freeze buildup
Supported Skills Consume Freeze on enemies to deal 50% more Damage
Buff duration is 8 seconds
Grants (16-531) Guard
Grants (3-106) to (5-159) Cold Thorns damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing them to deal more damage and trigger Nature's Exchange when consuming Freeze on enemies. Cannot support skills that Consume Freeze.
flavourText:
"Wild energy is as misunderstood as the Mórrigan
itself. Many revere life, yet revile death. What is dead
feeds the living. Death is but one aspect of the whole."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that stops the skill building freeze, and instead consumes existing freeze for 50% more damage while triggering Nature's Exchange, which grants guard and cold thorns for eight seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays out both offensively and defensively from the same freeze, which is unusual for a payoff support.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only alongside a separate freezing skill. It cannot create the freezes it needs to spend.

name: Multishot I
stats: Supported Skills deal 35% less Damage
Supported Skills fire 2 additional Projectiles
Supported Skills have 20% less Skill Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making them fire extra Projectiles. Also lowers Attack and Cast speed of supported skills, as well as lessening their damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support firing two extra projectiles, at the cost of 35% damage and 20% skill speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Three projectiles instead of one covers far more of a pack, which is usually worth more than the damage each one loses.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing with a projectile skill. Against a single target the extra projectiles often miss entirely.

name: Multishot II
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% less Damage
Supported Skills fire 2 additional Projectiles
Supported Skills have 20% less Skill Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making them fire extra Projectiles. Also lowers Attack and Cast speed of supported skills, as well as lessening their damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, with the damage penalty reduced from 35% to 25% for the same two extra projectiles.
beginner.whyItMatters: Keeping more damage per projectile means the spread still kills tougher monsters rather than only weak ones.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once the first version's penalty is leaving tougher monsters alive.

name: Murderous Intent
stats: Skills Empowered by Supported Skills have Culling Strike
description: Supports skills that can Empower skills other than themselves, causing skills they Empower to Cull enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that gives culling strike to skills empowered by the supported skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: It spreads a finishing effect across everything your empowering skill touches, rather than to one attack.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build using an empowering skill in front of several attacks, especially in content full of rare monsters.

name: Muster
stats: Supported Minions deal 7% more damage for each different type of Reviving Minion you have summoned
description: Supports Skills which summon Minions. Supported Minions deal more Damage the more different kinds of Reviving Minions you have summoned.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support giving 7% more minion damage for every different kind of reviving minion you have summoned.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards variety rather than volume, which is the opposite of how most minion builds are put together.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build deliberately running several different reviving minion types at once.

name: Mysticism I
stats: Deal 30% increased Spell Damage while on full Energy Shield while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to deal increased Spell Damage while on full Energy Shield while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs giving 30% increased spell damage while you are on full energy shield.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards keeping your shield untouched, which pushes a caster toward avoiding damage rather than absorbing it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an energy shield caster that recharges quickly between packs.

name: Mysticism II
stats: Deal 40% increased Spell Damage while on full Energy Shield while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to deal increased Spell Damage while on full Energy Shield while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 40% increased spell damage while at full energy shield.
beginner.whyItMatters: The larger bonus makes maintaining a full shield worth building around rather than a nice condition to meet.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it once your energy shield recharges fast enough that you are usually at full.

name: Neural Overload
stats: Supported Skills Electrocute Primed enemies on Hit
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies. Nearby enemies are marked when they are Primed for Electrocution, and hitting a marked enemy with a supported skill will Electrocute them.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that marks nearby enemies primed for electrocution, and electrocutes them when the supported skill hits.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes electrocution something you apply on purpose rather than something that builds up on its own schedule.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that wants to lock down specific dangerous enemies.

name: Nimble Reload
stats: Supported Skills have 60% increased Crossbow Reload Speed
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, causing them to Reload bolts significantly faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A crossbow support giving 60% increased reload speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reloading is dead time where a crossbow character does nothing, and this is the most direct way to shorten it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any crossbow skill whose reload interrupts your rhythm, especially heavy ones with slow reloads.

name: Nova Projectiles I
stats: Supported Skills fire Projectiles in a circle
description: Supports Projectile Skills, making them fire Projectiles in a circle. Does not Support Skills which rain down Projectiles from above.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support that fires the skill's projectiles in a full circle around you instead of forward.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers every direction at once, which suits being surrounded rather than facing a line of enemies.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that gets encircled. It wastes most of its projectiles when everything is in front of you.

name: Nova Projectiles II
stats: Supported Skills fire 6 additional Projectiles
Supported Skills fire Projectiles in a circle
Supported Skills deal 50% less Damage
description: Supports Projectile Skills, making them fire extra Projectiles in a circle, at the cost of Damage and gaining a cooldown. Does not Support Skills which rain down Projectiles from above. Cannot Support Skills which already have a cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version: six additional projectiles fired in a circle, at 50% less damage and with a cooldown added.
beginner.whyItMatters: It becomes an occasional burst covering the whole area around you rather than something you can repeat freely.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing a pack that has closed in. The cooldown makes it unsuitable as your main attack.

name: Oisín's Oath
stats: Mana Leech from Supported Skills recovers based on Elemental Damage Types instead of Physical Damage
description: Supports Skills which Hit enemies, causing their Mana Leech to recover based on Elemental damage instead of Physical damage.
flavourText: The first Warden of Eaves swore to patrol the border twixt the worlds forevermore, so that the tragedy of Gruthkul's stampede would never recur. In time, his vigil on the edge began to... change him.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that makes the skill's mana leech recover from elemental damage instead of physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Mana leech normally requires physical damage, which locks elemental builds out of it entirely; this opens that door.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an elemental build that wants leech-based mana sustain without carrying physical damage it does not use.

name: Olroth's Conviction
stats: Supported Skills Gain 100% of Life and Mana Cost as Extra Runic Ward Cost
Supported Skills Empower 2 additional Skill uses
description: Supports skills that can Empower a specific number of other skills, causing them to apply to more skill uses.
flavourText:
The Empty-Eyed Fiend emerged from darkness.
Olroth raised his sword, gem in its pommel.
The Fiend smiled. Olroth swung.
Its head rolled, sockets ablaze with delight.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that empowers two additional skill uses, at the cost of the skill also consuming runic ward equal to its life and mana cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: More empowered uses stretch an expensive buff across more of a fight, paid for out of your ward rather than your mana.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with runic ward to spare and an empowering skill it wants to reach further.

name: Olroth's Hubris
stats: Physical Damage from Hits also Contributes to Freeze Buildup
Supported Skills cost an additional 20% of maximum Runic Ward
Supported Skills deal added Cold damage equal to 15% of Runic Ward cost
Supported Skills deal added Physical damage equal to 15% of Runic Ward cost
description: Supports Attacks you use or Trigger yourself, causing them to cost Runic Ward to use but deal additional Physical and Cold damage based on their Runic Ward cost, in addition to causing Physical damage to Contribute to Freeze buildup. Cannot Support Channelling Skills, Sustained Skills, or Skills without a cost.
flavourText:
The gem warmed his palm. "Our fear of this
power cost many lives. No longer!" With his own
hands, Olroth sealed that expedition's demise.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage attack support costing an extra 20% of your maximum runic ward, adding physical and cold damage worth 15% of that cost each, and letting physical damage contribute to freeze buildup.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a defensive resource into damage and control at once, which is a heavy commitment of your ward.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a runic ward build that regenerates ward quickly and wants to freeze with physical hits.

name: Opening Move
stats: Supported Skills Daze when Hitting enemies that are on full life
description: Supports Travel Skills which Hit enemies. Hits with Supported Skills against enemies on full life will Daze.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for travel skills that dazes enemies on full life when you hit them.
beginner.whyItMatters: Dazing as you arrive interrupts whatever the pack was about to do, which makes charging into a group much safer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that opens fights with a movement skill rather than approaching on foot.

name: Overabundance I
stats: Supported Skills have +1 to Limit
Supported Skills have 50% less Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports Skills which have a Limit, increasing that Limit at the cost of their duration. Only applies to restrictions that use the word "Limit".

beginner.whatItIs: A support raising the skill's limit by one while cutting its effect duration in half.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets you have one more of something at once, provided each one lasting half as long is an acceptable price.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that recasts constantly. It hurts anything you place and want to leave standing.

name: Overabundance II
stats: Supported Skills have +1 to Limit
Supported Skills have 40% less Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports Skills which have a Limit, increasing that Limit at the cost of their duration. Only applies to restrictions that use the word "Limit".

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, raising the limit by one with only a 40% duration cut instead of 50%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The smaller duration loss makes the extra object noticeably more worthwhile.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in whenever the extra object is worth having; the shorter duration cut makes it easier to justify.

name: Overcharge
stats: 50% increased Magnitude of Shocks inflicted with Supported Skills
Shocks caused by Supported Skills are reflected back to you
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making its Shocks more effective but reflecting them back to you as well.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 50% increased shock magnitude, with those shocks also reflected back onto you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stronger shocks raise the damage everything takes, but taking your own shock means you are amplifying incoming damage too.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that can shrug off being shocked. It is dangerous on a fragile character.

name: Overreach
stats: Supported Skills have 40% increased Area of Effect
Supported Skills have 80% less Accuracy Rating against Enemies within two metres
description: Supports Attack Skills which deal Damage in an Area. Supported Skills have significantly increased Area of Effect, but are less Accurate against nearby targets.

beginner.whatItIs: An area attack support giving 40% increased area of effect, with 80% less accuracy against enemies within two metres.
beginner.whyItMatters: It widens your swing at the cost of reliably hitting anything standing right on top of you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an attacker who fights at the edge of their reach. Terrible if enemies routinely close inside two metres.

name: Paquate's Pact
stats: Supported SKills Cost 10% of maximum Life for each time they have been used or Triggered Recently, up to a maximum of 30%
Supported Skills Trigger Twisted Pact for each enemy in range
Twisted Pact
Level: (1-20)
This Skill will copy the Level of the Gem it is Socketed in
Cost: 0 Mana
Covers the target in large quantities of Corrupted Blood which severely damages them.
Inflicts 5 Corrupted Blood Debuffs
Corrupted Blood deals (7-339.1) Physical damage per second
Corrupted Blood duration is 5 seconds
description: Supports Warcries, Triggering Twisted Pact to inflict Corrupted Blood on enemies in their area of effect, at the cost of your Life.
flavourText:
The water used to cool the Locus of Corruption ran red
as blood, bright as flame, and bubbled with strange heat.
"Drink," he offered. "Suffuse your flesh with power!"

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage warcry support that triggers Twisted Pact on every enemy in range, applying five stacks of corrupted blood, and costs 10% of your maximum life per recent use, up to 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a warcry into heavy area damage over time, with a rising life cost that punishes shouting too often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a warcry build with strong recovery that opens fights with one shout rather than several.

name: Payload
stats: Supported Skills have 70% reduced Cooldown Recovery Rate
Grenades fired by Supported Skills have 50% chance to activate a second time
description: Supports Skills which fire Grenades, giving fired Grenades a chance to activate again, but lengthening their cooldowns.

beginner.whatItIs: A grenade support giving fired grenades a 50% chance to activate a second time, with 70% reduced cooldown recovery rate.
beginner.whyItMatters: Half your grenades going off twice is a large increase, paid for by being able to throw far less often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a grenade build that plants a few heavy grenades rather than throwing constantly.

name: Perfected Endurance
stats: Gain an Endurance Charge when hitting an Enemy with Supported Skill when Perfectly Timed
description: Supports skills which have a benefit for Perfect Timing. Supported Skills grant at least one Endurance Charge when Hitting an enemy with Perfect Timing.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants an endurance charge whenever you hit an enemy with perfect timing.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards playing the timing mechanic correctly with a defensive charge, so skill at the game turns into survivability.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with a perfect-timing skill you can hit consistently.

name: Perfection
stats: Successfully executing Perfect Timing with Supported Skills grants Perfection
All Perfection is lost on failing to execute any Perfect Timing
description: Supports skills which have a benefit for Perfectly Timing their use. On successfully executing Perfect Timing with Supported Skills, gain Perfection, which is a powerful damage buff. However, failing to execute any Perfect Timing (even with skills not supported by Perfection) will remove all Perfection on you.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants Perfection, a strong damage buff, each time you land a perfect timing. Failing any perfect timing at all, even on another skill, removes all of it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It offers a large reward for playing precisely, and takes the whole stack away for a single mistake anywhere.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a confident player on a build where perfect timing is the core rhythm. Avoid it if you use several timed skills carelessly.

name: Perpetual Charge
stats: Supported Skills have 25% chance to not remove Charges but still count as consuming them
description: Supports skills that consume Power, Frenzy or Endurance Charges on use, giving them a chance not to remove each Charge while still gaining the benefits of consuming them.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving a 25% chance not to remove each charge the skill consumes, while still granting the full benefit of consuming it.
beginner.whyItMatters: A quarter of your charge spending becomes free, so the same generation rate supports noticeably more charge consumption across a fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that regularly consumes power, frenzy or endurance charges as part of its rotation.

name: Persistent Ground I
stats: 50% increased duration of Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills which create Ground Surfaces, causing created Surfaces to last much longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving ground surfaces the skill creates 50% increased duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: A surface that lasts longer keeps working through more of the fight it was laid down for.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that fights on the ground it prepared rather than moving straight past it.

name: Persistent Ground II
stats: 50% increased duration of Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills
Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills cannot be destroyed except by expiring
description: Supports Skills which create Ground Surfaces, causing created Surfaces to last much longer and only end when their duration expires.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved ground-surface support: 50% increased duration, and the surfaces can no longer be destroyed by anything other than running out of time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Indestructible surfaces cannot be cleared away by an enemy effect, so the ground you laid stays yours for the whole fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Choose it wherever enemies or their own surfaces were wiping out the ground you laid.

name: Persistent Ground III
stats: 50% increased duration of Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills
Ground Surfaces from Supported Skills apply Suppressive Ground
Suppressive Ground inflicts 30% less Cooldown Recovery Rate
Ground Surfaces created by Supported Skills cannot be destroyed except by expiring
description: Supports Skills which create Ground Surfaces, causing created Surfaces to last much longer as well as lowering the Cooldown Recovery Speed of affected Enemies. Ground Surfaces from Supported Skills only end when their duration expires.

beginner.whatItIs: The final ground-surface support. Surfaces last 50% longer, cannot be destroyed early, and apply suppressive ground that cuts enemy cooldown recovery by 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slowing enemy cooldowns means the dangerous abilities you are trying to avoid come around less often while they stand on your ground.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for a build that fights on prepared ground, especially against enemies with heavy cooldown abilities.

name: Physical Mastery
stats: +1 to Level of Supported Physical Skills
description: Supports Physical skills, granting them an additional level. Does not support skills which do not have levels.

beginner.whatItIs: A support granting a physical skill one extra gem level.
beginner.whyItMatters: A level lifts every number on the skill together, which is normally a bigger step than any single modifier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A reliable pick in a physical build. Skills with no level get nothing from it.

name: Pierce I
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills Pierce an Enemy
Projectiles from Supported Skills deal 20% less Damage if they've Pierced an enemy
description: Supports Projectile skills, making their Projectiles Pierce an enemy but deal less damage after doing so.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support letting projectiles pierce one enemy, dealing 20% less damage after doing so.
beginner.whyItMatters: Piercing means a shot fired into a line of enemies hits two rather than stopping at the first.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs that line up. Against a single boss the pierce never happens and the penalty never applies.

name: Pierce II
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills Pierce an Enemy
description: Supports Projectile skills, making their Projectiles Pierce an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved pierce support, which pierces one enemy with no damage penalty at all.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra target becomes free rather than paid for, which is a straightforward gain over the first version.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it in place of the version that charges you damage, once your gem tier allows.

name: Pierce III
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills Pierce all Targets
Projectiles from Supported Skills deal 20% less Damage for each Enemy they Pierce
description: Supports Projectile skills, making their Projectiles Pierce an unlimited number of enemies, losing damage as they do so.

beginner.whatItIs: The final pierce support: projectiles pierce everything, losing 20% of their damage for each enemy they pass through.
beginner.whyItMatters: One shot can travel through an entire pack, though by the far end it is doing very little.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For dense lines of weak enemies. The stacking penalty makes it poor against tough monsters standing in a row.

name: Pin I
stats: Modifiers to Stun Buildup for Supported Skills instead apply to Pin Buildup
Supported Skills cannot cause Stun Buildup
Physical Damage from Supported Skill is Pinning
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, allowing its Physical damage to Pin enemies but making it unable to Stun.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that redirects your stun buildup into pin buildup, so physical damage pins instead of stunning.
beginner.whyItMatters: Pin holds an enemy in place rather than briefly interrupting it, which is the stronger form of control against something that keeps charging you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical build that wants enemies stuck rather than staggered. It removes your ability to stun entirely.

name: Pin II
stats: Supported Skills have 50% increased Critical Hit Chance against Immobilised Enemies
Modifiers to Stun Buildup for Supported Skills instead apply to Pin Buildup
Supported Skills cannot cause Stun Buildup
Physical Damage from Supported Skill is Pinning
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, allowing its Physical damage to Pin enemies but making it unable to Stun, as well as granting Critial Hit Chance against Immobilised enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved pin support, which also gives 50% increased critical hit chance against immobilised enemies.
beginner.whyItMatters: Pinning something and then critting it more often means the control step also raises your damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier version once available, and value it higher the more critical hit chance you carry.

name: Pin III
stats: Modifiers to Stun Buildup for Supported Skills instead apply to Pin Buildup
Supported Skills cannot cause Stun Buildup
Physical Damage from Supported Skill is Pinning
Hits with Supported Skills cause 60% less Pin buildup
Pin caused by Supported Skills has 30% more duration
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, allowing its Physical damage to Pin enemies but making it unable to Stun. Pin buildup caused by Supported Skill is lessened, but Pin duration is significantly longer.

beginner.whatItIs: The final pin support: pin buildup is 60% weaker, but the pins that do land last 30% longer.
beginner.whyItMatters: It suits builds that pin rarely but want each pin to hold, rather than ones that pin constantly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy physical hit. On a fast skill the earlier versions apply pin far more often.

name: Pinpoint Critical
stats: Supported Skills have 60% more Critical Hit Chance
Supported Skills have 30% less Critical Damage Bonus
description: Supports any skill that Hits Enemies, causing it to Critically Hit more often but deal less damage with Critical Hits.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 60% more critical hit chance for 30% less critical damage bonus.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades how hard your crits hit for how often they happen, which is right when crits trigger something rather than just dealing damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with on-critical effects. Poor if your crits are simply your damage.

name: Poison I
stats: Supported Skills have 40% chance to Poison on Hit
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to Poison enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving the skill a 40% chance to poison on hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Poison keeps damaging after you have moved on, which is how a build kills several things at once instead of one at a time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An easy early pick on any skill that hits often enough for the chance to pay out.

name: Poison II
stats: Supported Skills have 60% chance to Poison on Hit
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to Poison enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger poison support, raising the chance to poison on hit to 60%.
beginner.whyItMatters: At this rate most of your hits leave poison behind, so poison stacks build fast enough to be your main damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to run while a poison build comes together.

name: Poison III
stats: Supported Skills have 60% chance to Poison on Hit
20% more Magnitude of Poison inflicted by Supported Skills against Bleeding Enemies
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to Poison enemies and causing it to inflict more powerful Poisons against Bleeding Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: The final poison support: the same 60% chance, plus 20% more poison magnitude against bleeding enemies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards running bleed alongside poison, which is a combination many physical chaos builds already have.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Best on a build applying both ailments. If you never cause bleeding, the second version does the same job.

name: Poison Spores
stats: Supported Skills Trigger Toxic Pustule on Hitting an enemy
description: Supports Plant Skills which Hit enemies. Supported Skills Trigger Toxic Pustule on Hitting an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for plant skills that triggers a toxic pustule whenever the skill hits an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives plant skills a chaos payoff on every hit rather than only on the plant's own schedule.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a plant build that also wants poison damage from the same skill.

name: Potent Exposure
stats: Exposure applied by Supported Skills has 20% increased effect
description: Supports Skills which apply Exposure to Enemies, increasing the effect of applied Exposure.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving exposure the skill applies 20% increased effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: Deeper exposure means a bigger resistance reduction, which multiplies everything else you do to that target.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a skill that already applies exposure. It creates none by itself.

name: Practical Magic I
stats: Gain 30% increased Spell damage for 8 seconds on Heavy Stunning an enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills which Hit enemies. Heavy Stunning an enemy with Supported Skills increases your Spell damage for a duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 30% increased spell damage for eight seconds when the skill heavy stuns an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links a heavy attack to your casting, so a hybrid build gets paid for staggering something before it casts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that stuns with a weapon and then follows with spells.

name: Practical Magic II
stats: Gain 40% increased Spell damage for 8 seconds on Heavy Stunning an enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills which Hit enemies. Heavy Stunning an enemy with Supported Skills increases your Spell damage for a duration.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 40% increased spell damage for eight seconds on a heavy stun.
beginner.whyItMatters: The bigger buff makes the stun-then-cast rhythm worth building around rather than a small bonus you notice occasionally.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move to it once your weapon reliably heavy stuns and your spells are doing the killing.

name: Practiced Combo
stats: Supported Strike Skills have a 40% chance to build an additional Combo on Hit
description: Supports Strike Skills. Supported Skills have a chance to build additional Combo on Hit. Cannot support Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A strike support giving a 40% chance to build an extra combo point on hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Combo is what gates your finishers, so building it faster means the payoff comes around more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a melee build that spends combo on a finishing skill.

name: Precision I
stats: 30% Increased Accuracy Rating while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain increased Accuracy while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs granting 30% increased accuracy rating while active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Accuracy applies to all your attacks, not just one skill, so a buff carrying it lifts your whole build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an attack character that misses noticeably. Casters gain nothing from it.

name: Precision II
stats: 50% Increased Accuracy Rating while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain increased Accuracy while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, granting 50% increased accuracy rating while the buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: More accuracy from the same buff slot means fewer wasted swings across everything you do.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap it in once available; more accuracy on a buff slot helps every attack you own.

name: Profanity I
stats: Supported Skills consume a Corpse within 5 metres on use, if possible
Supported Skills deal 30% more
Chaos Damage if consuming a Corpse
description: Supports Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills consume a Corpse on use, dealing more Chaos Damage if they do.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that consumes a corpse within five metres on use, giving 30% more chaos damage when it does.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts the corpses left behind by your own clearing into a damage bonus for the next fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a chaos build fighting where corpses are plentiful. It gives nothing in an empty room.

name: Profanity II
stats: Supported Skills consume up to 10 Corpses within 5 metres on use, if possible
Supported Skills deal 5% more
Chaos Damage for each Corpse consumed this way
description: Supports Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills consume many Corpses on use, dealing more Chaos Damage per Corpse consumed.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, consuming up to ten nearby corpses for 5% more chaos damage each.
beginner.whyItMatters: A full ten corpses is a much larger bonus than the first version, but it needs a battlefield full of bodies.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For dense clearing where corpses pile up. In a boss fight with no adds it will find nothing to eat.

name: Projectile Acceleration I
stats: Supported Skills have 40% more Projectile Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making those Projectiles travel faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support giving 40% more projectile speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster projectiles reach a moving target before it steps out of the way, which is a hit rate increase disguised as a speed one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any projectile skill whose shots feel slow to arrive.

name: Projectile Acceleration II
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills have 40% chance to Pierce an Enemy
Supported Skills have 40% more Projectile Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making those Projectiles travel faster, and granting them a chance to Pierce Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, keeping 40% more projectile speed and adding a 40% chance to pierce an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Piercing added on top means a fast shot also travels through the first target rather than stopping there.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it over the earlier one when you want reach as well as speed out of the same slot.

name: Projectile Acceleration III
stats: Increases and reductions to Projectile speed also apply to Projectile Damage with Supported Skills
Supported Skills have 40% more Projectile Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making those Projectiles travel faster, and causing increases and reductions to Projectile speed to also apply to Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 40% more projectile speed, and any increase or reduction to projectile speed also applies to projectile damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a movement stat into a damage stat, so every point of projectile speed elsewhere in your build counts twice.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that has stacked projectile speed on gear and passives. Without that investment the earlier versions are better.

name: Projectile Deceleration I
stats: Supported Skills have 25% less Projectile Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making those Projectiles travel more slowly.

beginner.whatItIs: A support making projectiles travel 25% more slowly.
beginner.whyItMatters: It exists for skills where a slow projectile lingers longer in the enemy's path, giving more time to hit something.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when the skill benefits from a slow-moving shot. As a general choice it makes you miss more.

name: Projectile Deceleration II
stats: Supported Skills have 30% less Projectile Speed
description: Supports Projectile skills, making those Projectiles travel more slowly.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, making projectiles travel 30% more slowly.
beginner.whyItMatters: The deeper slowdown suits a projectile you want to hang in the air rather than one you want on target quickly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For lingering projectiles used as area denial. Never on a shot you need to land now.

name: Prolonged Duration I
stats: Supported Skills have 30% more Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports any skill that has a duration, making that duration longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving the skill 30% more effect duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: For a buff, a hazard or a lingering effect, longer duration is simply more of what the skill does per cast.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any skill you want to leave running. It works against skills built around fast repetition.

name: Prolonged Duration II
stats: Supported Skills have 35% more Skill Effect Duration
description: Supports any skill that has a duration, making that duration longer.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 35% more effect duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra time means fewer recasts and more of the fight spent doing something other than maintenance.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier version wherever you want a lasting effect to stay up longer between casts.

name: Prototype Seventeen
stats: Supported Skills get 20% increased Critical Hit chance per 5 Rage
Lose all Rage when you deal a Critical Hit with Supported Skills
description: Supports non-Channelling skill you use yourself that Hits enemies, causing it to gain Critical Hit chance based on Rage, but also remove all Rage upon Critically Hitting.
flavourText:
"The murals tell a story of creation, of design... the Precursors
delved into the secrets of life itself. In their war with the Abyssals,
they sought to breed warriors, grown in legions, to fight back..."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support giving 20% increased critical hit chance for every five rage you hold, and removing all your rage the moment the skill lands a critical hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts rage into a rising chance of a critical hit, then resets the meter as soon as that crit lands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage build with a slow skill, where the ramp has time to matter before it is spent.

name: Punch Through
stats: Supported Skills apply Easy Target on Knockback
Easy Target applied this way has a magnitude of 3% per metre of Expected Knockback Distance
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills apply Easy Target when Knocking Back Enemies, causing the next Projectile Attack Hit they take to deal increased Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support applying easy target when you knock an enemy back, so the next projectile attack that hits them lands harder, scaled by how far they flew.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links a melee knockback to a ranged follow-up, which is a combination usually left to two separate characters.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a hybrid build that pushes enemies away and then shoots them, or in a group with a ranged ally.

name: Pursuit I
stats: Supported Skills deal 20% more Melee Damage if you have Damaged an Enemy with a Projectile Attack Hit in the last eight seconds
Supported Skills deal no Projectile damage
description: Supports Melee Attacks. Supported Skills deal more Melee damage if you have struck with a Projectile Attack Hit in the last eight seconds, but cannot themselves deal Projectile Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support giving 20% more melee damage if you have landed a projectile attack in the last eight seconds, while removing the skill's projectile damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards switching between a ranged opener and a melee follow-up, which is how many hybrid weapon builds already play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only in a build that actually fires projectiles. On a pure melee character the condition is never met.

name: Pursuit II
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% more Melee Damage if you have Damaged an Enemy with a Projectile Attack Hit in the last eight seconds
Supported Skills deal no Projectile damage
description: Supports Melee Attacks. Supported Skills deal more Melee damage if you have struck with a Projectile Attack Hit in the last eight seconds, but cannot themselves deal Projectile Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 25% more melee damage under the same eight second projectile condition.
beginner.whyItMatters: More reward for the same rhythm makes the ranged-then-melee pattern worth committing to.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once you have settled into a ranged-then-melee pattern you can keep to.

name: Pursuit III
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more Melee Damage if you have Damaged an Enemy with a Projectile Attack Hit in the last two seconds
Supported Skills deal no Projectile damage
description: Supports Melee Attacks. Supported Skills deal more Melee damage if you have struck with a Projectile Attack Hit in the last two seconds, but cannot themselves deal Projectile Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 30% more melee damage, but the projectile hit must have landed within the last two seconds rather than eight.
beginner.whyItMatters: The tighter window demands you interleave the two attack types closely instead of firing once and forgetting it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that genuinely alternates every couple of seconds. Otherwise the earlier versions are more reliable.

name: Quill Burst
stats: Supported Skills trigger Quill Burst on their next 3 Hits after you Retaliate with Thorns
description:
Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills trigger Quill Burst, which deals your Thorns Damage in an Area around the target struck. Quill Burst can only be triggered on Hit after you've
Retaliated with Thorns Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support that triggers quill burst on your next three hits after you retaliate with thorns, dealing your thorns damage in an area around the target.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a defensive retaliation into three follow-up area attacks, so getting hit becomes the start of your offence.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a thorns build that takes hits deliberately. Without retaliation nothing triggers.

name: Rage I
stats: Supported Skills grant 3 Rage on Melee Hit
description: Supports Melee Attacks, causing them to grant Rage on Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support granting three rage on each melee hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Rage powers a whole family of warrior effects, and this is the plainest way to keep it topped up.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage build with a fast melee attack. Slower attacks build it more slowly.

name: Rage II
stats: Supported Skills grant 5 Rage on Melee Hit
description: Supports Melee Attacks, causing them to grant Rage on Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, granting five rage per melee hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Nearly double the generation means you reach and hold maximum rage in fights the first version could not sustain.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it as soon as you can; faster rage generation feeds every rage-spending effect you own.

name: Rage III
stats: Supported Skills grant 5 Rage on Melee Hit
Supported Skills have 15% increased Attack speed while you are not at maximum Rage
description: Supports Melee Attacks, causing them to grant Rage on Hit. Supported Skills have signficantly higher Attack speed while you or supported minion are not at maximum Rage.

beginner.whatItIs: The final rage support: five rage per melee hit, plus 15% increased attack speed while you are below maximum rage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Attacking faster while short of rage means you reach the cap sooner, so the support helps close its own gap.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for any melee rage build; the attack speed closes the gap to maximum rage on its own.

name: Rageforged I
stats: Supported Skills spend 10 Rage if possible to deal 35% more Damage
description: Supports any damaging skill that you use or Trigger yourself, causing it to spend Rage to deal more damage. If you don't have enough Rage to spend, the damage bonus will not apply.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that spends ten rage on use for 35% more damage. With too little rage, no bonus applies.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a direct conversion of rage into damage, which gives a rage build somewhere useful to spend what it generates.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only alongside a reliable rage source. Without one the skill just deals its normal damage.

name: Rageforged II
stats: Supported Skills have 30% chance to gain the benefits of this Support without spending additional Rage
Supported Skills spend 10 Rage if possible to deal 35% more Damage
description: Supports any damaging skill that you use or Trigger yourself, causing it to spend Rage to deal more damage, with a chance to skip spending Rage while still benefitting as though it had. If you don't have enough Rage to spend, the damage bonus will not apply.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, with a 30% chance to get the same damage bonus without spending the rage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Roughly a third of your uses become free, so the same rage generation supports more empowered hits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once available, since the free uses mean your rage stretches across more empowered hits.

name: Raging Cry
stats: Supported Skills grant 4 Rage per 5 Power of counted Enemies in range
description: Supports Warcry skills, causing them to grant you Rage on use depending on counted monster Power.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support granting four rage for every five power of the enemies counted in range.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns shouting at a big pack into a large lump of rage, which suits opening a fight rather than sustaining one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage build that opens on groups. Against a lone weak enemy it returns very little.

name: Rakiata's Flow
stats: Hits with Supported Skills treat Enemy Monster Elemental Resistance values as inverted
description: Supports Skills that can cause Damaging Hits, causing those Hits to treat Enemy Elemental Resistances as inverted.
flavourText:
The Tasalio Tribe developed their own Way, seeing
the world not as it is, but as it should be, given its
roiling and endless grace of constant motion.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support that makes the skill's hits treat enemy elemental resistances as inverted.
beginner.whyItMatters: A high resistance becomes a weakness instead, which flips the usual endgame problem completely on its head.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an elemental build fighting highly resistant monsters. Against low-resistance enemies it can work against you.

name: Rapid Attacks I
stats: Supported Skills have 15% increased Attack Speed
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to Attack faster.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support giving 15% increased attack speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster attacks mean more hits, which means more of everything that triggers on a hit as well as more damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An easy pick for almost any attack build, particularly one applying ailments on hit.

name: Rapid Attacks II
stats: Supported Skills have 25% increased Attack Speed
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to Attack faster.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 25% increased attack speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Still no drawback, and the higher speed compounds with every on-hit effect you carry.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it in place of the earlier version; more speed with no cost suits any attack skill.

name: Rapid Attacks III
stats: Supported Skills have 35% increased Attack Speed
Supported Skills deal 50% less Damage
description: Supports Attacks, causing them to Attack faster at the cost of Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 35% increased attack speed, but the skill deals half as much damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is only worth it when hit frequency matters more than hit size, such as for stacking ailments or building a resource.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an ailment or resource-building attack. On a damage skill the halved damage outweighs the speed.

name: Rapid Casting I
stats: Supported Skills have 15% increased Cast Speed
description: Supports Spells, causing them to cast faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support giving 15% increased cast speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Casting faster means less time rooted in place, which is safety as well as damage for a caster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A simple pick on any spell you cast repeatedly.

name: Rapid Casting II
stats: Supported Skills have 20% increased Cast Speed
description: Supports Spells, causing them to cast faster.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 20% increased cast speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: A little more speed for no drawback keeps it one of the easiest supports to justify.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier one whenever your gem tier reaches it.

name: Rapid Casting III
stats: Supported Skills have 10% increased Cast Speed for each different Spell you've Cast in the last eight seconds
description: Supports Spells, causing them to cast faster for each different Spell you've cast in the last eight seconds.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version, giving 10% increased cast speed for each different spell you have cast in the last eight seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards rotating through several spells rather than repeating one, which suits a varied caster and punishes a single-spell one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with three or more spells in regular use. On a one-spell caster the flat versions are better.

name: Ratha's Assault
stats: Supported Crossbow Ammunition Skills cannot reload
Supported Skills have 10% increased Attack Speed
Supported Skills load 4 bolts when you Dodge
Supported Skills load 3 additional bolts
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills, causing them to load multiple extra bolts and attack faster. Supported Skills cannot reload normally, instead loading bolts when you Dodge.
flavourText:
"No plan. No stealth. I want shock. Awe. I want them to
know who did it, and I want them telling tales. That's the
only way for us to earn their respect... and their fear."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage crossbow support: three extra bolts loaded, 10% increased attack speed, and no normal reloading at all. Instead you load four bolts each time you dodge.
beginner.whyItMatters: It replaces the reload button with the dodge button, so staying alive and staying loaded become the same action.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a mobile crossbow build that dodges constantly. If you rarely dodge, you will simply run out of ammunition.

name: Rearm I
stats: Hazards created by Supported Skills have 20% chance to rearm after they are triggered
description: Supports Skills which create Hazards. Hazards created by Supported Skills have a chance to be rearmed a short duration after triggering.

beginner.whatItIs: A hazard support giving hazards a 20% chance to rearm shortly after they trigger.
beginner.whyItMatters: A rearmed hazard catches a second wave without you placing anything new, which stretches one setup across a longer fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a hazard build holding a position against repeated waves.

name: Rearm II
stats: Hazards created by Supported Skills have 30% chance to rearm after they are triggered
description: Supports Skills which create Hazards. Hazards created by Supported Skills have a chance to be rearmed a short duration after triggering.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, raising the rearm chance to 30%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Nearly a third of your hazards resetting themselves makes a placed field noticeably more durable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once you are holding ground against waves rather than a single group.

name: Refraction I
stats: Refractive Plating grants Deflection Rating equal to 15% of Evasion Rating
Refractive Plating causes 20% of Armour to apply to Elemental Hit Damage taken
description: Supports Banner Skills, causing those affected by Auras they create to gain Refractive Plating, a Buff which grants Deflection Rating and causes Armour to partially apply to Elemental Hit Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A banner support granting everyone in the banner's aura Refractive Plating: deflection rating worth 15% of evasion, and 20% of armour applying to elemental hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Armour normally does nothing against elemental hits, so this lets an armoured character defend against damage types they were exposed to.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an armour or evasion build running a banner, especially in areas full of elemental damage.

name: Refraction II
stats: Refractive Plating grants Deflection Rating equal to 20% of Evasion Rating
Refractive Plating causes 30% of Armour to apply to Elemental Hit Damage taken
description: Supports Banner Skills, causing those affected by Auras they create to gain Refractive Plating, a Buff which grants Deflection Rating and causes Armour to partially apply to Elemental Hit Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, raising deflection to 20% of evasion and armour applying to 30% of elemental hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The higher share means a large armour pool covers a meaningful part of the elemental damage you take.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it once your armour pool is large enough that a bigger share of it is worth applying.

name: Refraction III
stats: Supported Banners apply Refractive Dissolution to Enemies in their radius
Refractive Dissolution applies 2% Elemental Exposure per 1000 player Armour, up to 80%
description: Supports Banner Skills, causing Enemies within their area to gain Refractive Dissolution, a Debuff which lowers Elemental Resistances.

beginner.whatItIs: The offensive version: instead of buffing allies, the banner applies Refractive Dissolution to enemies inside it, giving 2% elemental exposure per thousand of your armour, up to 80%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a defensive stat into a debuff on the enemy, which is a rare way for an armoured character to contribute damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-armour build that wants its banner attacking rather than protecting.

name: Reinforced Totems I
stats: Totems summoned by Supported Skills have +40% to all Elemental Resistances
description: Supports Skills which create Totems. Totems created by Supported Skills have additional Elemental Resistances.

beginner.whatItIs: A totem support granting your totems 40% to all elemental resistances.
beginner.whyItMatters: Elemental damage is what usually destroys totems, so resistance keeps them attacking rather than exploding on arrival.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any totem build heading into elemental-heavy content.

name: Reinforced Totems II
stats: Totems summoned by Supported Skills have +10% to all Maximum Elemental Resistances
Totems summoned by Supported Skills have +40% to all Elemental Resistances
description: Supports Skills which create Totems. Totems created by Supported Skills have additional Elemental Resistances.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, adding 10% to your totems' maximum elemental resistances on top of the 40%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Raising the maximum lets the resistance actually apply, which is what makes the bonus count in high-damage content.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once you reach content where 40% resistance alone stops keeping totems standing.

name: Remnant Potency I
stats: Remnants from Supported Skills have
20% increased effect
description: Supports Skills which create Remnants, making those Remnants more powerful.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving remnants the skill creates 20% increased effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stronger remnants mean each pickup is worth more, without changing how many you have to collect.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any remnant build. It has no drawback attached.

name: Remnant Potency II
stats: Effects of Remnants generated by Supported Skills occur 4 seconds after being collected
Remnants from Supported Skills have
30% increased effect
description: Supports Skills which create Remnants, making those Remnants more powerful, but delaying their effect.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 30% increased remnant effect but delaying the effect by four seconds after collection.
beginner.whyItMatters: A delayed buff is worth less in a short fight and just as good in a long one, so the trade depends on your content.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For sustained fights. Poor when you need the remnant's effect the moment you grab it.

name: Remnant Potency III
stats: Effects of Remnants generated by Supported Skills occur 3 seconds after being collected
Remnants from Supported Skills have
40% increased effect
description: Supports Skills which create Remnants, making those Remnants more powerful, but delaying their effect.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 40% increased remnant effect with a three second delay instead of four.
beginner.whyItMatters: More effect and less waiting than the second version, so it is the better of the two delayed options.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to end on if you accept the delay at all. If you cannot, the first version stays instant.

name: Rending Apex
stats: Final Strikes of Supported Skills Break Armour equal to 75% of Attack Damage dealt
description: Supports Strikes that perform a Final Strike at the end of a combination of attacks, causing the Final Strike to Break Armour based on a portion of Attack damage dealt.

beginner.whatItIs: A strike support where the final strike of a combination breaks armour equal to 75% of the attack damage it dealt.
beginner.whyItMatters: That is a large chunk of armour stripped in one blow, which sets up everything you do for the rest of the fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a combination melee build fighting armoured bosses.

name: Retaliate I
stats: Supported Skills deal up to 40% more Attack Damage, scaling up as your Stun Bar increases
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills gain much more damage the closer you are to being Heavily Stunned.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support giving up to 40% more attack damage, rising as your own stun bar fills toward being heavily stunned.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays out exactly when you are about to be staggered, giving you a chance to end the exchange first.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a durable melee character who takes hits. If you avoid damage entirely, the bonus never builds.

name: Retaliate II
stats: Hits from Supported Skills Stun Enemies as though dealing more Damage equivalent to the current percentage of your Stun Bar
Supported Skills deal up to 40% more Attack Damage, scaling up as your Stun Bar increases
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills gain much more damage and are more capable of Stunning Enemies the closer you are to being Heavily Stunned.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, which also makes your hits stun enemies as though they dealt more damage, scaled by how full your own stun bar is.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being close to stunned makes you better at stunning, which turns a dangerous moment into a chance to reverse it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move to it once you are deliberately trading blows rather than avoiding them.

name: Retreat I
stats: Supported Skills deal no Melee damage
Supported Skills deal 20% more Projectile Damage if you have Damaged an Enemy with a Melee Hit in the last eight seconds
description: Supports Skills which create Projectiles. Supported Skills deal more damage with Projectiles if you have struck with a Melee Hit in the last eight seconds, but cannot themselves deal Melee Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support giving 20% more projectile damage if you landed a melee hit in the last eight seconds, and removing the skill's melee damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the mirror of the melee-after-ranged supports, rewarding a build that closes in and then backs off shooting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only in a build with real melee hits. On a pure ranged character the condition never triggers.

name: Retreat II
stats: Supported Skills deal no Melee damage
Supported Skills deal 25% more Projectile Damage if you have Damaged an Enemy with a Melee Hit in the last eight seconds
description: Supports Skills which create Projectiles. Supported Skills deal more damage with Projectiles if you have struck with a Melee Hit in the last eight seconds, but cannot themselves deal Melee Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 25% more projectile damage under the same eight second melee condition.
beginner.whyItMatters: A larger payout for the same rhythm makes the close-then-shoot pattern worth planning around.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it once you are consistently landing a melee hit before backing off to shoot.

name: Retreat III
stats: Supported Skills deal no Melee damage
Supported Skills deal 30% more Projectile Damage if you have Damaged an Enemy with a Melee Hit in the last two seconds
description: Supports Skills which create Projectiles. Supported Skills deal more damage with Projectiles if you have struck with a Melee Hit in the last two seconds, but cannot themselves deal Melee Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 30% more projectile damage, but the melee hit must be within the last two seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: The narrow window forces genuine alternation instead of one melee hit at the start of a fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that swaps constantly between weapons. Otherwise the eight second versions are easier to keep up.

name: Ricochet I
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills have 40% chance to Chain an additional time from terrain
description: Supports any Skill which creates Projectiles, giving those Projectiles a chance to Chain when impacting terrain.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile support giving projectiles a 40% chance to chain once off terrain.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shots that would have been wasted on a wall come back into the fight, which is a large gain in tight spaces.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For fighting in corridors and rooms. In open ground there is little terrain to bounce from.

name: Ricochet II
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills have 50% chance to Chain an additional time from terrain
description: Supports any Skill which creates Projectiles, giving those Projectiles a chance to Chain when impacting terrain.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, raising the terrain chain chance to 50%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Half your wall impacts becoming extra shots makes indoor fighting noticeably faster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in when you are running content full of walls and corridors.

name: Ricochet III
stats: Projectiles from Supported Skills Pierce all Targets
Modifiers granting additional Projectiles instead cause Projectiles from Supported Skills to Chain an additional time from terrain per Projectile they would have gained
description: Supports any Skill which creates Projectiles, causing those Projectiles to Chain when impacting terrain, at the cost of any additional Projectiles, as well as causing them to always Pierce.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: projectiles always chain off terrain and always pierce, but any modifier that would grant extra projectiles instead grants another terrain chain.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts your whole projectile count into wall bounces, which is a complete change of how the skill covers a room.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For enclosed fighting on a build with lots of extra projectiles. In open ground you lose the projectiles and gain nothing.

name: Rigwald's Ferocity
stats: Supported Skills have 30% increased Attack Speed if used in Weapon Set I
Supported Skills deal 15% less Damage if used in Weapon Set I
Supported Skills have 10% reduced Attack Speed if used in Weapon Set II
Supported Skills deal 30% more Damage if used in Weapon Set II
description: Supports Attack skills, granting them Attack Speed at the cost of Damage or Damage at the cost of Attack Speed depending on Weapon Set they are used in. Does not modify skills used by Minions.
flavourText:
"Skothe kept us idle, sitting safe on these islands, while our
brethren remain slaves. We are one and the same! We must
fight! So, I bring you his head. I am now your Wolven King!"

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage attack support whose effect depends on which weapon set you use: 30% increased attack speed and 15% less damage in the first set, or 30% more damage and 10% reduced attack speed in the second.
beginner.whyItMatters: One support covers two roles, so swapping weapon sets changes how the same skill behaves rather than needing a second setup.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that genuinely uses both weapon sets, with a fast set for clearing and a heavy set for bosses.

name: Rip
stats: Remnants created by Supported Skills last for 8 seconds
Supported Skills create a Blood Remnant when dealing a killing blow to a Bleeding Enemy
Remnants created this way increase Life regeneration rate by 10% for 5 seconds when collected, up to a maximum of 100%
Remnants are created within a 1.5 metre radius of the slain Enemy
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills you use or Trigger yourself. Killing Blows with Supported Skills on Bleeding enemies create a Blood Remnant. Blood Remnants increase your Life regeneration rate for a short while after being collected.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support that creates a blood remnant when you land a killing blow on a bleeding enemy. Collecting one raises your life regeneration by 10% for five seconds, stacking to 100%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns bleed kills into stacking healing, so clearing a pack leaves you steadily more able to survive the next one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a bleed melee build clearing groups. Against a single boss there are no kills to make remnants from.

name: Rising Tempest
stats: Supported Skills deal 12% more Elemental Damage for each Skill used Recently of a different Elemental type
description: Supports Skills which deal Damage, raising Elemental Damage dealt for each Skill used Recently of a different Elemental type. Cannot support Minion Skills.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 12% more elemental damage for each skill of a different elemental type you have used recently.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a caster who rotates fire, cold and lightning rather than committing to one element.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a multi-element build. A single-element caster gets almost nothing from it.

name: Ritualistic Curse
stats: Supported Skills have 50% increased Area of Effect
Curse zones from Supported
Skills erupt after 30% more delay
description: Supports Curse skills, causing them to cover a larger area but take longer to Curse enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A curse support giving 50% increased area of effect while making the curse zone take 30% longer to erupt.
beginner.whyItMatters: You cover far more of a pack, at the cost of a delay that mobile enemies can walk out of.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For cursing a large stationary group. Poor against fast enemies that will not stay in the zone.

name: Romira's Requital
stats: 10% of Damage from Hits is taken from Supported Companion's Life before you
You Recoup 200% of Damage taken by Supported Minions this way as Life
Minions from Supported Skills have 30% less maximum Life
description: Supports Skills that create Companions which can be damaged. Minions created by Supported Skills take a portion of Hit Damage you would otherwise have taken, but have lowered maximum Life. A percentage of Damage taken this way is Recouped by you as Life.
flavourText:
"Come, my faithful wife," he crooned. "Sit. Eat. I wanted to
reward you for your loyalty. I even cooked this myself..."
She looked 'round for her sons, but hers was the only chair.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage companion support where the companion takes a tenth of the hit damage aimed at you and has 30% less life, but you recoup twice that damage back as life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts damage aimed at you into healing routed through your companion, which is defence and recovery in one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with a companion you can afford to lose. The recoup only works while the companion is alive to absorb hits.

name: Runic Extraction
stats: Remnants created by Supported Skills last for 8 seconds
Supported Skills Gain 20% of Life and Mana Cost as Extra Runic Ward Cost
Supported Skills have 35% chance create a Verisium Infusion Remnant on kill
description: Supports any Skill that deals damage. Enemies you kill with supported Skills have a chance to drop a Verisium Infusion Remnant.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving kills a 35% chance to drop a Verisium infusion remnant, at the cost of the skill also spending 20% of its life and mana cost again as runic ward.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts ordinary kills into a stream of remnants, paid for out of your ward rather than your other resources.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a runic ward build that clears packs and wants the remnants those kills produce.

name: Runic Infusion
stats: Supported Skills cost an additional 20% of maximum Runic Ward
Supported Skills deal added Physical damage equal to 25% of Runic Ward cost
description: Supports Attacks you use or Trigger yourself, causing them to cost Runic Ward to use but deal additional Physical damage based on their Runic Ward cost. Cannot Support Channelling Skills, Sustained Skills, or Skills without a cost.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support costing an extra 20% of your maximum runic ward, and adding physical damage worth a quarter of that cost.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a plain conversion of ward into damage, which suits a character who regenerates ward faster than they need it defensively.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a runic ward attack build. It cannot support channelled or sustained skills, or skills with no cost.

name: Rupture
stats: Supported Skills Aggravate Bleeding on Hitting Heavy Stunned Enemies
description: Supports skills that Hit Enemies. Supported skills Aggravate Bleeding on Hitting Heavily Stunned Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that aggravates bleeding when the skill hits a heavily stunned enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: Aggravated bleeding deals its damage much faster, so this is how a bleed build cashes in a stun.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a bleed build that also heavy stuns. Without stuns it never fires.

name: Rusted Spikes
stats: Supported Skills Aggravate Bleeding on Enemies when Pinning them
description: Supports Skills which deal Damage with Hits. When Supported Skills Pin an Enemy, they also Aggravate Bleeding on that Enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that aggravates bleeding on any enemy the skill pins.
beginner.whyItMatters: It joins two physical mechanics that usually sit apart, so pinning something also speeds up the bleed already on it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical build running both pin and bleed. With only one of them it does nothing.

name: Sacrificial Lamb I
stats: Your Skills target Minions from Supported Skills within 6 metres if possible
