description: Supports Skills which create Minions, causing your Skills which can target Minions to prioritise targeting Minions from the Supported Skill before your other Minions where possible.

beginner.whatItIs: A minion support making your minion-targeting skills prefer minions from this skill within six metres.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives you control over which minion gets sacrificed or targeted, which stops an important companion being consumed by accident.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that consumes or detonates minions and runs more than one kind.

name: Sacrificial Lamb II
stats: Minions created by Supported Skills are always considered to be Detonatable
Your Skills target Minions from Supported Skills within 6 metres if possible
description: Supports Skills which create Minions, causing your Skills which can target Minions to prioritise targeting Minions from the Supported Skill before your other Minions where possible, as well as causing them to always be considered Detonatable.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, which also makes those minions always count as detonatable.
beginner.whyItMatters: Making them always detonatable means the skill always has a valid target, removing the moments where nothing happens.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once you have had detonation skills fail to find a valid minion.

name: Sacrificial Offering
stats: Supported Offering Skills have 30% increased Buff effect
Supported Skills Sacrifice 15% of Life on use
Supported Offering Skills deal 30% more Damage
description: Supports Offering Skills. Supported Skills Sacrifice a portion of your life on use, but deal much more damage and have more powerful Buffs in return.

beginner.whatItIs: An offering support giving 30% more damage and 30% increased buff effect, in exchange for sacrificing 15% of your life on use.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a large boost to an offering paid for in health, so its safety depends on how quickly you heal that back.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an offering build with decent recovery. Avoid it if you cast offerings while already hurt.

name: Salvo
stats: Supported Skills have a maximum of 6 Seals
Supported Skills gain a Seal every 1 second
Projectiles from Supported Skills are fired in random directions
Supported Skills fire 1 additional Projectile per Seal broken
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself which fire Projectiles, Sealing them over time. The Seals are broken when used, causing additional Projectiles to be fired. Projectiles from Supported Skills are fired in random directions. Cannot Support Skills which require Combo, have a Cooldown or which already gain Seals.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile attack support that gains a seal every second, up to six. Using the skill breaks the seals, firing one extra projectile per seal in random directions.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards holding fire, turning a wait into a spray of arrows across the area rather than a single aimed shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing after a pause between packs. The random directions make it unreliable against one target.

name: Scouring Flame
stats: Supported Skills Gain 25% of Life and Mana Cost as Extra Runic Ward Cost
50% more Magnitude of Ignite inflicted with Supported Skills
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing inflicted Ignites to deal more damage but the skill to gain a Runic Ward cost.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 50% more ignite magnitude, at the cost of the skill also spending 25% of its life and mana cost again as runic ward.
beginner.whyItMatters: It offers a large ignite boost with no damage penalty, priced in a resource fire builds do not usually spend.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an ignite build with runic ward to give. Without ward regeneration the cost becomes the limiting factor.

name: Searing Flame I
stats: Supported Skills deal 25% less Damage with Hits
75% more Magnitude of Ignite inflicted with Supported Skills
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing inflicted Ignites to deal more damage but its Hits to deal less damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 75% more ignite magnitude for 25% less hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shifts damage out of the hit and into the burn, which is the trade any ignite build wants to make.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when ignite is your main damage. On a hit-based fire build you are giving away what you use.

name: Searing Flame II
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% less Damage with Hits
100% more Magnitude of Ignite inflicted with Supported Skills
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing inflicted Ignites to deal more damage but its Hits to deal less damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, doubling ignite magnitude for 30% less hit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The deeper trade is better the more completely your damage comes from burning rather than striking.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The version to run once ignite is doing nearly all your work.

name: Second Wind I
stats: Supported Skills have 50% less Cooldown Recovery Rate
Supported Skills have twice as many Cooldown Uses
description: Supports Skills which have a cooldown, giving them extra uses of that cooldown. Cannot support Meta, instant, or Triggered Skills, and cannot modify the Skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support doubling the skill's cooldown uses while halving its cooldown recovery rate.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets you use a cooldown skill twice in quick succession, at the price of a longer wait before the pair comes back.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a movement or burst skill where two uses back to back save your life. Poor if you need it constantly available.

name: Second Wind II
stats: Supported Skills have 40% less Cooldown Recovery Rate
Supported Skills have twice as many Cooldown Uses
description: Supports Skills which have a cooldown, giving them extra uses of that cooldown. Cannot support Meta, instant, or Triggered Skills, and cannot modify the Skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, with the recovery penalty reduced from 50% to 40%.
beginner.whyItMatters: The same two uses come back faster, which is a straight improvement with no new condition.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Replace the earlier version whenever it is available; the faster recovery costs nothing.

name: Second Wind III
stats: Supported Skills have 40% less Cooldown Recovery Rate
When a Supported Skill is used and goes on cooldown, recover 1% of maximum Life per second of cooldown
Supported Skills have twice as many Cooldown Uses
description: Supports Skills which have a cooldown, giving them extra uses of that cooldown and causing them to recover your Life when a Skill is used and goes on cooldown. Cannot support Meta, instant, or Triggered Skills, and cannot modify the Skills of Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: double cooldown uses, a 40% recovery penalty, and 1% of maximum life recovered per second of cooldown when the skill goes on cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: It attaches a heal to a skill you were already using, which turns a mobility button into a recovery one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for a cooldown skill, particularly one with a long cooldown to convert into healing.

name: Selfless Remnants
stats: Remnants from Supported Skills affect Allies in your Presence instead of you when collected
description: Supports Skills that generate Remnants, causing those Remnants to affect Allies in your Presence when collected instead of you.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes collected remnants affect allies near you instead of yourself.
beginner.whyItMatters: It hands your remnant buffs to your party or your minions, which is a support role rather than a personal upgrade.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a group or a minion build with allies to buff. Solo with no companions, you get nothing at all.

name: Seraph's Heart
stats: Enemy Hits have 20% chance to treat all your Resistances as being 90% while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, providing a chance for enemies to calculate their Hits as though your Resistances were 90% while the skill is active.
flavourText:
Intricate machinery imperceptibly woven into a
biological foundation. It felt delicate in her hands.
In him, it would be her greatest achievement.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for persistent buffs giving enemy hits a 20% chance to treat all your resistances as 90%.
beginner.whyItMatters: One hit in five landing against near-maximum resistances is a large reduction in the damage that gets through.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any character whose resistances are lower than they would like, especially against heavy elemental damage.

name: Shock
stats: Supported Skills have 100% more chance to Shock
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, making it more likely to Shock.

beginner.whatItIs: A support doubling the skill's chance to shock.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shock raises the damage the target takes from everything, so applying it more often multiplies your whole build.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build struggling to shock consistently.

name: Shock Conduction
stats: Shocking Hits from supported Skills have a 50% chance to also Shock enemies in a 2.5 metre radius
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to also Shock nearby enemies when you Shock an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving shocking hits a 50% chance to also shock enemies within 2.5 metres.
beginner.whyItMatters: It spreads shock from one target to the pack around it, so the damage bonus applies to everything rather than one monster.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build clearing groups. Against a lone enemy there is nothing to spread to.

name: Shocking Leap
stats: Supported Skills create Shocked Ground for 4 seconds when they Critically Hit, no more than once per Skill use
Shocked Ground created this way has a radius of 2 metres
description: Supports Skills that leap into the air and deal damage, causing them to create Shocked Ground the first time they Critically Hit an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for leaping skills that creates shocked ground for four seconds the first time the leap critically hits, once per use.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a movement skill into an area setup, leaving damage amplification where you landed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build that leaps into packs and has enough critical hit chance to trigger it.

name: Short Fuse I
stats: Supported Skills have 40% less Detonation Time
description: Supports Skills which Detonate after some amount of time has elapsed, shortening the time before Detonation.

beginner.whatItIs: A support cutting the skill's detonation time by 40%.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shorter fuse means the explosion happens while the enemy is still where you threw it, rather than after they have wandered off.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For reactive grenade play in the middle of a fight, rather than planting ahead of one.

name: Short Fuse II
stats: Supported Skills have 80% less Detonation Time
Supported Skills deal 30% less Damage
description: Supports Skills which Detonate after some amount of time has elapsed, massively shortening the time before Detonation at the cost of Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, cutting detonation time by 80% at the cost of 30% of the damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a delayed explosive into something close to an instant one, which is worth real damage if timing is your problem.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For fast-moving fights where a slow fuse means the blast always misses. Skip it if your grenades already land on time.

name: Sione's Temper
stats: Gain 1 Wildshard on casting Supported Spells
Supported Skills have a 20% chance to fire 8 additional Projectiles in a circle per Wildshard
All Wildshards are lost when Supported Skills fire Projectiles in a circle
description: Supports Projectile Spells. Supported Spells have an increasingly higher chance to fire many additional Projectiles in a circle, resetting when they do.
flavourText:
She holds in her hand a shattered crystal, a vision of her desire: to
see her sister's silver palace obliterated, to see it cast across the
heavens. One cross word, and the sky will rain down her fury.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for projectile spells. Each cast grants a Wildshard, and each Wildshard adds a 20% chance to fire eight extra projectiles in a circle. All Wildshards are lost when that happens.
beginner.whyItMatters: The chance rises the longer you go without the burst, so a big circular volley is guaranteed eventually rather than left to luck.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a projectile caster that casts repeatedly and wants a periodic area burst without a second skill.

name: Skittering Stone I
stats: After 5 Enemies are killed within 4 metres of objects created by Supported Skills, they will shatter and Trigger Skittering Stones
Skittering Stones
Creates Skittering Stone Minions from shattered objects created by Supported Skill.
Minions from this skill have 1% increased Damage per 1 of your Strength
Creates 1 Skittering Stone
Level of Minions is based on Level of Triggering Skill
Minion duration is 10 seconds
Limit 8 Skittering Stones
description: Supports Skills which create shatterable earthen objects. After killing enough Enemies in range of these objects, they will shatter, releasing skittering stone Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for skills that create shatterable earthen objects. Once five enemies die within four metres of one, it shatters into a skittering stone minion, up to eight at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts the debris of your clearing into free attackers that scale off your strength.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a strength build clearing dense packs, where five kills near an object happens naturally.

name: Skittering Stone II
stats: After 5 Enemies are killed within 4 metres of objects created by Supported Skills, they will shatter and Trigger Skittering Stones
Skittering Stones
Creates Skittering Stone Minions from shattered objects created by Supported Skill.
Minions from this skill have 1% increased Damage per 1 of your Strength
Creates 2 Skittering Stone
Level of Minions is based on Level of Triggering Skill
Minion duration is 20 seconds
Limit 12 Skittering Stones
description: Supports Skills which create shatterable earthen objects. After killing enough Enemies in range of these objects, they will shatter, releasing skittering stone Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, creating two minions per shatter, lasting twenty seconds, with a limit of twelve.
beginner.whyItMatters: Twice the minions lasting twice as long turns an incidental bonus into a real second source of damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it once your clearing is fast enough to shatter objects regularly.

name: Slow Potency
stats: Debuffs inflicted with Supported Skills have 15% increased Slow Magnitude
description: Supports any skill, causing inflicted Slows to be more powerful.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving slows the skill inflicts 15% increased magnitude.
beginner.whyItMatters: A deeper slow means enemies spend longer crossing the ground between you, which is defence you get from a debuff you already apply.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only on a skill that already slows. It creates no slow of its own.

name: Soul Drain
stats: Recover 12% of maximum Mana over four seconds when Supported Skills Cull an Enemy
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing you to recover Mana when it Culls an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support recovering 12% of your maximum mana over four seconds whenever the skill culls an enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pairs finishing off a rare with a large mana refill, so an expensive caster is ready for the next fight rather than empty.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster with culling already in the build. Without a culling source nothing triggers.

name: Spar
stats: Hits from Supported Skills Stun Enemies as though dealing more Damage equivalent to the current percentage of your Stun Bar
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills are more capable of Stunning Enemies the closer you are to being Heavily Stunned.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support making your hits stun enemies as though they dealt more damage, scaled by how full your own stun bar is.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards trading blows, giving you a better chance of stunning the enemy first as you both approach being staggered.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a durable melee character who fights toe to toe rather than avoiding damage.

name: Spectral Volley
stats: Attacks with Supported Skills create a Spectral Projectile
Spectral Projectiles will fire if no Spectral Projectiles have been created in the last 3 seconds
Supported Skills deal 60% less Damage when not fired from Spectral Projectiles
Supported Skills deal 20% more Damage when fired from Spectral Projectiles
Maximum 5 Spectral Projectiles
description: Supports Bow or Spear Projectile Attacks you use yourself. Supported Skills deal lower damage initially, but generate Spectral Projectiles, which deal more damage when they fire. Spectral Projectiles linger and will fire a short duration after no new Spectral Projectiles have been created. Cannot support Channelling Skills, Leaping skills, or skills which rain Projectiles from above.

beginner.whatItIs: A bow or spear support where attacks deal 60% less damage but create spectral projectiles, up to five. Those fire three seconds after the last one was made, at 20% more damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It banks several weak shots into one delayed volley, which suits building up on a target rather than hitting it immediately.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a stationary fight where you can build the full five. Poor if you keep interrupting to reposition.

name: Spell Cascade
stats: Supported Skills have 20% less Area of Effect
Cascades from Supported Skills have 20% less Area of Effect
Supported Skills deal 30% less Damage
Supported Skills Cascade to either side of the targeted Area along a random axis
description: Supports Cascadable Spells, causing them to Cascade to either side of the target area, along a randomly chosen axis.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for cascadable spells, casting the spell to either side of the target along a random axis, at 30% less damage and 20% less area on all of it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Three casts covering a line instead of one on a point is a large increase in coverage for a real cut in strength.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs. Against a single target the side casts miss and you only feel the penalty.

name: Spell Echo
stats: Supported Spells Echo 1 time
Supported Skills have 30% less Cast Speed
Echoes from Supported Spells have 40% increased Area of Effect
description: Supports Cascadable Spells you use yourself. Supported Spells Echo.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that makes the spell echo once, with the echo covering 40% more area, at the cost of 30% cast speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: The echo effectively doubles what one cast does, and the wider echo often catches enemies the first cast missed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an area spell used to clear. The slower casting makes it worse on a spell you need to fire quickly.

name: Splinter Totem I
stats: Supported Skills can only have one active Totem
Totems created by Supported Skills can splinter up to 2 times
Totems created by Supported Skills have 20% less area of effect for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills deal 20% less damage for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills have 20% less maximum
Life for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills have 10% less Skill Speed for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills splinter after performing 1 action
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, preventing having more than one active Totem but causing that Totem to splinter into smaller versions of itself after it uses an Attack or Spell, with each Totem becoming less effective. Each splintered Totem can further splinter, up to a maximum. Does not Support Skills used by Minions. Only one Totem can be splintering at a time.

beginner.whatItIs: A totem support limiting you to one totem, which splinters into weaker copies of itself after each action, up to two times, losing 20% of its damage, area, life and some speed each split.
beginner.whyItMatters: One totem becomes several, so a single placement covers more ground than a single stronger post would.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a totem build that wants spread rather than a single durable totem.

name: Splinter Totem II
stats: Supported Skills can only have one active Totem
Totems created by Supported Skills can splinter up to 2 times
Totems created by Supported Skills have 15% less area of effect for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills deal 15% less damage for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills have 15% less maximum
Life for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills have 7% less Skill Speed for each time they have splintered
Totems created by Supported Skills splinter after performing 1 action
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, preventing having more than one active Totem but causing that Totem to splinter into smaller versions of itself after it uses an Attack or Spell, with each Totem becoming less effective. Each splintered Totem can further splinter, up to a maximum. Does not Support Skills used by Minions. Only one Totem can be splintering at a time.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, with each splinter losing only 15% of its damage, area and life instead of 20%.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stronger splinters mean the later copies still contribute rather than fading into nothing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once the third splinter from the earlier version stopped being worth having.

name: Static Shocks
stats: Supported Skills Trigger Static Shocks when Shocking an enemy
description: Supports Skills which can Hit enemies. Shocking an enemy with Supported Skills Triggers Static Shocks, causing that enemy to become a source of Lightning damage sending pulses towards nearby enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that triggers static shocks when the skill shocks an enemy, turning that enemy into a source of lightning pulses aimed at everything nearby.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes one shocked monster damage the whole pack around it, which is clearing you get for free from a debuff.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build fighting groups. Against a lone target the pulses find nothing.

name: Steadfast I
stats: You have 50% more Stun Threshold while Channelling Supported Skills
description: Supports Channelling Skills you use yourself, granting you higher Stun Threshold while Channelling them.

beginner.whatItIs: A channelling support giving 50% more stun threshold while you are channelling.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being stunned mid-channel wastes the whole build-up, so raising your threshold protects the time you have already invested.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any channelled skill you use in melee or in the middle of a pack.

name: Steadfast II
stats: You have 100% more Ailment Threshold while Channelling Supported Skills
You have 50% more Stun Threshold while Channelling Supported Skills
description: Supports Channelling Skills you use yourself, granting you higher Stun Threshold and Ailment Threshold while Channelling them.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, adding 100% more ailment threshold on top of the same stun threshold bonus.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ailments interrupt a channel as surely as a stun does, so covering both keeps the channel intact far more reliably.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move to it once ailments rather than stuns are what keep breaking your channel.

name: Stoicism I
stats: Supported Skills gain 1% more Damage every second, up to 20%
This Damage Bonus resets if you
Dodge Roll or use a Travel Skill
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills steadily gain more Damage, up to a cap. This Damage bonus is reset if you Dodge Roll or use a Travel Skill.

beginner.whatItIs: An attack support gaining 1% more damage per second up to 20%, reset whenever you dodge roll or use a travel skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays you for standing your ground, and takes the reward away the moment you disengage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a tanky attacker who fights without rolling. On a mobile build the bonus resets before it builds.

name: Stoicism II
stats: Supported Skills gain 2% more Damage every second, up to 20%
This Damage Bonus resets if you
Dodge Roll or use a Travel Skill
description: Supports Attack Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills steadily gain more Damage, up to a cap. This Damage bonus is reset if you Dodge Roll or use a Travel Skill.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, building 2% more damage per second to the same 20% cap, so it fills in half the time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reaching the cap in ten seconds rather than twenty makes the bonus achievable in an ordinary fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it once you can hold a position for ten seconds without rolling away.

name: Stomping Ground
stats: Support
Triggers a Shockwave when you take a step while using Supported Skills
Shockwave
Attack Damage of this skill is 50% of Default Attack Damage
Shockwave radius is 2 metres
description: Supports Travel skills, causing your footsteps to crack the earth and emit damaging shockwaves while using the skill.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for travel skills that triggers a damaging shockwave with every step you take while using them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes running through a pack into an attack, so movement and damage stop being separate actions.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that travels through enemies rather than around them.

name: Stormchain
stats: Supported Skills Cannot inflict Shock
description: Supports Projectile Skills and Skills which can Chain. Supported Skills always Chain when initially Hitting a Shocked Enemy, but cannot themselves inflict Shock. Does not support Skills which cannot Chain.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where the skill always chains when it first hits a shocked enemy, but it can no longer shock anything itself.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a two-skill lightning setup, turning a shocked target into the starting point of a chain.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only when another skill applies the shock. Alone it cannot create the condition it needs.

name: Stormfire
stats: Enemies Shocked by Supported Skills take 20% of damage from Ignite as Lightning damage as well as Fire damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies. Enemies Shocked by Supported Skills take a percentage of damage from Ignite as Lightning damage as well as Fire damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where enemies shocked by the skill take 20% of their ignite damage as lightning damage in addition to fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets an ignite scale off lightning as well as fire, which suits a build that has invested in both.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that both shocks and ignites the same targets. With only one of them it does nothing.

name: Streamlined Rounds
stats: Supported Skills have 50% more Attack speed
Supported Skills deal 60% less Damage
Supported Skills have 50% less reload speed
Supported Skills load 5 additional bolts
description: Supports Crossbow Ammunition Skills. Supported Skills have significantly higher Attack speed and bolt capacity, but deal less damage and have longer reload time.

beginner.whatItIs: A crossbow support with 50% more attack speed and five extra bolts, at the cost of 60% of the damage and half the reload speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a heavy crossbow into a rapid one, which matters when hit frequency is what your build actually scales.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an ailment or on-hit crossbow build. On a build that wants big individual hits it is a large loss.

name: Strong Hearted
stats: 50% less Shock duration on you while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing Shock applied to you to last for a shorter duration while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs that halves how long shocks last on you while the buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shock on you raises all the damage you take, so cutting its duration cuts your exposure in exactly the wrong moments.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth a slot in areas full of lightning damage. Elsewhere the slot is better spent.

name: Stun I
stats: Hits with Supported Skills cause 50% more Stun buildup
description: Supports any skill that Hits Enemies, causing it to build up Stun more quickly.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving hits 50% more stun buildup.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stunning interrupts whatever the monster was doing, so this is control bought with a support slot rather than a skill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy weapon build that wants to keep dangerous enemies from acting.

name: Stun II
stats: Hits with Supported Skills cause 70% more Stun buildup
description: Supports any skill that Hits Enemies, causing it to build up Stun more quickly.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving hits 70% more stun buildup.
beginner.whyItMatters: The higher buildup reaches a stun in fewer hits, which matters most against tough enemies with large stun bars.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once enemies have stun bars large enough that the earlier version stopped filling them.

name: Stun III
stats: Supported Skills deal 50% less Damage
Hits with Supported Skills cause 300% more Stun buildup
description: Supports any skill that Hits Enemies, causing it to build up Stun significantly more quickly, at the cost of Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 300% more stun buildup, but the skill deals half as much damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a skill into a dedicated stunning tool, which only makes sense if a second skill is providing the damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a setup attack in a two-skill combination. Never on your main damage skill.

name: Styrn's Ferocity
stats: Supported Skills Crush targets they Hit for 8 seconds
Hits against targets Crushed by Supported Skills Break Armour equal to 10% of Physical damage dealt
description: Supports Shield Skills that Hit enemies, causing those Hits to Crush their targets, additionally causing any Physical Damage Hits against those targets while Crushed to Break their Armour.
flavourText:
Each knight who encountered Styrn challenged
him to the traditional duel. One by one, he fought
his way across all of Middengard... and beyond.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage shield support that crushes enemies your shield hits for eight seconds, and makes physical damage against crushed targets break 10% of that damage as armour.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a shield build a way to strip armour passively, so your shield sets up your weapon.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical shield build fighting armoured bosses.

name: Styrn's Mountain
stats: Melee Skills that don't raise a Shield deal 20% more Damage if you've Blocked while using Supported Skills Recently
50% more Stun Threshold for Heavy Stuns while using Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills that Raise your Shield causing your other melee skills to deal more damage if you block.
flavourText:
Bound by his oath to the Runefathers, Styrn the
Indomitable refused to bow to Cadigan the First.
His resistance laid the seeds for future defiance.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for shield-raising skills, giving your other melee skills 20% more damage if you have blocked recently, plus 50% more heavy stun threshold while raising the shield.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards actually blocking rather than merely holding a shield, and protects you from being stunned while you do it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a block-based melee build that raises its shield deliberately against incoming attacks.

name: Supercritical
stats: Supported Skills have 100% increased Critical Damage Bonus
Supported Skills have 20% less Critical Hit chance
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, causing it to deal more damage with Critical Hits but have less Critical Hit chance.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 100% increased critical damage bonus for 20% less critical hit chance.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is the mirror of the crit-chance supports, making rarer crits hit far harder.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with high critical hit chance already. On a low-crit build you make an unreliable effect rarer still.

name: Swift Affliction I
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more non-Ailment Damage over Time
20% less Duration of Supported Skills and Damaging Ailments they inflict
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, causing it to deal more non-Ailment damage over time but have a shorter duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving 30% more non-ailment damage over time while cutting the duration of the skill and its damaging ailments by 20%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It compresses the same damage into less time, which suits fights that end before a full duration would run out.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a damage-over-time build clearing quickly. Poor if your effects need to run their full length.

name: Swift Affliction II
stats: Supported Skills deal 30% more non-Ailment Damage over Time
10% less Duration of Supported Skills and Damaging Ailments they inflict
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, causing it to deal more non-Ailment damage over time but have a shorter duration.

beginner.whatItIs: The improved version, with the same damage bonus and only a 10% duration cut.
beginner.whyItMatters: Half the drawback for the same gain makes it the safer of the two for most builds.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it whenever you want the damage without giving away a fifth of every effect's life.

name: Swift Affliction III
stats: Supported Skills deal 50% more non-Ailment damage over time if their duration is less than one second
30% less Duration of Supported Skills and Damaging Ailments they inflict
description: Supports any skill that deals damage, causing effects with a duration of one second or less to deal more non-Ailment damage over time.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 50% more non-ailment damage over time for effects lasting under a second, with a 30% duration cut on everything.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is built for very short effects, and the heavy duration cut is what pushes them under the one second threshold.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only for a build using rapid, very short damage-over-time effects. It hurts anything designed to linger.

name: Syzygy
stats: Hits from Supported Skills are considered Crushing Blows against Ignited and Fully Armour Broken Enemies
Heavily Stunning Enemies which are Ignited and Fully Armour Broken with Supported Skills will permanently Intimidate them
description: Supports Slam Skills you use yourself. Hits from Supported Skills are considered Crushing Blows against Enemies which are both Ignited and Fully Armour Broken. Hits with Supported Skills that Heavily Stun Ignited and Fully Armour Broken Enemies will Intimidate them.

beginner.whatItIs: A slam support where hits count as crushing blows against enemies that are both ignited and fully armour broken, and heavy stunning such an enemy intimidates them permanently.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stacks a heavy payoff on top of two setup conditions, so a build that arranges both gets a very large reward.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a slam build that ignites and breaks armour. With only one condition met, nothing happens.

name: Tacati's Ire
stats: Poisons from Supported Skills deal Damage 2% faster per Rage
description: Supports Skills which can cause Damaging Hits. Poison inflicted with Supported Skills deals Damage faster the higher your Rage.
flavourText:
He almost saved the Vaal. His unique poison made it past
the Queen's cupbearers; he had only to direct his anger...
but in her presence, he could feel naught but lust.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support making poison from the skill deal its damage 2% faster for each point of rage you hold.
beginner.whyItMatters: It joins two systems that rarely meet, letting a warrior's rage speed up a poison build's damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a rage-generating build that also poisons. Without rage the poisons tick at their normal rate.

name: Tangmazu's Thurible
stats: Companions from Supported Skills are Gigantic
Companions from Supported Skills have +4 to Evasion Rating per 10 Evasion Rating you have
Companions from Supported Skills have +4 to Deflection Rating per 10 Deflection Rating you have
description: Supports Skills which summon Companions causing them to be Gigantic and gain Evasion and Deflection based on your own.
flavourText:
In his roiling fog, their fear becomes form.
Dark truths unveiled by a shroud. They see only
their perception of him, and thus, he is remade.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage companion support making companions gigantic and granting them evasion and deflection scaled off your own.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties your companion's defences to your gear, so investing in your own evasion also makes your companion survive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an evasion-based character with a companion they want to keep alive.

name: Tasalio's Rhythm
stats: Successfully executing Perfect Timing with Supported Skills grants a stack of Tasalio's Rhythm
All Tasalio's Rhythm is lost on failing to execute any Perfect Timing
Supported Skills deal 10% more Damage for each stack of Tasalio's Rhythm
Supported Skills have a 30% shorter Perfect Timing window for each stack of Tasalio's Rhythm
Tasalio's Rhythm stacks up to 5 times
Supported Skills have a 100% longer Perfect Timing window
description: Supports Skills which have a benefit for Perfectly Timing their use. On successfully executing Perfect Timing with Supported Skills, gain Tasalio's Rhythm. Tasalio's Rhythm causes Supported Skills to deal more damage and have shorter Perfect Timing windows for each stack. Failing to execute any Perfect Timing (even with skills not supported by Tasalio's Rhythm) will remove all Tasalio's Rhythm on you.
flavourText:
The Chieftain built a grand waikoama, and boasted that
it could never be sunk. Tasalio grinned, and the waves
rolled in, tilting the ship, cresting higher and higher...

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support granting a stack of Tasalio's Rhythm on each perfect timing, up to five. Each stack gives 10% more damage and shortens the perfect timing window by 30%, and any failed perfect timing clears the whole stack.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gets harder as it gets stronger, so the reward is deliberately tuned to how precisely you can play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a confident player on a perfect-timing build. A single mistake anywhere resets everything.

name: Tawhoa's Tending
stats: Support
Totems created by Supported
Skills have 25% more maximum Life
Totems created by Supported Skills trigger Tawhoa's Vengeance on death
Tawhoa's Vengeance
Critical Hit Chance: 5.00%
Deal Physical Damage in an area, based on Totem Life.
Expliosion radius is 3 meters
Explosion deal base Physical Damage equal to 10% of Totem's maximum Life
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, causing those Totems to have more Life. Totems created by Supported Skills explode on death, dealing Physical damage based on their Life.
flavourText:
A scavenging warrior found Tawhoa meditating in a grove.
"There is only so much jade in this world," intoned the god.
"Take my gift to your tribe. Ironwood will grow for all time."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage totem support giving totems 25% more life and making them explode for physical damage based on that life when they die.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes a totem's death a payoff rather than a loss, and the extra life makes the explosion bigger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a totem build that places totems into danger and expects to lose them.

name: Tear
stats: 50% Chance for On-Kill Effects caused by killing blows on Bleeding Enemies with Supported Skills to occur twice
description: Supports Melee Attacks you use or Trigger yourself. On-Kill effects caused by Killing Blows with Supported Skills on Bleeding enemies have a chance to occur twice.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee support giving a 50% chance for on-kill effects to happen twice when the killing blow lands on a bleeding enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It doubles up whatever your build already gets from kills, which compounds with every other on-kill effect you carry.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a bleed build that already has on-kill effects. With none, it does nothing at all.

name: Tecrod's Revenge
stats: Minions from Supported Skills die 20 seconds after their Life is reduced to 0
Minions from Supported Skills gain Soul Eater when their Life is reduced to 0
Minions from Supported Skills gain 40% increased Attack and Cast Speed when their Life is reduced to 0
description: Supports Skills that create Persistent Minions, causing those Minions to fight on when they are fatally wounded, dying after a duration. Minions from Supported Skills gain Soul Eater and a burst of speed on entering this state.
flavourText:
The Lich Lords destroyed his body, but with his dying fury,
Tecrod found a way. He lurks deep, in the blood, in the flesh,
in the Well... perhaps walking among them even now, unseen.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage minion support where fatally wounded minions fight on for twenty seconds, gaining soul eater and 40% increased attack and cast speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Twenty seconds of an accelerated minion is often more valuable than the minion was while alive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build in hard content, where minions dying is the norm rather than the exception.

name: Tectonic Slams
stats: Supported Skills have 30% less Aftershock area of effect
Supported Skills deal 45% less damage with Aftershocks
Supported Skills cause 1 additional Aftershock ahead and to each side of the initial area
Supported Skills have 15% less Attack Speed
description: Supports Slams you use yourself, causing them to create simultaneous Aftershocks behind the Slam, but lowering Aftershock damage and area of effect with Supported Skills. Cannot Support Skills which create Fissures.

beginner.whatItIs: A slam support creating an extra aftershock ahead and to each side of the slam, at the cost of 45% aftershock damage, 30% aftershock area and 15% attack speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It spreads a slam across a much wider footprint, trading the force of each aftershock for coverage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs with slams. Against a single boss the extra aftershocks land on empty ground.

name: Thornskin I
stats: Deal 40% increased Thorns Damage while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to deal increased Thorns Damage while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs giving 40% increased thorns damage while active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Thorns damage happens without you pressing anything, so raising it makes being attacked more profitable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a thorns build that gets hit deliberately. It gives nothing to a character who avoids damage.

name: Thornskin II
stats: Deal 70% increased Thorns Damage while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to deal increased Thorns Damage while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 70% increased thorns damage while the buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: The larger increase makes thorns a real damage source rather than a small bonus on the side.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it once thorns is carrying real damage rather than chipping in occasionally.

name: Thrill of the Kill I
stats: Attacks Gain 25% of Damage as Lightning Damage for 8 seconds on Culling an enemy with Supported Skills
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which Hit enemies. Culling a Shocked enemy with Supported Skills infuses all of your Attacks with Lightning damage for a short time.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where culling a shocked enemy grants all your attacks 25% of their damage again as lightning damage for eight seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It spreads a reward from one skill across everything you do, so a single cull lifts your whole rotation.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a lightning build with culling and reliable shocks. Missing either one and it never triggers.

name: Thrill of the Kill II
stats: Attacks Gain 25% of Damage as Lightning Damage for 8 seconds on Culling an enemy with Supported Skills
Thrill of the Kill Buff also grants 40% increased Shock chance
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which Hit enemies. Culling a Shocked enemy with Supported Skills infuses all of your Attacks with Lightning damage and grants an increased chance to Shock for a short time.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, which also grants 40% increased shock chance while the buff is up.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra shock chance makes the next cull easier to set up, so the buff helps sustain itself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once you are culling reliably, so the shock chance keeps the loop going.

name: Tireless
stats: Supported Skills have 25% chance to not count Attacks they Empower
description: Supports Warcry Skills. Attacks Empowered by Supported Skills have a chance not to lower the Empowerment count of Supported Skills when they are used.

beginner.whatItIs: A warcry support giving a 25% chance for an empowered attack not to count against the warcry's empowerment total.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stretches each warcry across roughly a third more attacks, so you shout less and fight more.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a warcry build whose empowerment runs out before the warcry comes off cooldown.

name: Trickster's Shard
stats: Supported Spells Trigger Fragment Self
Supported Spells deal 50% less Damage when cast by Fractured Mimics
Fractured Mimics are created within 1.5 metres
Fractured Mimic duration is 5 seconds
Limit 4 Fractured Mimics
description:
Supports non-instant Spells you cast yourself. Supported Spells will Trigger Fragment Self, creating a Fractured Mimic which will cast that Spell if you get enough of them.
Creates a Fractured Mimic of yourself, suspended in time at the point of casting the Triggering Spell. If you reach the Limit of Fractured Mimics, they will all finish casting their Spells and disappear.
flavourText:
They'd cast him out, declared him a dark omen. Their judgement
rattled in his head. He'd no control over crops, or herds, but
that mattered little. Upon his return, their fear was his weapon.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage spell support that creates a fractured mimic of you at the point of casting, up to four. When the limit is reached they all finish casting the spell at 50% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It banks four casts into a delayed multi-point burst spread across wherever you were standing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster who moves between casts, so the mimics cover different parts of the fight.

name: Tul's Avalanche
stats: Supported Skills have a maximum of 4 Seals
Supported Spells Echo 1 time per Seal broken
Supported Skills gain a Seal every 2 times you Block
description: Supports Cascadable Spells you cast yourself, Sealing them when you Block, The Seals are broken when used, each making the Spell Echo. Cannot support skills with a Cooldown or which already gain Seals.
flavourText:
Then, there was movement. What once preserved them
now pulled them free from their silence. In the
absence of stillness, their screams echoed.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage spell support that gains a seal every two blocks, up to four. Breaking the seals on cast makes the spell echo once per seal.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts successful blocking into extra casts, which is a direct link between your defence and your damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a blocking caster. Without blocks you will never accumulate a seal.

name: Tul's Stillness
stats: Chaos Damage from Hits with Supported Skills also Contributes to Freeze Buildup
Supported Skills Gain 40% of Cold Damage as Extra Chaos Damage
description: Supports Skills that can cause Damaging Hits, granting extra Chaos damage and causing Chaos damage to Contribute to Freeze Buildup.
flavourText:
"Countless graves glow silently in endless rows that stretch
on unseen. The living lie within, but do not decay, do not
die. Their eyes remain open, their essence stilled, waiting."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support adding 40% of your cold damage again as chaos damage, and letting that chaos damage contribute to freeze buildup.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a cold build keep freezing while adding a damage type that ignores energy shield.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build that needs an answer to shielded enemies without giving up its freezes.

name: Uhtred's Augury
stats: +2 to level of Supported Skills if exactly two other Supports are modifying them
description: Supports Skills which can gain levels, granting them additional levels provided exactly two other supports are used with the supported Skill. Does not support skills which do not have levels.
flavourText:
Studying the ill omens of the stars, Uhtred came to suspect
something was very wrong among the first Kalguurans.
Olroth, Vorana, Medved... three there were. Three dangers.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support granting the skill two extra levels, but only when exactly two other supports are attached to it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a specific socket count rather than a build style, so it either applies fully or not at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When your setup happens to be this support plus exactly two others. Adding or removing one silently loses the bonus.

name: Uhtred's Constellation
stats: Supported Skills have 50% less Cooldown Recovery Rate
Supported Non-Instant Skills have +2 Cooldown Uses
Supported Skills deal 8% more Damage for each different Skill with a Cooldown you have used in the last 8 seconds
description: Supports non-instant skills which have a cooldown, granting them two additional cooldown uses and more damage per different skill with a cooldown you have used recently.
flavourText:
"In the stars, I see our future. My plans are laid,
lines tracing a constellation. You may only see
pieces, but I see the whole, and it will be glorious."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support giving non-instant cooldown skills two extra cooldown uses and 8% more damage for each different cooldown skill used in the last eight seconds, at 50% less cooldown recovery.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards rotating through several cooldown skills rather than repeating one, which suits a varied, deliberate playstyle.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build carrying three or more cooldown skills used in sequence.

name: Uhtred's Exodus
stats: +3 to level of Supported Skills if no other Supports are modifying them
description: Supports Skills which can gain levels, granting them many additional levels provided no other supports are used with the supported Skill. Does not support skills which do not have levels.
flavourText:
By the time Uhtred realised the truth, only Vorana remained
to defend them. While the rest fled, she implanted her flesh
with gems and set forth alone to face the endless hordes.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support granting three extra gem levels, but only when no other support is attached to the skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: Three levels is a large gain for a skill that works well unsupported, and impossible to combine with anything else.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a strong skill you are happy to run bare. Add any other support and the bonus disappears entirely.

name: Uhtred's Omen
stats: +2 to level of Supported Skills if exactly one other Support is modifying them
description: Supports Skills which can gain levels, granting them additional levels provided exactly one other support is used with the supported Skill. Does not support skills which do not have levels.
flavourText:
Day and night, his priests followed each of the Kalguuran
heroes. When Medved disappeared, Uhtred grew even more
paranoid. Now, only two remained... Olroth and Vorana.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support granting two extra gem levels, but only when exactly one other support is attached to the skill.
beginner.whyItMatters: It fills the gap between running a skill bare and running it fully supported, at a fixed socket count.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When your setup is this support plus exactly one other. Any third support removes the bonus.

name: Uhtred's Rite
stats: Supported Skills grant Overflowing Chalice when used, for 1 second per 1 second of their cooldown
Supported Skills deal 20% more damage during effect of any Life Flask
Supported Skills have 20% increased Mana
Cost Efficiency during effect of any Mana Flask
description: Supports skills with Cooldowns, causing them to grant Overflowing Chalice when used. Supported skills deal more damage during the effect of your Life Flask and have increased Mana Cost Efficiency during the effect of your Mana Flask.
flavourText:
"To control the stars, we swallow the firmament.
We imbibe the truth. We are filled with the void.
We embrace the vast emptiness, or we die."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support granting Overflowing Chalice for a second per second of the skill's cooldown, with 20% more damage while a life flask is active and 20% increased mana cost efficiency while a mana flask is.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties a cooldown skill to your flask usage, so drinking becomes part of your damage rotation rather than an emergency.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with a long cooldown skill and flasks it uses on a rhythm.

name: Unleash
stats: Supported Skills have a maximum of 2 Seals
Supported Skills Repeat 1 time per Seal broken
Supported Spells gain a Seal every 0.2% of cast time
Supported Skills deal 50% less Damage when Repeating
description: Supports Repeatable Spells you cast yourself, Sealing them over time. The Seals are broken when cast, each causing the Spell to Repeat. Cannot support skills with a Cooldown or which already gain Seals.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support gaining up to two seals over time. Breaking them on cast makes the spell repeat once per seal, with repeats at 50% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards pausing between casts, turning waiting into two extra weaker casts you did not pay mana for.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a spell you cast intermittently. On a spell you hold down, the seals never accumulate.

name: Upheaval I
stats: Supported Skills create an additional fissure
Supported Skills deal 20% less Damage
Supported Skills have 20% less Skill Speed
description: Supports Skills which create fissures in the ground, causing them to create an additional fissure at the cost of damage and speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A support creating one extra fissure at the cost of 20% damage and 20% skill speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two fissures cover twice the ground, which is usually worth more than the damage each one loses while clearing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For fissure skills used against groups. Against one target the extra fissure adds nothing.

name: Upheaval II
stats: Supported Skills create 2 additional fissures
Supported Skills deal 40% less Damage
Supported Skills have 20% less Skill Speed
description: Supports Skills which create fissures in the ground, causing them to create additional fissures at the cost of damage and speed.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, creating two extra fissures for 40% less damage and 20% less skill speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Three fissures cover a wide area, but at this penalty each is weak enough that only softer enemies die.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing large groups of ordinary monsters. Poor against anything with real health.

name: Upwelling I
stats: Your Minions deal 30% increased Damage while you are not on full Mana while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing your Minions to deal increased Damage while you are not on full Mana while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs giving your minions 30% increased damage while you are not on full mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards actually spending your mana, which a minion build often has little reason to do otherwise.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build that casts regularly. If you sit at full mana it gives nothing.

name: Upwelling II
stats: Your Minions deal 50% increased Damage while you are not on full Mana while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing your Minions to deal increased Damage while you are not on full Mana while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving your minions 50% increased damage while you are below full mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: The bigger bonus makes keeping your mana partly spent a deliberate part of how the build is played.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once you are spending mana in every fight rather than sitting on a full pool.

name: Urgent Totems I
stats: Supported Skills have 80% increased Totem Placement speed
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, causing those Skills to place Totems much more quickly.

beginner.whatItIs: A totem support giving 80% increased totem placement speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Placing a totem is time you spend defenceless, so making it quick is both a damage and a safety improvement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For any totem build that has to place totems in the middle of a fight.

name: Urgent Totems II
stats: Supported Skills have 100% increased Totem Placement speed
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, causing those Skills to place Totems much more quickly.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving 100% increased totem placement speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster still means the gap where you are exposed all but disappears.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it as soon as it is available; placement time is pure exposure and this cuts more of it.

name: Urgent Totems III
stats: Spells Cast by Totems created by Supported Skills have 20% increased Cast Speed
Attacks used by Totems created by Supported Skills have 20% increased Attack Speed
Supported Skills have 100% increased Totem Placement speed
description: Supports Skills which create Totems, causing those Skills to place Totems much more quickly. Totems created by Supported Skills have increased Attack and Cast Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: The final version: 100% increased placement speed, plus 20% increased attack and cast speed for the totems themselves.
beginner.whyItMatters: It speeds up both getting the totem down and what it does afterwards, which the earlier versions do not.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Settle here for any totem build, since it speeds up the totem as well as the placement.

name: Uruk's Smelting
stats: Fully Breaking Armour with Supported Skills causes affected targets to permanently take 5% increased Physical Damage, up to 20%
Supported Skills Break 70% more Armour
description: Supports any skill, causing Armour Break it inflicts to be stronger. Fully Breaking Armour with Supported Skills permanently increases the Physical Damage taken by those affected, up to a cap.
flavourText:
The volcano roared, but there was no thunder, only the boom
of Uruk's hammer. Wraeclast had forgotten the old alliance,
but by the Molten One's will, the fires would rage again.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support breaking 70% more armour, and permanently raising the physical damage a target takes by 5% each time you fully break its armour, up to 20%.
beginner.whyItMatters: A permanent stacking increase is rare, and against a long boss fight it keeps paying for the whole encounter.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical build fighting armoured bosses over an extended fight.

name: Uul-Netol's Embrace
stats: Break Armour equal to 20% of Chaos Damage dealt by Supported Skills
Supported Skills Gain 40% of Physical Damage as Extra Chaos Damage
description: Supports Skills that can cause Damaging Hits, granting extra Chaos damage and causing Chaos damage to Break Armour.
flavourText:
"The Lords could not breathe, so they grew new lungs.
The Lords could not venture, so they grew new skin.
The Lords were alone, so they grew us, to serve them."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support adding 40% of your physical damage again as chaos damage, and letting that chaos damage break armour worth a fifth of it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage normally cannot break armour, so this keeps a physical build's armour stripping while adding a shield-ignoring damage type.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a physical build that wants a chaos component without losing its armour break.

name: Vanguard I
stats: Gain 2 Guard per ten Strength when you Stun an Enemy
Gain an additional 4 Guard per ten Strength if Heavily Stunning
Guard duration is 4 seconds
description: Supports Shield Skills, causing you to gain Guard on Stunning Enemies with the Supported Skill.

beginner.whatItIs: A shield support granting two guard per ten strength when you stun an enemy, with four more per ten strength on a heavy stun, lasting four seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts stunning into a shield on yourself, so a defensive character is rewarded for controlling the fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a high-strength shield build that stuns regularly.

name: Vanguard II
stats: Gain 2 Guard per ten Strength when you Stun an Enemy
Gain an additional 6 Guard per ten Strength if Heavily Stunning
Guard duration is 4 seconds
description: Supports Shield Skills, causing you to gain Guard on Stunning Enemies with the Supported Skill.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, with the heavy stun bonus raised from four to six guard per ten strength.
beginner.whyItMatters: Heavy stuns become noticeably more rewarding, which pushes you toward landing the bigger stun rather than the small one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once you are landing heavy stuns rather than only ordinary ones.

name: Varashta's Blessing
stats: Supported Skills deal 10% more Damage for each different Command Skill you have used in the last 15 seconds
description: Supports any Skill that can deal damage, causing it to deal more damage for each different Command Skill you have used in the past few seconds. Cannot modify the Skills of Minions.
flavourText:
"These traditions we shall set forth, so that we may remain
strong, so that we may endure throughout the ages. Not to
bind, not to dominate, but to protect... and guide."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support giving 10% more damage for each different command skill you have used in the last fifteen seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pays you for actively directing your minions rather than leaving them to fight on their own.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a minion build with several distinct command skills it uses in rotation.

name: Verglas
stats: Destroying an Ice Crystal grants Supported Skills 1% of Damage Gained as extra Cold for 6 seconds, per two thousand maximum Life of the destroyed Ice Crystal
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which can Hit Enemies. Supported Skills Gain a percentage of their Damage as Cold Damage when you destroy Ice Crystals.

beginner.whatItIs: A support granting extra cold damage for six seconds when you destroy an ice crystal, scaled by that crystal's maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives you a reason to break your own crystals, converting them into a personal damage buff.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold build that creates and then shatters large ice crystals.

name: Vilenta's Propulsion
stats: 75% of increases and reductions to Cast speed also apply to Projectile Speed for Supported Skills
description: Supports Spell Skills that fire Projectiles, causing increases and reductions to cast speed to also apply to Projectile speed.
flavourText:
Day and night, she hammered away, obsessed with proving it
could be done; a vast ring of artifice under the earth, pushing
energy to speeds never before seen - all to prove Qotra wrong.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support making 75% of your cast speed increases also apply to projectile speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a caster's existing cast speed investment double as projectile speed, so one stat covers two problems.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a projectile caster with heavy cast speed investment. Without it, there is nothing to convert.

name: Vitality I
stats: Regenerate 1% of maximum Life per second while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain Life Regeneration while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs regenerating 1% of your maximum life per second while active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Steady regeneration heals you between fights without any input, which is the least demanding form of recovery there is.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build with no leech or flask sustain, especially while levelling.

name: Vitality II
stats: Regenerate 2% of maximum Life per second while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing you to gain Life Regeneration while the Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, regenerating 2% of maximum life per second while the buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Twice the regeneration can outpace ongoing damage rather than only topping you up afterwards.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move to it once regeneration is your main way of recovering between fights.

name: Volatility
stats: Supported Skills grant Volatility on Critical Hit
description: Supports Skills you use yourself which can cause Damaging Hits. Supported Skills grant Volatility on Critical Hit of an enemy.

beginner.whatItIs: A support that grants volatility whenever the skill lands a critical hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It generates the resource that volatility-spending skills need, from an action a critical build was performing anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a critical build that has a second skill built around detonating volatility.

name: Volcanic Eruption
stats: Supported Strikes trigger Volcanic Eruption on Hitting Ignited Enemies
description: Supports Melee Strike Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills trigger Volcanic Eruption on Hit against Ignited Enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: A melee strike support that triggers a volcanic eruption whenever your strike hits an ignited enemy.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a melee fire build an area explosion attached to hits it was already making on burning targets.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a melee build that ignites first. Without ignites it never fires.

name: Volt
stats: Supported Skills gain 2 Voltaic Charge per Metre travelled
Supported Skills have 30 maximum Voltaic Charge
Supported Skills consume all Voltaic Charge on use
Supported Skills gain 1% of Damage as extra Lightning Damage per Voltaic Charge consumed
description: Supports Projectile Attack Skills you use yourself. Supported Skills gain Voltaic Charge as you move, up to a maximum. When used, Supported Skills expend that Charge to gain extra Lightning Damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A projectile attack support gaining two voltaic charge per metre you travel, up to thirty, all spent on use for 1% of damage as extra lightning damage per charge.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts walking into damage, so a kiting ranged character is rewarded for the movement that keeps them alive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a mobile ranged build. Standing still it accumulates nothing.

name: Vorana's Siege
stats: Supported Skills have 35% increased Area of Effect
Supported Skills deal 20% more Damage with Hits against Isolated targets
description: Supports skills which Hit targets and have an area of effect, increasing the affected area and causing it to Hit Isolated targets harder.
flavourText:
"Your laws of war are asinine. I shall prevail!
I'll crush every pawn you put before me.
Face me, coward! Play by my rules."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support giving 35% increased area of effect and 20% more hit damage against isolated targets.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers more ground and hits harder when there is only one enemy, so it works for both clearing and single targets.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A broadly useful pick on any area skill, particularly one used against separated enemies.

name: Vruun's Aftermath
stats: Supported Warcries cause Ice Crystals to explode
Supported Warcries Detonate your Ice Fragments
Supported Warcries Empower 3 additional Attacks if they destroy at least 5 total Ice Crystals and Ice Fragments
description: Supports Warcries, causing them to destroy Ice Crystals and Ice Fragments. Supported Skills empower additional Attacks if they destroy enough Ice Crystals and Ice Fragments.
flavourText:
Vruun tore through Tul's preserved, shattering their
bodies with reckless malice. "The will of the Lords!"
he roared over his decimation. "All broods must serve."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage warcry support that destroys your ice crystals and ice fragments, and empowers three additional attacks if it destroys at least five of them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a field of frozen debris into empowered attacks, so the crystals you made become the fuel for your warcry.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a cold warrior build that reliably has five or more crystals and fragments on the ground.

name: Vruun's Inevitability
stats: Supported Skills can gain up to 10 Combo
Supported Skills expend all Combo on use
Supported Skills have 6% increased area of effect per Combo expended
Supported Skills lose Combo if they generate no Combo for 6 seconds
description: Supports Melee Attack Skills. Supported Skills gain Combo when you successfully Strike Enemies with other Melee Attacks. Supported Skills expend their Combo when used, gaining more area of effect the higher Combo they had. Cannot support skills which already gain Combo. Cannot modify the Skills of Minions.
flavourText:
"If you think you've won, it's only because you don't
understand their strategy. Each Vruun you kill only
teaches the next one how to endure against you."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage melee support that builds up to ten combo from your other melee strikes and spends it all on use for 6% increased area of effect per point.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a combo build's payoff into coverage rather than damage, which is a different way to spend the same setup.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For clearing packs with a combo finisher. For single-target damage a combo damage support is better.

name: Warm Blooded
stats: 50% less Freeze duration on you while a Supported Skill is active
description: Supports Persistent Buff Skills, causing Freeze applied to you to last for a shorter duration while the Supported Skill is active.

beginner.whatItIs: A support for persistent buffs halving how long freezes last on you while the buff is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being frozen means being unable to act at all, so cutting that time in half is a direct survival gain.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Worth a slot in cold-heavy areas. Elsewhere it does nothing you will notice.

name: Wildfire
stats: Ignites inflicted by Supported Skills Spread to other enemies that stay within 1.5 metres for 1 second
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, Spreading Ignites it inflicts to nearby enemies after a delay.

beginner.whatItIs: A support where ignites you inflict spread to enemies that stay within 1.5 metres for a second.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets one ignite work its way through a tightly packed group without you applying it again.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an ignite build clearing packs that cluster. Against spread-out enemies it rarely spreads at all.

name: Wildshards I
stats: Supported Skills have a 20% chance to fire 8 additional Projectiles in a circle
description: Supports Projectile Spells. Supported Spells have a chance to fire many additional Projectiles in a circle.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving projectile spells a 20% chance to fire eight extra projectiles in a circle.
beginner.whyItMatters: One cast in five turning into a full circular volley is a large amount of area coverage at no cost to the ordinary casts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a projectile caster clearing groups, where the circle catches enemies on every side.

name: Wildshards II
stats: Supported Skills have a 25% chance to fire 8 additional Projectiles in a circle
description: Supports Projectile Spells. Supported Spells have a chance to fire many additional Projectiles in a circle.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, raising the circular volley chance to 25%.
beginner.whyItMatters: A quarter of your casts bursting means the extra coverage shows up often enough to rely on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it whenever your gem tier reaches it; a quarter of casts bursting beats a fifth every time.

name: Window of Opportunity I
stats: Supported Skills have a 35% shorter Perfect Timing window
Supported Skills deal 35% more Damage when released with Perfect Timing
description: Supports Channelling skills that have special effects if released with Perfect Timing, causing them to deal much more damage if released with Perfect Timing but reducing the Perfect Timing window.

beginner.whatItIs: A channelling support giving 35% more damage when released with perfect timing, while shortening the perfect timing window by 35%.
beginner.whyItMatters: It raises the reward and the difficulty together, so it is worth what your reflexes can actually claim.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a player comfortable with a tight release. If you miss the window often, you lose more than you gain.

name: Window of Opportunity II
stats: Releasing Supported Skills with Perfect Timing grants Deflection Rating equal to 15% of Evasion Rating for 8 seconds
Supported Skills have a 35% shorter Perfect Timing window
Supported Skills deal 35% more Damage when released with Perfect Timing
description: Supports Channelling skills that have special effects if released with Perfect Timing, causing them to deal much more damage and grant Perfect Deflection if released with Perfect Timing but reducing the Perfect Timing window.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, which also grants deflection rating worth 15% of your evasion for eight seconds on a perfectly timed release.
beginner.whyItMatters: It adds a defensive reward to the same skilled release, so a good timing keeps you safer as well as hitting harder.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Swap in once your release timing is dependable, and value it higher on an evasion character.

name: Withering Touch
stats: Withered lasts 4 seconds
Supported Skills deal 25% less Damage
Chance to inflict Withered on Hit with Supported
Skills can Surpass 100%
Supported Skills have 1% chance to inflict
Withered on Hit for every 0.57% of enemy
Ailment Threshold dealt as Chaos damage
description: Supports any skill that Hits enemies, giving it a chance to Wither enemies on Hit.

beginner.whatItIs: A support giving a chance to inflict withered on hit, scaled by how much chaos damage the hit dealt against the enemy's ailment threshold, at 25% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Withered raises the chaos damage a target takes, so this is setup for a chaos build rather than damage in itself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a chaos build whose main damage comes from another skill. The damage penalty makes it a poor main attack.

name: Xibaqua's Rending
stats: Support
Supported Skills trigger Fiery Reclamation on landing
Fiery Reclamation
Deals Fire damage in an area around the exploding Corpse based on its maximum Life.
Explosion deals base Fire Damage equal to 6% of the Corpse's Maximum Life
Explosion radius is 1.5 metres
Detonates Corpses in a radius of 3.5 metres
description: Supports Skills that leap into the air, causing Corpses in the area you land to violently explode, damaging surrounding enemies.
flavourText:
Born of the gods, his treachery was met with divine fury.
One by one, the gods reclaimed their flesh, until all that
remained was a droplet of pure light: the first Vaal.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support for leaping skills that detonates corpses within 3.5 metres of where you land, each exploding for fire damage based on its own maximum life.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the bodies from your last fight into the opening damage of the next one, at no cost.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build leaping between packs in dense content. In a clean room there are no corpses to use.

name: Xoph's Pyre
stats: Chaos Damage from Hits with Supported Skills also Contributes to Flammability and Ignite Magnitudes
Supported Skills Gain 40% of Fire Damage as Extra Chaos Damage
description: Supports Skills that can cause Damaging Hits, granting extra Chaos damage and causing Chaos damage to Contribute to Ignites.
flavourText:
"They drank until only dust remained. Ate until their gums
bled rust. Such was their greed, the only thing that remains
of the Broken Sun... is the Red Pyre, the Torus Eternal."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support adding 40% of your fire damage again as chaos damage, and letting that chaos damage contribute to flammability and ignite magnitude.
beginner.whyItMatters: It keeps a fire build's ignites scaling while adding a damage type that gets past energy shield.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For an ignite build that needs an answer to shielded enemies without losing its burns.

name: Zarokh's Refrain
stats: Supported Spells Echo 3 times
Echoes from Supported Spells have 40% increased Area of Effect
description: Supports Cascadable Spells you cast yourself. Supported Spells Echo thrice, but are given a Cooldown. Cannot support skills which already have a Cooldown.
flavourText:
Reliving the same day for all time, Zarokh raged against
the moments that made up his prison. There would be
no redemption, for he had broken his only barya.

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage spell support making the spell echo three times, with every echo carrying the same flat 40% increased area of effect, at the cost of gaining a cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: Four casts from one press, three of them wider than the first, is enormous coverage, paid for by not being able to repeat it immediately. The echoes are all the same size as each other, so the area does not build up across them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a heavy area spell used once per pack. It cannot support a spell that already has a cooldown.

name: Zarokh's Revolt
stats: Supported Skills have a maximum of 5 Seals
Supported Skills Repeat 1 time per Seal broken
Supported Spells gain a Seal every 0.05% of cast time
Supported Skills deal 20% less Damage when Repeating
description: Supports Repeatable Spells you cast yourself, Sealing them over time and giving them a moderate Cooldown. The Seals are broken when cast, each causing the Spell to Repeat. Cannot support skills which already have a Cooldown or gain seals.
flavourText:
Zarokh's ire built over the centuries as he planned his escape.
The Afarud would find what he sought, and then... the
Weeping Black would break the chains of his prison.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support gaining up to five seals over time and adding a cooldown. Breaking the seals makes the spell repeat once per seal, with repeats at 20% less damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Five repeats at only a fifth less damage each is a very large single release, held back by the cooldown.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a spell you save for a moment that matters. Poor as a continuous attack because of the cooldown.

name: Zenith I
stats: Supported Spells deal 30% more Damage while you are above 90% of your Maximum Mana
description: Supports Spell Skills. Supported Skills deal more damage while you are above 90% of your Maximum Mana. Does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: A spell support giving 30% more damage while you are above 90% of your maximum mana.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a caster who keeps their mana nearly full, which means investing in regeneration or cheap spells.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a caster with strong mana sustain. If you drain your pool in every fight the bonus is rarely active.

name: Zenith II
stats: Supported Skills have 25% increased Mana Cost Efficiency
Supported Spells deal 30% more Damage while you are above 90% of your Maximum Mana
description: Supports Spell Skills. Supported Skills have increased Mana cost Efficiency and deal more damage while you are above 90% of your maximum Mana. Does not modify Skills used by Minions.

beginner.whatItIs: The stronger version, giving the same 30% more damage above 90% mana plus 25% increased mana cost efficiency.
beginner.whyItMatters: The cheaper casting helps you stay above the threshold, so the support partly maintains its own condition.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Move up to it once you want the cheaper casting to help you stay above the mana threshold.

name: Zerphi's Infamy
stats: Supported Skills requires 50 Glory to use
Supported Skills gain Glory equal to 5% of Life spent on other Skills
Supported Skills have 50% increased Area of Effect
Supported Skills deal 50% more Damage
description:
Supports Attacks and Warcries you use yourself. Supported Skills gain a Glory requirement, and build Glory when you spend Life on Skills. Supported Skills deal more damage and have significantly
increased area of effect.
flavourText:
"It was the quality of his heinous acts that set him apart, not
the quantity... all of the physical trauma inflicted occurred
while the victim was still alive. Perhaps this was the key."

beginner.whatItIs: A Lineage support requiring fifty glory to use, built from 5% of the life you spend on other skills, in return for 50% more damage and 50% increased area of effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links two systems: paying life elsewhere in your build becomes the fuel for a much larger attack here.
beginner.whenToUseIt: For a build that already spends life on its other skills. Without that spending you will never reach fifty glory.
